ACOUSTIC|Absorption.name: Absorption
ACOUSTIC|Absorption.definition: A material that soaks up sound energy (acoustic foam, carpet). Reduces reflections.
ACOUSTIC|Absorption.condition: A porous material (foam, carpet) absorbs sound energy; reflection coefficient is low.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic ecology.name: Acoustic ecology
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic ecology.definition: The study of sound in the environment. How organisms use sound, and how sounds shape behavior.
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic ecology.condition: The study of sound in the environment; how organisms use sound, and how sounds shape behaviour.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic holography.name: Acoustic holography
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic holography.definition: Record the interference pattern of sound waves. Reconstruct the 3D sound field. "Hearing" an image.
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic holography.condition: The interference pattern of sound waves is recorded; the 3D sound field is reconstructed.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic lens.name: Acoustic lens
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic lens.definition: A curved medium that focuses or defocuses sound waves. Like a lens, but for pressure waves.
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic lens.condition: A curved medium focuses or defocuses sound waves; like a lens, but for pressure waves.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic levitation.name: Acoustic levitation
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic levitation.definition: A standing wave trap. Small objects can be suspended at the pressure nodes (zero net force).
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic levitation.condition: A standing wave trap; small objects are suspended at pressure nodes where net force is zero.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic mirror.name: Acoustic mirror
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic mirror.definition: A curved surface that focuses sound at a single point. Like a parabolic microphone.
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic mirror.condition: A curved surface that focuses sound at a single point; like a parabolic microphone.

ACOUSTIC|Acoustic radiation pressure.name: Acoustic radiation pressure
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic radiation pressure.definition: Sound carries momentum. It can push objects. An acoustic tractor beam.
ACOUSTIC|Acoustic radiation pressure.condition: Sound carries momentum; it can push objects (acoustic tractor beam).

ACOUSTIC|Beat freq.name: Beat freq
ACOUSTIC|Beat freq.definition: Two close frequencies produce a pulsating wave. The beat frequency is the difference between them (f₁ - f₂).

ACOUSTIC|Beat frequency.condition: Two close frequencies produce a pulsating wave; the beat frequency is

ACOUSTIC|Binaural beat.name: Binaural beat
ACOUSTIC|Binaural beat.definition: Two slightly different frequencies played to different ears. The brain perceives a phantom beat at the difference frequency. Affects brainwave states.
ACOUSTIC|Binaural beat.condition: Two slightly different frequencies played to different ears; the brain perceives a phantom beat at the difference frequency.

ACOUSTIC|Chladni pattern.name: Chladni pattern
ACOUSTIC|Chladni pattern.definition: Vibrate a metal plate at a resonant frequency. The sand settles into geometric patterns (nodal lines). Visualizes sound.
ACOUSTIC|Chladni pattern.condition: Vibrating a metal plate at a resonant frequency creates nodal lines; sand settles into geometric patterns.

ACOUSTIC|Cochlear implant.name: Cochlear implant
ACOUSTIC|Cochlear implant.definition: A device that converts sound into electrical signals. Bypasses damaged hair cells. Direct neural input.
ACOUSTIC|Cochlear implant.condition: A device converts sound into electrical signals; bypasses damaged hair cells; direct neural input.

ACOUSTIC|Coherence.name: Coherence
ACOUSTIC|Coherence.definition: A measure of how "together" different parts of a sound wave are. High coherence = a pure tone; low = noise.
ACOUSTIC|Coherence.condition: A measure of how "together" different parts of a sound wave are; high coherence = pure tone; low = noise.

ACOUSTIC|Cymascan.name: Cymascan
ACOUSTIC|Cymascan.definition: High-resolution imaging of sound patterns on a vibrating surface. Visualizes the quantum of a sound.
ACOUSTIC|Cymascan.condition: High‑resolution imaging of sound patterns on a vibrating surface; visualises the quantum of a sound.

ACOUSTIC|Damping material.name: Damping material
ACOUSTIC|Damping material.definition: A material engineered to absorb specific frequencies. Makes rooms acoustically "dead."
ACOUSTIC|Damping material.condition: A composite material engineered to absorb specific frequencies; makes rooms acoustically "dead."

ACOUSTIC|Digital synthesis.name: Digital synthesis
ACOUSTIC|Digital synthesis.definition: Generate any sound by combining pure tones (additive synthesis) or shaping noise (subtractive).
ACOUSTIC|Digital synthesis.condition: Any sound is generated by combining pure tones (additive) or shaping noise (subtractive).

ACOUSTIC|Doppler shift.name: Doppler shift
ACOUSTIC|Doppler shift.definition: A moving source changes the observed frequency: higher as it approaches, lower as it recedes. Detects motion.
ACOUSTIC|Doppler shift.condition: Observed frequency is higher as source approaches, lower as it recedes; Δf = f₀·v/c.

ACOUSTIC|Echolocation.name: Echolocation
ACOUSTIC|Echolocation.definition: Emit a sound pulse; measure the time until the echo returns. Distance = (speed × time) / 2. Maps the environment in darkness.
ACOUSTIC|Echolocation.condition: Distance = (speed × time) / 2; a map of the environment is built from echoes.

ACOUSTIC|Helmholtz.name: Helmholtz
ACOUSTIC|Helmholtz.definition: A resonant cavity (bottle) with a neck. It resonates at a specific frequency determined by its volume and neck dimensions.

ACOUSTIC|Helmholtz resonator.name: Helmholtz resonator
ACOUSTIC|Helmholtz resonator.definition: A resonant cavity with a neck; resonates at a specific frequency.
ACOUSTIC|Helmholtz resonator.condition: A resonant cavity (bottle) with a neck; resonates at a frequency determined by volume and neck dimensions.

ACOUSTIC|Infrasound.name: Infrasound
ACOUSTIC|Infrasound.definition: Sub-audible frequencies. They resonate with large structures (buildings, bridges). Can be felt as unease or even damage.
ACOUSTIC|Infrasound.condition: Sub‑audible frequencies (f < 20 Hz) resonate with large structures (buildings, bridges); can be felt as unease.

ACOUSTIC|Masking.name: Masking
ACOUSTIC|Masking.definition: A loud sound renders a softer sound inaudible. Used in noise cancellation.
ACOUSTIC|Masking.condition: A loud sound renders a softer sound inaudible; used in noise cancellation.

ACOUSTIC|Misophonia.name: Misophonia
ACOUSTIC|Misophonia.definition: Certain sounds (chewing, tapping) trigger strong emotional responses in some individuals. A sound-based adversarial tool.
ACOUSTIC|Misophonia.condition: Certain sounds (chewing, tapping) trigger strong emotional responses; an adversarial tool.

ACOUSTIC|Nonlinear acoustics.name: Nonlinear acoustics

ACOUSTIC|Nonlinear acoustics.condition: At high amplitudes, sound waves distort, generate harmonics, and create shock waves (sonic booms).

ACOUSTIC|Phased array.name: Phased array
ACOUSTIC|Phased array.definition: Multiple sound sources with precisely controlled phase delays. Steers the beam without moving parts.
ACOUSTIC|Phased array.condition: Multiple sources with controlled phase delays; beam is steered without moving parts.

ACOUSTIC|Reflection.name: Reflection
ACOUSTIC|Reflection.definition: A hard, smooth surface reflects sound; angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
ACOUSTIC|Reflection.condition: A hard, smooth surface reflects sound like a mirror; angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.

ACOUSTIC|Reflection ac.name: Reflection ac
ACOUSTIC|Reflection ac.definition: A hard, smooth surface reflects sound like a mirror reflects light. Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.

ACOUSTIC|Resonance freq.name: Resonance freq

ACOUSTIC|Resonance freq.condition: Driving at a specific frequency produces a large amplitude; amplitude drops quickly away from resonance.

ACOUSTIC|Reverberation.name: Reverberation
ACOUSTIC|Reverberation.definition: The persistence of sound after the source stops. Long reverberation = "live" room. Short = "dead" room.
ACOUSTIC|Reverberation.condition: The sound persists after the source stops; decay time (RT60) is long (> 1s) → "live" room.

ACOUSTIC|Shepard tone.name: Shepard tone
ACOUSTIC|Shepard tone.definition: An infinite ascending/descending tone. The pitch feels like it goes up forever (audio illusion).
ACOUSTIC|Shepard tone.condition: An infinite ascending/descending tone; the pitch feels like it goes up forever (audio illusion).

ACOUSTIC|Snell ac.name: Snell ac
ACOUSTIC|Snell ac.definition: Sound bends when passing between mediums of different density (e.g., air → water). Snell's law for pressure waves.

ACOUSTIC|Snell's law.name: Snell's law
ACOUSTIC|Snell's law.definition: Sound bends when passing between mediums of different density.
ACOUSTIC|Snell's law.condition: Sound bends when passing between mediums of different density; n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ (for pressure waves).

ACOUSTIC|Sonar.name: Sonar
ACOUSTIC|Sonar.definition: Send a pulse; listen for the echo. Maps underwater terrain, detects objects, tracks movement.
ACOUSTIC|Sonar.condition: Send a pulse underwater; multiple receivers map the terrain and detect objects.

ACOUSTIC|Soundscape.name: Soundscape
ACOUSTIC|Soundscape.definition: The entire acoustic environment as perceived by a listener. The background hum of existence.
ACOUSTIC|Soundscape.condition: The entire acoustic environment as perceived by a listener; the background hum of existence.

ACOUSTIC|Supersonic.name: Supersonic
ACOUSTIC|Supersonic.definition: Moving faster than sound creates a shock wave. A sonic boom. The geometry of the boom (Mach cone) is a pressure cone.
ACOUSTIC|Supersonic.condition: Moving faster than sound creates a shock wave (sonic boom); the Mach cone is a pressure cone.

ACOUSTIC|The field.name: The field
ACOUSTIC|The field.definition: The acoustic field is a scalar pressure distribution across space. It is the complete description of the sound state.
ACOUSTIC|The field.condition: The acoustic field is a scalar pressure distribution across space; the complete description of the sound state.

ACOUSTIC|Ultrasound.name: Ultrasound

ACOUSTIC|Whispering gallery.name: Whispering gallery

ADVERSARIAL|Blind spot.definition: act where another is known not to read
ADVERSARIAL|Blind spot.condition: Agent acts in a part of the state space that the other agent's policy is known not to monitor.

ADVERSARIAL|Break the pattern.name: Break the pattern
ADVERSARIAL|Break the pattern.definition: establish a regularity, then violate it
ADVERSARIAL|Break the pattern.condition: Agent establishes a regular pattern, then violates it to create a surprise attack.

ADVERSARIAL|Cascade of decoys.name: Cascade of decoys
ADVERSARIAL|Cascade of decoys.definition: many false targets, one real approach
ADVERSARIAL|Cascade of decoys.condition: Many false targets are presented, each defended; the real target is hidden among them.

ADVERSARIAL|Conceal.name: Conceal
ADVERSARIAL|Conceal.definition: occupy the part another cannot see
ADVERSARIAL|Conceal.condition: The object is placed in a region that the target agent cannot see (behind an occluder or outside visual field).

ADVERSARIAL|Confabulate.name: Confabulate
ADVERSARIAL|Confabulate.definition: a false story linking unrelated things
ADVERSARIAL|Confabulate.condition: Agent weaves a false, plausible story linking unrelated ambiguous events; target accepts it.

ADVERSARIAL|Decoy.name: Decoy
ADVERSARIAL|Decoy.definition: attend to one thing to redirect inference about another
ADVERSARIAL|Decoy.condition: Agent attends to (gazes at) one object but acts toward another, causing the observer to misattribute the goal.

ADVERSARIAL|Defended stand-in.name: Defended stand-in
ADVERSARIAL|Defended stand-in.definition: make another defend the wrong thing

ADVERSARIAL|Dissimulate.name: Dissimulate
ADVERSARIAL|Dissimulate.definition: let a false model of yourself be read

ADVERSARIAL|Double blind.name: Double blind
ADVERSARIAL|Double blind.definition: a false goal and a decoy at once
ADVERSARIAL|Double blind.condition: Agent provides a false goal and a decoy simultaneously; observer is misled on both counts.

ADVERSARIAL|Entrain.name: Entrain
ADVERSARIAL|Entrain.condition: Two agents synchronize their gaze shifts or movements in a reciprocal, rhythmic pattern.

ADVERSARIAL|False history.name: False history
ADVERSARIAL|False history.definition: make the past look settled so nobody looks
ADVERSARIAL|False history.condition: Agent mimics past patterns to make the present look settled, so nobody examines it closely.

ADVERSARIAL|Feint.name: Feint
ADVERSARIAL|Feint.definition: approach by a route that looks like another route
ADVERSARIAL|Feint.condition: Agent approaches via a route that looks like it is heading to one goal from the observer's viewpoint, but is actually heading to another.

ADVERSARIAL|Layered feint.name: Layered feint
ADVERSARIAL|Layered feint.definition: several misleading moves hiding one path
ADVERSARIAL|Layered feint.condition: Several misleading moves are made, hiding a single true path; each feint is concealed as a real intent.

ADVERSARIAL|Look different.name: Look different
ADVERSARIAL|Look different.condition: The object’s appearance (colour, shape, orientation) changes with the observer’s viewpoint, making it look different to different observers.

ADVERSARIAL|Lower vigilance.name: Lower vigilance
ADVERSARIAL|Lower vigilance.definition: act against your own path to be discounted
ADVERSARIAL|Lower vigilance.condition: Agent acts against its own apparent goal, causing the observer to discount that agent's future actions.

ADVERSARIAL|Mimic.name: Mimic
ADVERSARIAL|Mimic.condition: The agent copies the target's gaze pattern, using a neutral object as a proxy for the real interest.

ADVERSARIAL|Mislead.name: Mislead
ADVERSARIAL|Mislead.condition: Agent acts on a belief that is false; the deceiver provided information that caused the false belief.

ADVERSARIAL|Pretext.name: Pretext
ADVERSARIAL|Pretext.definition: act inefficiently to hide the efficient path
ADVERSARIAL|Pretext.condition: Agent takes a visibly inefficient action to hide the fact that it is actually using a more efficient hidden path.

ADVERSARIAL|Stand-in.name: Stand-in
ADVERSARIAL|Stand-in.definition: use a neutral object in place of the real one

ADVERSARIAL|Strike the gap.name: Strike the gap
ADVERSARIAL|Strike the gap.condition: Agent uses a decoy to draw attention, then acts in the known blind spot at the precise time.

ADVERSARIAL|Time the gap.name: Time the gap
ADVERSARIAL|Time the gap.definition: sync to a rhythm, act in the gap
ADVERSARIAL|Time the gap.condition: Agent synchronises with the target's rhythm, then acts during the target's known blind interval.

ADVERSARIAL|Turn the rhythm.name: Turn the rhythm
ADVERSARIAL|Turn the rhythm.condition: Agent uses the target's own timing against it; acts in the gap created by the target's rhythm.

AESTHETIC|Aesthetic attractor.name: Aesthetic attractor
AESTHETIC|Aesthetic attractor.condition: Certain patterns (e.g., fractals, golden ratio) reliably draw attention and evoke pleasure.

AESTHETIC|Aesthetic judgement.name: Aesthetic judgement
AESTHETIC|Aesthetic judgement.definition: the decision that a thing is good, and what goes into it
AESTHETIC|Aesthetic judgement.condition: A decision about whether a thing is good (beautiful) is based on fluency, emotion, and belief.

AESTHETIC|Aesthetic reward.name: Aesthetic reward
AESTHETIC|Aesthetic reward.definition: an elegant solution feels different from a working one
AESTHETIC|Aesthetic reward.condition: An elegant solution that meets expectations feels different; a reward signal is present.

AESTHETIC|Ambiguous figure.name: Ambiguous figure
AESTHETIC|Ambiguous figure.definition: two readings of one image, neither wrong
AESTHETIC|Ambiguous figure.condition: One image has two legitimate readings; the mind can switch between them; neither is wrong.

AESTHETIC|Beauty in imperfection.recipe: Clr imperfect + Sym broken + Var organic
AESTHETIC|Beauty in imperfection.name: Beauty in imperfection
AESTHETIC|Beauty in imperfection.definition: incompleteness and irregularity read as alive
AESTHETIC|Beauty in imperfection.condition: Incompleteness and irregularity are perceived as alive and natural; aesthetically pleasing.

AESTHETIC|Clear edge.name: Clear edge
AESTHETIC|Clear edge.definition: no ambiguity about what is figure and what is ground
AESTHETIC|Clear edge.condition: No ambiguity about where the figure ends and ground begins; clear boundary.

AESTHETIC|Closure.name: Closure
AESTHETIC|Closure.definition: the mind completes a broken pattern
AESTHETIC|Closure.condition: The mind fills in missing parts to complete a pattern; perceived as whole.

AESTHETIC|Continuation.name: Continuation
AESTHETIC|Continuation.definition: things along a line read as one path
AESTHETIC|Continuation.condition: Elements along a line are perceived as a continuous path; the eye follows.

AESTHETIC|Elegance.recipe: Uni high + Var minimal + Clr max
AESTHETIC|Elegance.name: Elegance
AESTHETIC|Elegance.definition: the greatest effect from the least means
AESTHETIC|Elegance.condition: The greatest effect achieved with the fewest means; maximum clarity.

AESTHETIC|Evocative ambiguity.name: Evocative ambiguity
AESTHETIC|Evocative ambiguity.condition: Suggests meaning without fully revealing it; invites the viewer to look deeper.

AESTHETIC|Evolved preference.name: Evolved preference
AESTHETIC|Evolved preference.definition: preferences for symmetry and proportion have a history
AESTHETIC|Evolved preference.condition: Preferences for symmetry and proportion have been shaped by evolutionary selection.

AESTHETIC|Fluency.name: Fluency
AESTHETIC|Fluency.definition: how easily a thing is processed; high fluency reads as good
AESTHETIC|Fluency.condition: The object is easy to process (clear, symmetrical, proportional); high fluency is judged as good.

AESTHETIC|Focus.name: Focus
AESTHETIC|Focus.definition: one element made distinct enough to draw attention
AESTHETIC|Focus.condition: One element is made distinct (by contrast) to draw attention.

AESTHETIC|Gestalt switch.name: Gestalt switch
AESTHETIC|Gestalt switch.definition: the reading flips; a hidden solution appears
AESTHETIC|Gestalt switch.condition: The perceptual reading flips suddenly; a hidden solution appears.

AESTHETIC|Harmony.name: Harmony
AESTHETIC|Harmony.condition: Different elements coexist without conflict; they share enough features to belong together.

AESTHETIC|Iconicity.name: Iconicity
AESTHETIC|Iconicity.definition: meaning compressed into a form that is instantly recognisable
AESTHETIC|Iconicity.condition: Meaning is compressed into a form that is instantly recognisable; high clarity and unity.

AESTHETIC|Illusion.name: Illusion
AESTHETIC|Illusion.definition: exploits an assumption the perceiver did not know it had
AESTHETIC|Illusion.condition: It exploits an assumption (e.g., size constancy) that the observer was not aware of.

AESTHETIC|Logarithmic spiral.name: Logarithmic spiral
AESTHETIC|Logarithmic spiral.definition: a curve that keeps its proportion as it grows
AESTHETIC|Logarithmic spiral.condition: A self‑similar spiral where the radius grows by a constant factor per turn (golden spiral).

AESTHETIC|Optimal complexity.name: Optimal complexity
AESTHETIC|Optimal complexity.definition: enough variation to be interesting, little enough to be readable — Dynamic Criticality is the same shape
AESTHETIC|Optimal complexity.condition: Enough variation to be interesting, but little enough to be readable; a sweet spot.

AESTHETIC|Order under apparent chaos.name: Order under apparent chaos
AESTHETIC|Order under apparent chaos.definition: looks disordered, has an organising principle
AESTHETIC|Order under apparent chaos.condition: Appears chaotic but has an underlying organising principle; pattern emerges at large scale.

AESTHETIC|Ostinato.name: Ostinato
AESTHETIC|Ostinato.definition: a repeating pattern that changes slightly each cycle
AESTHETIC|Ostinato.condition: A repeating pattern that changes slightly each cycle; persistent but evolving.

AESTHETIC|Proportional division.name: Proportional division
AESTHETIC|Proportional division.definition: divide so the parts relate by a fixed ratio
AESTHETIC|Proportional division.condition: The whole is divided so that the parts maintain a fixed, often simple ratio (e.g., 1:1, 1:φ).

AESTHETIC|Prototype preference.name: Prototype preference
AESTHETIC|Prototype preference.definition: the average member of a category reads as the best one
AESTHETIC|Prototype preference.condition: The average member of a category is perceived as the most pleasing or "best" example.

AESTHETIC|Proximity grouping.name: Proximity grouping
AESTHETIC|Proximity grouping.definition: things near each other read as a group
AESTHETIC|Proximity grouping.condition: Elements near each other are perceived as a group; distance threshold.

AESTHETIC|Pulse.name: Pulse
AESTHETIC|Pulse.definition: a regular beat that action can be timed to
AESTHETIC|Pulse.condition: Events occur at regular intervals; a beat that action can be timed to.

AESTHETIC|Resonance.name: Resonance
AESTHETIC|Resonance.definition: a rhythm that matches the observer's own rate
AESTHETIC|Resonance.condition: The rhythm matches the observer's internal rhythm (e.g., heartbeat), evoking a strong emotional response.

AESTHETIC|Rhythmic asymmetry.name: Rhythmic asymmetry
AESTHETIC|Rhythmic asymmetry.definition: unbalanced by position, balanced by rhythm
AESTHETIC|Rhythmic asymmetry.condition: Not balanced by position, but balance is achieved through rhythm/temporal pattern.

AESTHETIC|Self-similarity.name: Self-similarity
AESTHETIC|Self-similarity.definition: the same structure at several scales

AESTHETIC|Similarity grouping.name: Similarity grouping
AESTHETIC|Similarity grouping.definition: things alike read as a group
AESTHETIC|Similarity grouping.condition: Elements sharing a feature (color, shape, size) are perceived as a group.

AESTHETIC|Symmetrise.name: Symmetrise
AESTHETIC|Symmetrise.condition: Applying reflection, rotation, or translation yields the same shape (within tolerance).

AESTHETIC|The sublime.name: The sublime
AESTHETIC|The sublime.definition: too large to take in at once, and organised anyway
AESTHETIC|The sublime.condition: So large or complex that it cannot be taken in at once, yet it has an underlying order.

AESTHETIC|Thirds.name: Thirds
AESTHETIC|Thirds.definition: divide into nine; put what matters at the intersections
AESTHETIC|Thirds.condition: Divide the frame into a 3×3 grid; place key elements at intersections or along lines.

AESTHETIC|Triangle.name: Triangle
AESTHETIC|Triangle.definition: three elements forming an implied shape; stable and dynamic at once
AESTHETIC|Triangle.condition: Three elements form an implied triangle; visually stable yet dynamic.

AESTHETIC|Visible affordance.name: Visible affordance
AESTHETIC|Visible affordance.definition: a thing's appearance says what can be done with it
AESTHETIC|Visible affordance.condition: The appearance of the object suggests how it can be used; function is legible from form.

AESTHETIC|Visual hierarchy.name: Visual hierarchy
AESTHETIC|Visual hierarchy.definition: order elements by importance so the eye moves in sequence
AESTHETIC|Visual hierarchy.condition: Elements are ordered by importance; the eye moves in a sequence from most to least important.

AESTHETIC|Visual weight.name: Visual weight
AESTHETIC|Visual weight.definition: a dark or large thing weighs more; balance equalises it
AESTHETIC|Visual weight.condition: Larger or darker objects have more visual weight; balance is achieved when moments sum to zero.

ALEATORY|Bell laplace demon.name: Bell laplace demon
ALEATORY|Bell laplace demon.definition: A hypothetical intelligence that knows all initial conditions and all laws; it can predict the future perfectly. Chance is just hidden information.

ALEATORY|Central limit.name: Central limit
ALEATORY|Central limit.definition: The sum of many independent random variables tends toward a Gaussian distribution.

ALEATORY|Central limit theorem.name: Central limit theorem
ALEATORY|Central limit theorem.definition: The sum of many independent random variables tends toward a Gaussian.
ALEATORY|Central limit theorem.condition: The sum of many independent random variables tends toward a Gaussian distribution.

ALEATORY|Chaos theory.name: Chaos theory
ALEATORY|Chaos theory.definition: Deterministic systems that are highly sensitive to initial conditions. Randomness emerges from order.
ALEATORY|Chaos theory.condition: Deterministic systems that are highly sensitive to initial conditions; randomness emerges from order.

ALEATORY|Coin flip.name: Coin flip
ALEATORY|Coin flip.definition: A binary random event. Heads/tails. Success/failure. 50/50.
ALEATORY|Coin flip.condition: A binary random event; P(heads) = P(tails) = 0.5.

ALEATORY|Correlation causation.name: Correlation causation
ALEATORY|Correlation causation.definition: Mistaking a random association for a causal link. Spurious correlations.

ALEATORY|Correlation ≠ causation.name: Correlation ≠ causation
ALEATORY|Correlation ≠ causation.definition: Mistaking a random association for a causal link.
ALEATORY|Correlation ≠ causation.condition: Mistaking a random association for a causal link; spurious correlations.

ALEATORY|Cosmic lottery.name: Cosmic lottery
ALEATORY|Cosmic lottery.definition: The fine-tuning of the universe's constants. The probability of life existing is infinitesimally small. We are the lottery winners.
ALEATORY|Cosmic lottery.condition: The fine‑tuning of the universe's constants; the probability of life existing is infinitesimally small.

ALEATORY|Dice roll.name: Dice roll
ALEATORY|Dice roll.definition: A multi-outcome random event. 1d6, 1d20. Uniform distribution.
ALEATORY|Dice roll.condition: A multi‑outcome random event; each outcome has equal probability (1/6).

ALEATORY|Entropy.name: Entropy
ALEATORY|Entropy.definition: The entropy of a distribution is the average amount of information.
ALEATORY|Entropy.condition: The entropy of a distribution is the average amount of information (surprise) per event.

ALEATORY|Entropy inf.name: Entropy inf
ALEATORY|Entropy inf.definition: The entropy of a distribution is the average amount of information (surprise) per event.

ALEATORY|Fatalism.name: Fatalism
ALEATORY|Fatalism.definition: The belief that outcomes are predetermined. Action is meaningless.
ALEATORY|Fatalism.condition: The belief that outcomes are predetermined; action is meaningless.

ALEATORY|Free will illusion.name: Free will illusion
ALEATORY|Free will illusion.definition: The feeling of making a free choice is a deterministic illusion. Or is it the quantum randomness that enables freedom?
ALEATORY|Free will illusion.condition: The feeling of making a free choice is a deterministic illusion; or quantum randomness enables freedom.

ALEATORY|Gambler fallacy.name: Gambler fallacy
ALEATORY|Gambler fallacy.definition: Believing that a streak of heads makes tails more likely. The "law of small numbers."

ALEATORY|Gambler's fallacy.name: Gambler's fallacy
ALEATORY|Gambler's fallacy.definition: Believing that a streak of heads makes tails more likely.
ALEATORY|Gambler's fallacy.condition: Believing that a streak of heads makes tails more likely; the "law of small numbers."

ALEATORY|Gaussian.name: Gaussian
ALEATORY|Gaussian.definition: The normal distribution. The "bell curve." Most outcomes cluster near the mean.
ALEATORY|Gaussian.condition: The normal distribution; most outcomes cluster near the mean; tails are rare.

ALEATORY|Hedge.name: Hedge
ALEATORY|Hedge.definition: Take two opposing positions to reduce overall risk. Insure against bad outcomes.
ALEATORY|Hedge.condition: Take two opposing positions to reduce overall risk; insure against bad outcomes.

ALEATORY|Hot hand.name: Hot hand
ALEATORY|Hot hand.definition: Believing that a streak of successes makes future successes more likely.
ALEATORY|Hot hand.condition: Believing that a streak of successes makes future successes more likely.

ALEATORY|Karma mechanics.name: Karma mechanics
ALEATORY|Karma mechanics.definition: A random outcome is interpreted as a moral consequence of a past action. Reward or punishment.
ALEATORY|Karma mechanics.condition: A random outcome is interpreted as a moral consequence of a past action; reward or punishment.

ALEATORY|Laplace's demon.name: Laplace's demon
ALEATORY|Laplace's demon.definition: A hypothetical intelligence that knows all conditions; can predict perfectly.
ALEATORY|Laplace's demon.condition: A hypothetical intelligence that knows all initial conditions and all laws; it can predict the future perfectly.

ALEATORY|Law large numbers.name: Law large numbers
ALEATORY|Law large numbers.definition: As the sample size increases, the average outcome converges to the expected value.

ALEATORY|Law of large numbers.name: Law of large numbers
ALEATORY|Law of large numbers.definition: As sample size increases, average converges to expected value.
ALEATORY|Law of large numbers.condition: As the sample size increases, the average outcome converges to the expected value.

ALEATORY|Lottery.name: Lottery
ALEATORY|Lottery.definition: A random draw with a very low probability of a specific outcome. High variance.
ALEATORY|Lottery.condition: A random draw with a very low probability of a specific outcome; high variance.

ALEATORY|Luck attribution.name: Luck attribution
ALEATORY|Luck attribution.definition: The subjective judgment that a random outcome was caused by "luck" rather than probability.
ALEATORY|Luck attribution.condition: The subjective judgment that a random outcome was caused by "luck" rather than probability.

ALEATORY|Markov chain.name: Markov chain
ALEATORY|Markov chain.definition: The next state depends only on the current state.
ALEATORY|Markov chain.condition: A sequence where the next state depends only on the current state, not the past; memoryless.

ALEATORY|Markov chain al.name: Markov chain al
ALEATORY|Markov chain al.definition: A sequence where the next state depends only on the current state, not the past. Memoryless.

ALEATORY|Martingale.name: Martingale
ALEATORY|Martingale.definition: A betting strategy where you double your bet after every loss. Guaranteed to win eventually (if you have infinite money).
ALEATORY|Martingale.condition: A betting strategy where you double your bet after every loss; guaranteed to win eventually (if infinite money).

ALEATORY|Maximax.name: Maximax
ALEATORY|Maximax.definition: Choose the strategy that maximizes your maximum possible payoff. Go for the jackpot.
ALEATORY|Maximax.condition: Choose the strategy that maximises your maximum possible payoff; go for the jackpot.

ALEATORY|Mean reversion.name: Mean reversion
ALEATORY|Mean reversion.definition: Extreme outcomes are followed by more average outcomes. The "regression to the mean."
ALEATORY|Mean reversion.condition: Extreme outcomes are followed by more average outcomes; regression to the mean.

ALEATORY|Minimax.name: Minimax
ALEATORY|Minimax.definition: Choose the strategy that maximizes your minimum possible payoff. Play it safe.
ALEATORY|Minimax.condition: Choose the strategy that maximises your minimum possible payoff; play it safe.

ALEATORY|Monte Carlo.name: Monte Carlo
ALEATORY|Monte Carlo.definition: Using random sampling to approximate the outcome of a deterministic process. The stochastic simulation.
ALEATORY|Monte Carlo.condition: Using random sampling to approximate the outcome of a deterministic process; stochastic simulation.

ALEATORY|Monte Carlo tree search.name: Monte Carlo tree search
ALEATORY|Monte Carlo tree search.definition: Simulate many random playouts; choose the move that wins most often.
ALEATORY|Monte Carlo tree search.condition: Simulate many random playouts from a game state; choose the move that wins most often (MCTS).

ALEATORY|Monte carlo tree.name: Monte carlo tree
ALEATORY|Monte carlo tree.definition: Simulate many random playouts from a game state. Choose the move that wins most often. MCTS.

ALEATORY|Poisson.name: Poisson
ALEATORY|Poisson.definition: The distribution of the number of events in a fixed interval. Rare, independent events.
ALEATORY|Poisson.condition: The distribution of the number of events in a fixed interval; rare, independent events.

ALEATORY|Probabilistic inference.name: Probabilistic inference
ALEATORY|Probabilistic inference.definition: Update beliefs based on evidence. The probability of a hypothesis given the data.
ALEATORY|Probabilistic inference.condition: Update beliefs based on evidence; the probability of a hypothesis given the data.

ALEATORY|Pseudo random.name: Pseudo random
ALEATORY|Pseudo random.definition: A sequence that appears random but is generated by a deterministic process. The illusion of chance.

ALEATORY|Quantum indeterminacy.name: Quantum indeterminacy
ALEATORY|Quantum indeterminacy.definition: True randomness at the quantum scale. The universe is fundamentally indeterministic.
ALEATORY|Quantum indeterminacy.condition: True randomness at the quantum scale; the universe is fundamentally indeterministic.

ALEATORY|Random seed.name: Random seed
ALEATORY|Random seed.definition: The initial value that determines a sequence of pseudo-random numbers. Change the seed; change the universe.
ALEATORY|Random seed.condition: The initial value that determines a sequence of pseudo‑random numbers; change the seed, change the universe.

ALEATORY|Random walk.name: Random walk
ALEATORY|Random walk.definition: A path where each step is determined by chance. Diffusion, Brownian motion.
ALEATORY|Random walk.condition: A path where each step is determined by chance; position evolves as a diffusion process.

ALEATORY|Risk arbitrage.name: Risk arbitrage
ALEATORY|Risk arbitrage.definition: Exploit differences between perceived and actual probabilities. Bet on mispriced odds.
ALEATORY|Risk arbitrage.condition: Exploit differences between perceived and actual probabilities; bet on mispriced odds.

ALEATORY|Risk perception.name: Risk perception
ALEATORY|Risk perception.definition: The subjective assessment of risk. Low-probability, high-impact events are either ignored or overestimated.
ALEATORY|Risk perception.condition: The subjective assessment of risk; low‑probability, high‑impact events are ignored or overestimated.

ALEATORY|Sensitivity analysis.name: Sensitivity analysis
ALEATORY|Sensitivity analysis.definition: How much does the output change when the random parameters are varied?
ALEATORY|Sensitivity analysis.condition: How much does the output change when the random parameters are varied?

ALEATORY|Survivor bias.name: Survivor bias
ALEATORY|Survivor bias.definition: Observing only the outcomes that survived a selection process, ignoring the failures.
ALEATORY|Survivor bias.condition: Observing only the outcomes that survived a selection process, ignoring the failures.

ALEATORY|The dice is cast.name: The dice is cast
ALEATORY|The dice is cast.definition: The moment of commitment. The decision is made; the outcome is out of your hands.

ALEATORY|The die is cast.name: The die is cast
ALEATORY|The die is cast.definition: The moment of commitment; the outcome is out of your hands.
ALEATORY|The die is cast.condition: The moment of commitment; the decision is made; the outcome is out of your hands.

ALEATORY|The goddess Fortuna.name: The goddess Fortuna
ALEATORY|The goddess Fortuna.definition: The personification of chance. The spinning wheel. Fortune favors the bold (or the prepared).
ALEATORY|The goddess Fortuna.condition: The personification of chance; the spinning wheel; fortune favours the bold (or the prepared).

ALEATORY|The long run.name: The long run
ALEATORY|The long run.definition: In the infinite limit, probability becomes certainty. The law of large numbers is a law of cosmic justice.
ALEATORY|The long run.condition: In the infinite limit, probability becomes certainty; the law of large numbers is a law of cosmic justice.

ATMOSPHERIC|Anticyclone.name: Anticyclone
ATMOSPHERIC|Anticyclone.definition: A rotating high-pressure system. Winds spiral outward and sink. Clockwise (Northern Hemisphere).
ATMOSPHERIC|Anticyclone.condition: A rotating high‑pressure system; winds spiral outward and sink; clockwise (Northern Hemisphere).

ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric blocking.name: Atmospheric blocking
ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric blocking.definition: A stubborn high-pressure system that blocks the normal flow of weather. Causes prolonged heat or cold.
ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric blocking.condition: A stubborn high‑pressure system that blocks the normal flow of weather; causes prolonged heat or cold.

ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric river.name: Atmospheric river
ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric river.definition: A narrow corridor of very high water vapor transport. Can cause extreme rainfall and flooding.
ATMOSPHERIC|Atmospheric river.condition: A narrow corridor of very high water vapour transport; can cause extreme rainfall and flooding.

ATMOSPHERIC|Bomb cyclone.name: Bomb cyclone
ATMOSPHERIC|Bomb cyclone.definition: A cyclone that deepens extremely rapidly (pressure drop ≥ 24 mb in 24 hours). Powerful winter storms.
ATMOSPHERIC|Bomb cyclone.condition: A cyclone that deepens extremely rapidly (pressure drop ≥ 24 mb in 24 hours); powerful winter storms.

ATMOSPHERIC|Cloud formation.name: Cloud formation
ATMOSPHERIC|Cloud formation.definition: Water vapor condenses on microscopic particles (aerosols). The visible manifestation of humidity.
ATMOSPHERIC|Cloud formation.condition: Water vapour condenses on microscopic particles (aerosols); the visible manifestation of humidity.

ATMOSPHERIC|Cold front.name: Cold front
ATMOSPHERIC|Cold front.definition: A fast-moving cold air mass lifts warm air abruptly. Thunderstorms, squall lines.
ATMOSPHERIC|Cold front.condition: A fast‑moving cold air mass lifts warm air abruptly; thunderstorms, squall lines.

ATMOSPHERIC|Convection.name: Convection
ATMOSPHERIC|Convection.definition: Warm, moist air rises. Cooler, denser air sinks. The vertical circulation of the atmosphere.
ATMOSPHERIC|Convection.condition: Warm, moist air rises; cooler, denser air sinks; vertical circulation of the atmosphere.

ATMOSPHERIC|Cyclone.name: Cyclone
ATMOSPHERIC|Cyclone.definition: A rotating storm system. Winds spiral inward and upward. Counterclockwise (Northern Hemisphere).
ATMOSPHERIC|Cyclone.condition: A rotating storm system; winds spiral inward and upward; counterclockwise (Northern Hemisphere).

ATMOSPHERIC|Drought.name: Drought
ATMOSPHERIC|Drought.definition: An extended period of below-normal precipitation. Caused by persistent high pressure.
ATMOSPHERIC|Drought.condition: An extended period of below‑normal precipitation; caused by persistent high pressure.

ATMOSPHERIC|El Niño.name: El Niño
ATMOSPHERIC|El Niño.definition: A climate pattern where the equatorial Pacific warms.
ATMOSPHERIC|El Niño.condition: A climate pattern where the equatorial Pacific warms; alters global weather patterns.

ATMOSPHERIC|El nino.name: El nino
ATMOSPHERIC|El nino.definition: A climate pattern where the equatorial Pacific warms. Alters global weather patterns.

ATMOSPHERIC|Evapotranspiration.name: Evapotranspiration
ATMOSPHERIC|Evapotranspiration.definition: Water evaporates from the surface and transpires from plants. The source of atmospheric moisture.
ATMOSPHERIC|Evapotranspiration.condition: Water evaporates from the surface and transpires from plants; the source of atmospheric moisture.

ATMOSPHERIC|Front collision.name: Front collision
ATMOSPHERIC|Front collision.definition: A cold front meets a warm front. The warm air is forced up; clouds and rain form.
ATMOSPHERIC|Front collision.condition: A cold front meets a warm front; the warm air is forced up; clouds and rain form.

ATMOSPHERIC|Global circulation.name: Global circulation
ATMOSPHERIC|Global circulation.definition: The three-cell model: Hadley, Ferrel, and Polar cells. The architecture of the atmosphere.
ATMOSPHERIC|Global circulation.condition: The three‑cell model (Hadley, Ferrel, Polar cells); the architecture of the atmosphere.

ATMOSPHERIC|Heat wave.name: Heat wave
