DESIRE|The passionate soul.condition: The soul defined by its intense, sustained desires.

DESIRE|The satisfied moment.name: The satisfied moment
DESIRE|The satisfied moment.definition: The fleeting moment of desire fulfilled. The peace before the next desire arises.
DESIRE|The satisfied moment.condition: The fleeting moment of desire fulfilled; the peace before the next desire arises.

DESIRE|The unfulfilled.name: The unfulfilled
DESIRE|The unfulfilled.definition: The state of desire that is not yet fulfilled. The ache that fuels all striving.
DESIRE|The unfulfilled.condition: The state of desire that is not yet fulfilled; the ache that fuels all striving.

DESIRE|Want object.name: Want object
DESIRE|Want object.definition: A basic desire for a specific thing. The "I want that."
DESIRE|Want object.condition: Agent consistently chooses/approaches the object over alternatives; reports wanting it.

DESIRE|Wanting liking gap.name: Wanting liking gap
DESIRE|Wanting liking gap.definition: The phenomenon where wanting is stronger than liking. You pursue what you do not enjoy.

DYNAMIC|Adaptive homeostasis.name: Adaptive homeostasis
DYNAMIC|Adaptive homeostasis.definition: the baseline shifts to stay stable under changing load
DYNAMIC|Adaptive homeostasis.condition: The internal setpoint shifts to maintain stability under changing external load.

DYNAMIC|Anti-resonance.name: Anti-resonance
DYNAMIC|Anti-resonance.definition: damp one frequency deliberately to stop it amplifying

DYNAMIC|Ascent.name: Ascent
DYNAMIC|Ascent.definition: error shrinking under correction; the trajectory that ends in a win
DYNAMIC|Ascent.condition: Error is shrinking under correction; momentum carries the system toward the setpoint.

DYNAMIC|Avalanche.name: Avalanche
DYNAMIC|Avalanche.definition: a small push cascades through the whole system
DYNAMIC|Avalanche.condition: A small perturbation cascades through the whole system; scale‑free event sizes.

DYNAMIC|Bistability.name: Bistability
DYNAMIC|Bistability.definition: two stable states, and it remembers which one it was in
DYNAMIC|Bistability.condition: Two stable states exist; the system remembers which one it was in due to hysteresis.

DYNAMIC|Boom and bust.name: Boom and bust
DYNAMIC|Boom and bust.condition: Rapid expansion, followed by collapse, slow recovery, and then repeat.

DYNAMIC|Break habit.name: Break habit
DYNAMIC|Break habit.definition: inject noise while watching, and dissipate the momentum — a brake, and Damp exists in Dynamic, Acoustic and Cybernetic already
DYNAMIC|Break habit.condition: Injects small noise while observing, and applies damping to dissipate momentum and break a habitual cycle.

DYNAMIC|Burst.name: Burst
DYNAMIC|Burst.definition: a spike of activity, then quiet
DYNAMIC|Burst.condition: A brief, intense spike of activity followed by quiet; localised in time.

DYNAMIC|Catastrophe.name: Catastrophe
DYNAMIC|Catastrophe.definition: crosses a threshold and settles somewhere else entirely
DYNAMIC|Catastrophe.condition: Crosses a threshold and abruptly settles into a completely different state.

DYNAMIC|Chaos.recipe: Sens high + Coup high + Var extreme
DYNAMIC|Chaos.name: Chaos
DYNAMIC|Chaos.definition: deterministic and unpredictable; small differences explode; bounded, never repeats
DYNAMIC|Chaos.condition: Small initial differences grow exponentially; bounded but never repeats; high sensitivity to initial conditions.

DYNAMIC|Chaotic edge.name: Chaotic edge
DYNAMIC|Chaotic edge.definition: teeters without tipping; creative and risky
DYNAMIC|Chaotic edge.condition: Teeters at the edge of instability without tipping; creative but risky.

DYNAMIC|Criticality.name: Criticality
DYNAMIC|Criticality.definition: poised between order and disorder; maximal information processing
DYNAMIC|Criticality.condition: Poised at the boundary between order and chaos; maximal sensitivity to perturbations.

DYNAMIC|Death spiral.name: Death spiral
DYNAMIC|Death spiral.condition: Irreversible collapse; no recovery is possible; resources are zero.

DYNAMIC|Deep rest.name: Deep rest
DYNAMIC|Deep rest.condition: Complete shutdown; no response to any input; designed to allow recovery.

DYNAMIC|Descent.name: Descent
DYNAMIC|Descent.definition: error growing because nothing corrects it; the trajectory that ends in a loss
DYNAMIC|Descent.condition: Error is growing because no correction is applied; momentum carries it away.

DYNAMIC|Dither.name: Dither
DYNAMIC|Dither.definition: rapid small jitter that stops the system sticking to a false equilibrium
DYNAMIC|Dither.condition: Rapid, small‑amplitude oscillations that prevent the system from sticking to a false equilibrium.

DYNAMIC|Drift.recipe: Var slow + Coup low + Stim weak
DYNAMIC|Drift.name: Drift
DYNAMIC|Drift.condition: Slow, undirected change; weak coupling; no attractor; random walk.

DYNAMIC|Edge of chaos.name: Edge of chaos
DYNAMIC|Edge of chaos.definition: the boundary where computation is maximal
DYNAMIC|Edge of chaos.condition: The boundary region where computational power (information processing) is maximal.

DYNAMIC|Entrainment.name: Entrainment
DYNAMIC|Entrainment.condition: Two coupled oscillators lock phases and frequencies; phase difference constant.

DYNAMIC|Equilibrium.name: Equilibrium
DYNAMIC|Equilibrium.condition: Input equals output; net change of state variables is zero; variance low.

DYNAMIC|Excitation.name: Excitation
DYNAMIC|Excitation.definition: already under tension, so a small input produces a large response
DYNAMIC|Excitation.condition: The system is already under tension; a small input produces a disproportionately large output.

DYNAMIC|Exploit the deadlock.name: Exploit the deadlock
DYNAMIC|Exploit the deadlock.definition: act at the moment two forces cancel and neither can respond
DYNAMIC|Exploit the deadlock.condition: Acts at the exact moment when two opposing forces cancel and neither can respond.

DYNAMIC|Fatigue.name: Fatigue
DYNAMIC|Fatigue.condition: Performance degrades over time as stress continues and recovery is slow.

DYNAMIC|Flow.recipe: Stim optimal + Resp matched + Coup unity
DYNAMIC|Flow.name: Flow
DYNAMIC|Flow.definition: input matches capacity; no friction, no lag, no waste — also Psychological T3
DYNAMIC|Flow.condition: Input perfectly matches capacity; no lag; no waste; seamless integration.

DYNAMIC|Habituation.name: Habituation
DYNAMIC|Habituation.definition: the response weakens as the same thing keeps arriving
DYNAMIC|Habituation.condition: The response amplitude decreases with repeated presentation of the same stimulus.

DYNAMIC|Hysteresis.name: Hysteresis
DYNAMIC|Hysteresis.definition: the state depends on the path taken; the way up differs from the way down
DYNAMIC|Hysteresis.condition: The state depends on the direction of approach; threshold for up ≠ threshold for down.

DYNAMIC|Latency wins.name: Latency wins
DYNAMIC|Latency wins.definition: the outcome taken by the clock because nothing was chosen — not a branch selected, a default that fires on absence
DYNAMIC|Latency wins.condition: A timer has passed the threshold without any branch being selected; the default action fires.

DYNAMIC|Metastability.name: Metastability
DYNAMIC|Metastability.definition: near a stable point, easily kicked out of it
DYNAMIC|Metastability.condition: Near a stable point but with low barrier; easily kicked out; dwells then escapes.

DYNAMIC|Momentum.name: Momentum
DYNAMIC|Momentum.definition: accumulated tendency to continue; distinct from inertia, which is resistance to starting
DYNAMIC|Momentum.condition: A sustained response creates accumulated tendency to continue; resists stopping.

DYNAMIC|Negative feedback.name: Negative feedback
DYNAMIC|Negative feedback.definition: the response reduces the thing that caused it
DYNAMIC|Negative feedback.condition: The response (damping) increases with the error, reducing the error.

DYNAMIC|Oscillation.name: Oscillation
DYNAMIC|Oscillation.condition: A delayed response and low damping produce repetitive cycles; period is constant.

DYNAMIC|Perpetual novelty.name: Perpetual novelty
DYNAMIC|Perpetual novelty.definition: always new, always inside an envelope
DYNAMIC|Perpetual novelty.condition: Always produces new states but remains within a stable, adaptive envelope.

DYNAMIC|Positive feedback.name: Positive feedback
DYNAMIC|Positive feedback.condition: The response increases with the error, amplifying it further; coupling increases.

DYNAMIC|Quiescence.recipe: Stim zero + Resp zero + Var zero
DYNAMIC|Quiescence.name: Quiescence
DYNAMIC|Quiescence.definition: total stillness; no energy, no change
DYNAMIC|Quiescence.condition: No input; no output; zero fluctuations; complete stillness.

DYNAMIC|Reset.name: Reset
DYNAMIC|Reset.definition: return to a known state deliberately, rather than being returned to one
DYNAMIC|Reset.condition: Deliberately returns to a known initial state after a learning phase.

DYNAMIC|Resilience with reset.name: Resilience with reset
DYNAMIC|Resilience with reset.definition: absorbs perturbation; past a limit, resets clean
DYNAMIC|Resilience with reset.condition: Absorbs perturbations up to a limit; beyond that, resets cleanly to a baseline.

DYNAMIC|Resonance.name: Resonance
DYNAMIC|Resonance.definition: amplitude grows because the input matches the natural rate — also Aesthetic T4, Human T4
DYNAMIC|Resonance.condition: Amplitude is maximised when driving frequency matches natural frequency.

DYNAMIC|Rest.recipe: Stim low + Var low + Damp high
DYNAMIC|Rest.name: Rest
DYNAMIC|Rest.definition: stable, unchanging, unresponsive; nothing happens unless provoked
DYNAMIC|Rest.condition: Stimulus near zero; variance low; high damping; no output unless provoked.

DYNAMIC|Runaway.name: Runaway
DYNAMIC|Runaway.definition: growth with nothing to stop it
DYNAMIC|Runaway.condition: Positive feedback amplifies indefinitely; resources are not a constraint; unbounded growth.

DYNAMIC|Saturation.name: Saturation
DYNAMIC|Saturation.definition: output at a ceiling; more input changes nothing
DYNAMIC|Saturation.condition: Output is at a maximum ceiling; further increases in input produce no further output change.

DYNAMIC|Self-organised criticality.name: Self-organised criticality
DYNAMIC|Self-organised criticality.definition: it finds the edge without being tuned there

DYNAMIC|Self-sustaining rhythm.name: Self-sustaining rhythm
DYNAMIC|Self-sustaining rhythm.definition: oscillates at its own rate, independent of what drives it

DYNAMIC|Setpoint.name: Setpoint
DYNAMIC|Setpoint.definition: The reference a system compares its state against; the thing error is measured from.
DYNAMIC|Setpoint.condition: A fixed target value; error = setpoint − current; system acts to reduce error.

DYNAMIC|Setpoint [dup: Goal, Desire].name: Setpoint [dup: Goal, Desire]
DYNAMIC|Setpoint [dup: Goal, Desire].definition: the reference a system compares its state against; the thing error is measured from. Cybernetic says it directly — Goal seeking = Setpoint + Error + Action + Feedback

DYNAMIC|Slow-fast.name: Slow-fast
DYNAMIC|Slow-fast.definition: slow accumulation, fast release; two timescales

DYNAMIC|Stagnation.name: Stagnation
DYNAMIC|Stagnation.definition: error neither shrinking nor growing while the budget runs down; the trajectory that ends in a draw
DYNAMIC|Stagnation.condition: Error is neither shrinking nor growing, but the resource budget is depleting.

DYNAMIC|Stalemate.name: Stalemate
DYNAMIC|Stalemate.definition: two forces exactly balanced; nothing moves
DYNAMIC|Stalemate.condition: Two opposing forces are exactly equal and opposite; no movement; resources at zero.

DYNAMIC|Stress.recipe: Stim high + Res depleting + Damp overloaded
DYNAMIC|Stress.name: Stress
DYNAMIC|Stress.definition: pushing against a constraint while running down
DYNAMIC|Stress.condition: High input; resource decreases; damping cannot keep up; system is strained.

DYNAMIC|Urgency.name: Urgency
DYNAMIC|Urgency.definition: time pressure shortening how much gets searched before acting. Not downstream of desire — Frustration resp = Frust + Blockage, so urgency needs wanting AND being unable
DYNAMIC|Urgency.condition: Resource is running low and a threshold is approaching; time pressure shortens search.

ECONOMIC|Adverse selection.name: Adverse selection
ECONOMIC|Adverse selection.definition: when quality is unobservable, the bad drives out the good
ECONOMIC|Adverse selection.condition: When quality is unobservable, low‑quality goods drive out high‑quality goods; the market fails.

ECONOMIC|Arbitrage.name: Arbitrage
ECONOMIC|Arbitrage.definition: buy where cheap, sell where dear
ECONOMIC|Arbitrage.condition: Buy cheap in one market, sell dear in another simultaneously; price difference exploited.

ECONOMIC|Auction.name: Auction
ECONOMIC|Auction.definition: competition that reveals what people will actually pay
ECONOMIC|Auction.condition: Competitive bidding reveals participants' private valuations; highest bidder wins.

ECONOMIC|Barter.name: Barter
ECONOMIC|Barter.definition: exchange without a medium; needs both sides to want what the other has
ECONOMIC|Barter.condition: Two agents exchange goods directly; both prefer what they receive; no money involved.

ECONOMIC|Behavioural bias.name: Behavioural bias
ECONOMIC|Behavioural bias.definition: systematic departures from what payoffs imply
ECONOMIC|Behavioural bias.condition: Decisions systematically deviate from rational predictions due to heuristics and biases.

ECONOMIC|Boom and bust.name: Boom and bust
ECONOMIC|Boom and bust.condition: Expansion fuelled by credit and debt, followed by contraction and collapse; cycles.

ECONOMIC|Capital.name: Capital
ECONOMIC|Capital.definition: means of production that were themselves produced
ECONOMIC|Capital.condition: Goods that are themselves produced and used to produce more goods in the future; depreciates over time.

ECONOMIC|Collusion.name: Collusion
ECONOMIC|Collusion.condition: Competitors secretly agree to not compete, fixing prices or output.

ECONOMIC|Competition.name: Competition
ECONOMIC|Competition.definition: pressure toward lower price or higher quality
ECONOMIC|Competition.condition: Multiple sellers drive prices down and quality up; each acts independently.

ECONOMIC|Consumption.name: Consumption
ECONOMIC|Consumption.definition: the final use; the resource is gone
ECONOMIC|Consumption.condition: The resource is used and its utility is extracted; it is gone.

ECONOMIC|Cooperation dilemma.name: Cooperation dilemma
ECONOMIC|Cooperation dilemma.definition: rational individual choices produce a worse joint outcome
ECONOMIC|Cooperation dilemma.condition: Individual rational choices lead to a worse collective outcome; defection is tempting but cooperative would be better.

ECONOMIC|Corrective price.name: Corrective price
ECONOMIC|Corrective price.definition: make the private cost match the real one
ECONOMIC|Corrective price.condition: A tax is added to the private cost to make it equal to the total social cost.

ECONOMIC|Debt.name: Debt
ECONOMIC|Debt.definition: a promise of future resource for present resource
ECONOMIC|Debt.condition: A present resource is obtained in exchange for a future promise; includes interest and risk.

ECONOMIC|Emergent order.name: Emergent order
ECONOMIC|Emergent order.condition: Spontaneous coordination arises without central planning, driven by self‑interest and prices.

ECONOMIC|Equilibrium strategy.name: Equilibrium strategy
ECONOMIC|Equilibrium strategy.condition: No player can improve by changing strategy unilaterally; each strategy is a best response.

ECONOMIC|Externality.name: Externality
ECONOMIC|Externality.definition: someone outside the exchange bears part of it
ECONOMIC|Externality.condition: A cost of production is borne by a third party not involved in the transaction.

ECONOMIC|Inflation.name: Inflation
ECONOMIC|Inflation.definition: more of the measure chasing the same goods
ECONOMIC|Inflation.condition: The money supply grows faster than goods supply; general price level increases.

ECONOMIC|Institutions.name: Institutions
ECONOMIC|Institutions.definition: the structures that make repeated interaction possible
ECONOMIC|Institutions.condition: Structures (laws, norms) that enable repeated interaction; supported by enforcement and reputation.

ECONOMIC|Investment.name: Investment
ECONOMIC|Investment.condition: Deferring current consumption for a future return; resource committed now.

ECONOMIC|Liquidity.name: Liquidity
ECONOMIC|Liquidity.definition: how easily a thing converts without losing value
ECONOMIC|Liquidity.condition: The ease with which an asset can be converted to cash without losing value.

ECONOMIC|Market.name: Market
ECONOMIC|Market.definition: many buyers and sellers at agreed prices
ECONOMIC|Market.condition: Many buyers and sellers interact at agreed prices; some have private information.

ECONOMIC|Money.name: Money
ECONOMIC|Money.definition: a store of value that reduces the cost of transacting
ECONOMIC|Money.condition: A widely accepted, fungible token that reduces transaction costs; scarce.

ECONOMIC|Monopoly.name: Monopoly
ECONOMIC|Monopoly.condition: A single seller controls the market; prices are high, output low; barriers to entry.

ECONOMIC|Moral hazard.name: Moral hazard
ECONOMIC|Moral hazard.definition: one party takes risk because another bears the cost
ECONOMIC|Moral hazard.condition: One party takes more risk because another bears the cost; hidden actions are not observed.

ECONOMIC|Network effect.name: Network effect
ECONOMIC|Network effect.definition: worth more the more others use it
ECONOMIC|Network effect.condition: The value of a good increases as more people adopt it; positive externality.

ECONOMIC|Oligopoly.name: Oligopoly
ECONOMIC|Oligopoly.condition: A few sellers must anticipate each other's moves; strategic interdependence.

ECONOMIC|Price discovery.name: Price discovery
ECONOMIC|Price discovery.definition: converging on a price through offers
ECONOMIC|Price discovery.condition: Through offers and bids, a clearing price emerges; converges over time.

ECONOMIC|Production.name: Production
ECONOMIC|Production.condition: Inputs are transformed into an output worth more than the sum of input costs.

ECONOMIC|Public good.name: Public good
ECONOMIC|Public good.definition: nobody can be kept out and use does not deplete it
ECONOMIC|Public good.condition: Nobody can be excluded from using it, and one person's use does not deplete it.

ECONOMIC|Reputation.name: Reputation
ECONOMIC|Reputation.definition: past behaviour becomes an expectation about future behaviour
ECONOMIC|Reputation.condition: Past behaviour creates an expectation of future behaviour; reputation affects trust.

ECONOMIC|Saving.name: Saving
ECONOMIC|Saving.condition: Withholding a surplus resource against future uncertainty; not consuming it now.

ECONOMIC|Screening.name: Screening
ECONOMIC|Screening.definition: offer a menu that makes the other side reveal which they are
ECONOMIC|Screening.condition: A contract or menu is offered such that different types reveal themselves by their choice.

ECONOMIC|Signalling.name: Signalling
ECONOMIC|Signalling.definition: an action expensive enough that only a truthful sender would take it
ECONOMIC|Signalling.condition: An action is expensive enough that only a truthful sender would take it; it credibly conveys information.

ECONOMIC|Stated valuation.name: Stated valuation
ECONOMIC|Stated valuation.definition: estimate what an unpriced thing is worth by asking
ECONOMIC|Stated valuation.condition: Estimating the value of an unpriced good by directly asking people what they would pay.

ECONOMIC|Strategy learning.name: Strategy learning
ECONOMIC|Strategy learning.condition: Players update their strategies based on past payoffs; converge to an equilibrium over time.

ECONOMIC|Subsidy.name: Subsidy
ECONOMIC|Subsidy.definition: make the private benefit match the real one
ECONOMIC|Subsidy.condition: A payment is given to the producer to make the private benefit equal to the total social benefit.

ECONOMIC|Sunk cost.name: Sunk cost
ECONOMIC|Sunk cost.definition: already spent and unrecoverable; it should not affect the next choice and usually does
ECONOMIC|Sunk cost.condition: A past cost that cannot be recovered; it should not affect future decisions, but it often does.

ECONOMIC|Supply and demand.name: Supply and demand
ECONOMIC|Supply and demand.definition: the price at which the two meet
ECONOMIC|Supply and demand.condition: The intersection of supply and demand curves determines the market price.

ECONOMIC|Tragedy of the commons.name: Tragedy of the commons
ECONOMIC|Tragedy of the commons.definition: overuse because benefit is private and cost is shared
ECONOMIC|Tragedy of the commons.condition: Individuals acting in their own self‑interest overuse a shared resource; collective cost is high.

ECONOMIC|Unpriced service.name: Unpriced service
ECONOMIC|Unpriced service.definition: a benefit that nothing charges for and everything depends on
ECONOMIC|Unpriced service.condition: A benefit from a natural system that has no market price but is essential (e.g., pollination).

ELECTRICAL|AND.name: AND
ELECTRICAL|AND.condition: Output is high only if both inputs are high (switches in series).

ELECTRICAL|Amplifier.name: Amplifier
ELECTRICAL|Amplifier.definition: a small signal drives a large one
ELECTRICAL|Amplifier.condition: Output signal is a scaled copy of the input, using power from the battery.

ELECTRICAL|Battery.name: Battery
ELECTRICAL|Battery.condition: Maintains a constant potential difference between terminals; can deliver current for a period.

ELECTRICAL|Capacitor.name: Capacitor
ELECTRICAL|Capacitor.condition: C = Q/V; stores charge; voltage lags current.

ELECTRICAL|Conductor.name: Conductor
ELECTRICAL|Conductor.condition: Charge flows easily; low resistivity; current is proportional to voltage.

ELECTRICAL|Diode.name: Diode
ELECTRICAL|Diode.condition: Conducts current in one direction only; blocks in the reverse direction.

ELECTRICAL|Electromagnet.name: Electromagnet
ELECTRICAL|Electromagnet.condition: A magnetic field is produced when current flows through a coil; B ∝ I·N.

ELECTRICAL|Frequency filter.name: Frequency filter
ELECTRICAL|Frequency filter.definition: blocks above or below a rate
ELECTRICAL|Frequency filter.condition: LC circuit blocks or passes signals above/below a resonant frequency (f = 1/(2π√LC)).

ELECTRICAL|Generator.name: Generator
ELECTRICAL|Generator.condition: Mechanical rotation in a magnetic field induces a voltage; produces electrical current.

ELECTRICAL|Induction.name: Induction
ELECTRICAL|Induction.definition: a changing field drives a flow
ELECTRICAL|Induction.condition: A moving conductor in a magnetic field has an induced EMF; E = B·L·v.

ELECTRICAL|Inductor.name: Inductor
ELECTRICAL|Inductor.condition: V = L · dI/dt; opposes changes in current; voltage leads current.

ELECTRICAL|Insulator.name: Insulator
ELECTRICAL|Insulator.condition: Charge does not flow; very high resistivity; current ≈ 0 for any voltage.

ELECTRICAL|Levitation.name: Levitation
ELECTRICAL|Levitation.definition: hold a thing up without contact
ELECTRICAL|Levitation.condition: Magnetic repulsion balances gravity; object floats with a measurable air gap.

ELECTRICAL|Memory cell.name: Memory cell
ELECTRICAL|Memory cell.condition: The cell holds one bit; can be set/reset; retains state without input.

ELECTRICAL|Motor.name: Motor
ELECTRICAL|Motor.condition: Electrical input produces rotational mechanical output; torque is proportional to current.

ELECTRICAL|NOT.name: NOT
ELECTRICAL|NOT.condition: Output is high when input is low, and vice versa.

ELECTRICAL|OR.name: OR
ELECTRICAL|OR.condition: Output is high if either input is high (switches in parallel).

ELECTRICAL|Oscillator.name: Oscillator
ELECTRICAL|Oscillator.condition: RC circuit with inverter provides positive feedback; outputs a square wave of frequency 1/(RC).

ELECTRICAL|Permanent magnet.name: Permanent magnet
ELECTRICAL|Permanent magnet.condition: Ferromagnetic material has aligned domains; produces magnetic field without external current.

ELECTRICAL|Propagating wave.name: Propagating wave
ELECTRICAL|Propagating wave.condition: Oscillating currents in an antenna radiate electromagnetic waves; fields propagate at c.

ELECTRICAL|Receiver.name: Receiver
ELECTRICAL|Receiver.definition: extract a signal from a wave
ELECTRICAL|Receiver.condition: Antenna intercepts the wave; circuit extracts the original signal from the carrier.

ELECTRICAL|Rectifier.name: Rectifier
ELECTRICAL|Rectifier.condition: Diode allows only one half‑cycle; capacitor smoothes the output.

ELECTRICAL|Relay.name: Relay
ELECTRICAL|Relay.definition: a switch thrown by a field
ELECTRICAL|Relay.condition: Current through the electromagnet closes (or opens) a separate switch.

ELECTRICAL|Resistance law.name: Resistance law
ELECTRICAL|Resistance law.definition: flow is the difference over the opposition
ELECTRICAL|Resistance law.condition: V = I × R; measured values satisfy Ohm's law.

ELECTRICAL|Resistor.name: Resistor
ELECTRICAL|Resistor.condition: A component with a defined resistance; V = I·R; dissipates power as heat (I²R).

ELECTRICAL|Switch.name: Switch
ELECTRICAL|Switch.condition: When closed, current flows; when open, current stops.

ELECTRICAL|Transistor.name: Transistor
ELECTRICAL|Transistor.definition: a small input controls a large one
ELECTRICAL|Transistor.condition: A small current at the base controls a much larger current between collector and emitter.

ELECTRICAL|Zero resistance.name: Zero resistance
ELECTRICAL|Zero resistance.condition: Below critical temperature, resistance drops to zero; current persists indefinitely.

EMBODIMENT|Action binding.name: Action binding
EMBODIMENT|Action binding.definition: The perceived time between an action and its consequence shrinks. You feel in control when actions are tightly coupled.
EMBODIMENT|Action binding.condition: The perceived time between an action and its consequence is shortened; high agency correlates with stronger binding.

EMBODIMENT|Affordance sense.name: Affordance sense
EMBODIMENT|Affordance sense.definition: The immediate, non-cognitive sense of whether a gap is jumpable, a ledge is graspable, or a surface is walkable.
EMBODIMENT|Affordance sense.condition: The immediate, non‑cognitive sense of whether a gap is jumpable or a ledge is graspable is accurate.

EMBODIMENT|Balance vector.name: Balance vector
EMBODIMENT|Balance vector.definition: Sense the direction of "down" and the body's tilt relative to it. Determines if you're about to fall.
EMBODIMENT|Balance vector.condition: Vestibular signal indicates the direction of down; COM is projected over the support base.

EMBODIMENT|Core stability.name: Core stability
EMBODIMENT|Core stability.definition: The active engagement of core muscles to keep the torso stable while limbs move. A balance constraint.
EMBODIMENT|Core stability.condition: Core muscles are activated to keep the COM within the base of support; balance is maintained during limb movement.

EMBODIMENT|Cotard delusion.name: Cotard delusion
EMBODIMENT|Cotard delusion.definition: The extreme feeling of not being "in" one's body, or believing one is dead. Used for *critical system failure* states.
EMBODIMENT|Cotard delusion.condition: Internal signals are flat; presence is absent; no sense of agency; extreme detachment from body.

EMBODIMENT|Dissociation.name: Dissociation
EMBODIMENT|Dissociation.definition: The feeling of watching yourself from outside. Actions happen, but you don't feel like the author. A trap state.
EMBODIMENT|Dissociation.condition: Agent reports watching itself from outside; actions are perceived as not self‑authored.

EMBODIMENT|Efference sense.name: Efference sense
EMBODIMENT|Efference sense.definition: Predict what the next sensory frame *should* feel like if you move your arm. If the world moves differently, you know an external force is acting on you.
EMBODIMENT|Efference sense.condition: Predicted sensation matches actual sensation when action is self‑caused; mismatch indicates external force.

EMBODIMENT|Effort sense.name: Effort sense
EMBODIMENT|Effort sense.definition: The subjective feeling of "heaviness." Lifting a heavy object is felt as more effort than lifting a light one.
EMBODIMENT|Effort sense.condition: Subjective feeling of effort correlates with muscle activity and torque; heavier loads feel harder.

EMBODIMENT|Embodied cognition.name: Embodied cognition
EMBODIMENT|Embodied cognition.definition: Thinking is not just in the brain. The body shapes thought (e.g., holding a warm drink makes you feel socially warmer).
EMBODIMENT|Embodied cognition.condition: Thinking is shaped by the body (e.g., holding a warm drink makes social judgments warmer).

EMBODIMENT|Embodied grasp.name: Embodied grasp
EMBODIMENT|Embodied grasp.definition: When you pick up a tool, your brain shrinks the tool's length into your existing hand map. The tool feels like an extension.
EMBODIMENT|Embodied grasp.condition: When using a tool, the brain updates the hand map to include the tool's length; error in reach is reduced.

EMBODIMENT|Embodied simulation.name: Embodied simulation
EMBODIMENT|Embodied simulation.definition: To predict an adversary's move, you simulate it in your own motor cortex. You feel their movement as if it were your own.
EMBODIMENT|Embodied simulation.condition: To predict another's move, the agent's motor cortex simulates it; activation mirrors the observed action.

EMBODIMENT|Haptic exploration.name: Haptic exploration
EMBODIMENT|Haptic exploration.definition: Use touch to identify an object without looking at it (e.g., finding a key in a bag by feel).
EMBODIMENT|Haptic exploration.condition: Using touch alone, the agent can identify an object (e.g., a key in a bag) by its texture and shape.

EMBODIMENT|Heartbeat.name: Heartbeat
EMBODIMENT|Heartbeat.definition: A low-frequency rhythmic pulse. In a puzzle, it can serve as a hidden timer or signal resource depletion.
EMBODIMENT|Heartbeat.condition: A low‑frequency rhythmic pulse is detected from internal sensors; period is regular.

EMBODIMENT|Hyper agency.name: Hyper agency
EMBODIMENT|Hyper agency.definition: Over-attributing causal power to oneself. "I made that happen" even when it was random. Useful for adversarial bluffing.
EMBODIMENT|Hyper agency.condition: Agent over‑attributes causality to its own actions, even when the outcome was random.

EMBODIMENT|Joint angle.name: Joint angle
EMBODIMENT|Joint angle.definition: Know the exact flexion/extension of every joint (elbow, knee, wrist) without visual feedback.
EMBODIMENT|Joint angle.condition: Proprioceptive signal matches actual joint angle (from vision or goniometer) within 5°.

EMBODIMENT|Motor imagery.name: Motor imagery
EMBODIMENT|Motor imagery.definition: Vividly imagining a movement activates the same brain areas as performing it. Used to "practice" a solution without cost.
EMBODIMENT|Motor imagery.condition: Vividly imagining a movement activates the same motor areas as performing it, without muscle execution.

EMBODIMENT|Pain feedback.name: Pain feedback
EMBODIMENT|Pain feedback.definition: Intense pressure or heat triggers a pain signal. This forces a rapid withdrawal reflex (faster than conscious thought).
EMBODIMENT|Pain feedback.condition: Intense pressure or heat triggers a nociceptor signal; withdrawal reflex occurs within <100 ms.

EMBODIMENT|Peripersonal space.name: Peripersonal space
EMBODIMENT|Peripersonal space.definition: The immediate space within arm's reach. Objects in this space are processed as part of the "extended body."
EMBODIMENT|Peripersonal space.condition: Objects within arm's reach are processed as part of the extended body; faster reaction to threats in peripersonal space.

EMBODIMENT|Placebo effect.name: Placebo effect
EMBODIMENT|Placebo effect.definition: The mere belief that a tool/action will help causes real physiological changes (reduced pain, increased energy).
EMBODIMENT|Placebo effect.condition: The mere belief that a treatment will help causes real physiological changes (e.g., reduced pain, increased energy).

EMBODIMENT|Plastic boundary.name: Plastic boundary
EMBODIMENT|Plastic boundary.definition: The boundary between self and world is fundamentally porous and shifts moment-to-moment based on attention and use.
EMBODIMENT|Plastic boundary.condition: The boundary between self and world shifts moment‑to‑moment based on attention and tool use.

EMBODIMENT|Postural sway.name: Postural sway
EMBODIMENT|Postural sway.definition: The constant micro-adjustments the body makes to maintain balance. In a puzzle: a dynamic offset that must be countered.
EMBODIMENT|Postural sway.condition: Constant micro‑adjustments are detectable; sway amplitude and frequency are measurable.

EMBODIMENT|Pressure map.name: Pressure map
EMBODIMENT|Pressure map.definition: A spatial map of pressure on the skin. Knows if you are leaning against a wall, standing on a sharp object, or holding something.
EMBODIMENT|Pressure map.condition: A spatial map of pressure on the skin is available; localised to specific body parts.

EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive drift.name: Proprioceptive drift
EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive drift.definition: Under fatigue or sensory deprivation, the internal sense of limb position "drifts" and becomes unreliable.
EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive drift.condition: Under fatigue or sensory deprivation, the internal sense of limb position drifts from actual position.

EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive recalibration.name: Proprioceptive recalibration
EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive recalibration.definition: Put on prism goggles that shift your vision 20 degrees left. Your proprioception adapts to the new visual input within minutes.
EMBODIMENT|Proprioceptive recalibration.condition: After wearing prism goggles, proprioception adapts to the new visual input within minutes (e.g., pointing error reduces).

EMBODIMENT|Prototactic self.name: Prototactic self
EMBODIMENT|Prototactic self.definition: The most primitive sense of self: a collection of felt sensations that distinguish "inside" from "outside."
EMBODIMENT|Prototactic self.condition: The most primitive sense of "me" vs. "not‑me"; based on felt sensations and boundary.

EMBODIMENT|Resource gauge.name: Resource gauge
EMBODIMENT|Resource gauge.definition: The felt sense of "stamina" or "energy." Low resource = sluggish movements, weaker pushes.
EMBODIMENT|Resource gauge.condition: The felt sense of "stamina" correlates with ATP levels; low resource leads to sluggish movements.

EMBODIMENT|Rubber hand.name: Rubber hand
EMBODIMENT|Rubber hand.definition: The body schema can incorporate a foreign object (e.g., a rubber hand) if it is stroked synchronously with your real hand. *Tool incorporation.*
EMBODIMENT|Rubber hand.condition: When a rubber hand is stroked synchronously with the real hand, it is incorporated into the body schema; self‑report of ownership.

EMBODIMENT|Self agency.name: Self agency
EMBODIMENT|Self agency.definition: The felt sense that "I caused this." If your action produces the predicted outcome, agency is high. If not, agency is diminished (you feel like a puppet).
EMBODIMENT|Self agency.condition: The outcome matches the predicted consequence; temporal binding (time compression) is present.

EMBODIMENT|Self orient.name: Self orient
EMBODIMENT|Self orient.definition: Know which way is up relative to the head, independent of visual cues.
EMBODIMENT|Self orient.condition: Knows which way is up relative to the head, independent of visual cues; accurate in darkness.

EMBODIMENT|Somatic marker.name: Somatic marker
EMBODIMENT|Somatic marker.definition: Bodily signals (e.g., gut feelings, racing heart) influence decision-making. A "hunch" or intuition has a physical correlate.
EMBODIMENT|Somatic marker.condition: Physiological signals change before a decision; the decision is influenced by these bodily signals (hunch).

EMBODIMENT|The lived body.name: The lived body
EMBODIMENT|The lived body.definition: The body is not just a physical object; it is the *subject* of experience. It is a point of view anchored in space and time.
EMBODIMENT|The lived body.condition: Agent reports the body as a point of view, not just an object; experience is anchored in space and time.

EMBODIMENT|Tool extension.name: Tool extension
EMBODIMENT|Tool extension.definition: A grappling hook, a long stick, or a mechanical arm is incorporated into the body schema. Your perceived reach extends by its length.
EMBODIMENT|Tool extension.condition: A tool (grappling hook, stick) is incorporated; perceived reach extends to include its length; errors in distance estimation are reduced.

EMBODIMENT|Touch localization.name: Touch localization
EMBODIMENT|Touch localization.definition: Know exactly *where* on the body you are being touched (e.g., finger vs. shoulder).
EMBODIMENT|Touch localization.condition: Touch is perceived as occurring at a specific location on the body (e.g., finger, shoulder).

EMBODIMENT|Vestibular habituation.name: Vestibular habituation
EMBODIMENT|Vestibular habituation.definition: After repeated spinning or oscillating, the vestibular system adapts and no longer signals disorientation.
EMBODIMENT|Vestibular habituation.condition: After repeated spinning or oscillating, the vestibular signal diminishes; dizziness decreases.

EMOTION|Affect heuristic.name: Affect heuristic
EMOTION|Affect heuristic.definition: Decisions are made by consulting the "gut feeling" (affect) rather than rational analysis.
EMOTION|Affect heuristic.condition: Decisions are made by consulting the "gut feeling" (affect) rather than rational analysis.

EMOTION|Anger frame.name: Anger frame
EMOTION|Anger frame.definition: Perceive an obstacle as an injustice. Attack the obstacle with increased force.
EMOTION|Anger frame.condition: Perceive an obstacle as an injustice; attack the obstacle with increased force.

EMOTION|Arousal judge.name: Arousal judge
EMOTION|Arousal judge.definition: Automatically calibrate activation level. High arousal = urgent; Low arousal = indifferent.
EMOTION|Arousal judge.condition: Automatically calibrate activation level; high arousal = urgent; low arousal = indifferent.

EMOTION|Chronic anger.name: Chronic anger
EMOTION|Chronic anger.definition: A persistent state of irritability. Low threshold for aggression.
EMOTION|Chronic anger.condition: A persistent state of irritability; low threshold for aggression.

EMOTION|Chronic mood.name: Chronic mood
EMOTION|Chronic mood.definition: A stable, long-term emotional baseline. The agent's "tone."
EMOTION|Chronic mood.condition: A stable, long‑term emotional baseline; the agent's "tone."

EMOTION|Disgust reject.name: Disgust reject
EMOTION|Disgust reject.definition: Reject a stimulus (food, idea, agent) that is perceived as harmful or impure.

EMOTION|Disgust rejection.name: Disgust rejection
EMOTION|Disgust rejection.definition: Reject a stimulus perceived as harmful or impure.
EMOTION|Disgust rejection.condition: Reject a stimulus (food, idea, agent) perceived as harmful or impure.

EMOTION|Dissonance reduction.name: Dissonance reduction
EMOTION|Dissonance reduction.definition: When emotion and belief conflict, one or both change.
EMOTION|Dissonance reduction.condition: When emotion and belief conflict, one or both change to reduce dissonance.

EMOTION|Dissonance redux.name: Dissonance redux
EMOTION|Dissonance redux.definition: When emotion and belief conflict, one or both change. Cognitive dissonance.

EMOTION|Emotional cascade.name: Emotional cascade
EMOTION|Emotional cascade.definition: A fear response triggers physiological arousal, which amplifies the fear, etc. Panic attack.
EMOTION|Emotional cascade.condition: A fear response triggers physiological arousal, which amplifies the fear; panic attack.

EMOTION|Emotional debt.name: Emotional debt
EMOTION|Emotional debt.definition: Chronic emotional regulation has a cost. Burnout and emotional exhaustion.
EMOTION|Emotional debt.condition: Chronic emotional regulation has a cost; burnout and emotional exhaustion.

EMOTION|Emotional intelligence.name: Emotional intelligence
EMOTION|Emotional intelligence.definition: The ability to perceive, use, understand, and manage emotions effectively.
EMOTION|Emotional intelligence.condition: The ability to perceive, use, understand, and manage emotions effectively.

EMOTION|Emotional memory.name: Emotional memory
EMOTION|Emotional memory.definition: Emotions enhance memory consolidation. Highly emotional events are remembered better.
EMOTION|Emotional memory.condition: Emotions enhance memory consolidation; highly emotional events are remembered better.

EMOTION|Emotional regulation.name: Emotional regulation
EMOTION|Emotional regulation.definition: Deliberately reinterpret a situation to change the emotional response. Cognitive reframing.
EMOTION|Emotional regulation.condition: Deliberately reinterpret a situation to change the emotional response; cognitive reframing.

EMOTION|Empathy.name: Empathy
EMOTION|Empathy.condition: Feel what another agent feels; the mirror neuron system.

EMOTION|Empathy emo.name: Empathy emo
EMOTION|Empathy emo.definition: Feel what another agent feels. The mirror neuron system.

EMOTION|Envy.name: Envy
EMOTION|Envy.definition: Negative valence at another's success. Promotes competition or sour grapes.
EMOTION|Envy.condition: Negative valence at another's success; promotes competition or sour grapes.

EMOTION|Fear condition.name: Fear condition
EMOTION|Fear condition.definition: Associate a neutral stimulus with a threat. The neutral stimulus now triggers fear.

EMOTION|Fear conditioning.name: Fear conditioning
EMOTION|Fear conditioning.definition: Associate a neutral stimulus with a threat.
EMOTION|Fear conditioning.condition: A neutral stimulus paired with a threat now triggers a fear response (e.g., freezing).

EMOTION|Felt sense.name: Felt sense
EMOTION|Felt sense.definition: The embodied, pre-reflective sense of what is true or right. A "gut feeling."
EMOTION|Felt sense.condition: The embodied, pre‑reflective sense of what is true or right; a "gut feeling."

EMOTION|Flow modulation.name: Flow modulation
EMOTION|Flow modulation.definition: Positive emotion at the intersection of high skill and high challenge. The flow state.
EMOTION|Flow modulation.condition: Positive emotion at the intersection of high skill and high challenge; the flow state.

EMOTION|Gratitude.name: Gratitude
EMOTION|Gratitude.definition: Positive valence toward an agent who provided a benefit. Promotes reciprocity.
EMOTION|Gratitude.condition: Positive valence toward an agent who provided a benefit; promotes reciprocity.

EMOTION|Guilt.name: Guilt
EMOTION|Guilt.definition: Negative valence directed at the self for a perceived transgression. Promotes reparation.
EMOTION|Guilt.condition: Negative valence directed at the self for a perceived transgression; promotes reparation.

EMOTION|Joy reward.name: Joy reward
EMOTION|Joy reward.definition: A positive outcome reinforces the preceding action. Dopamine release.
EMOTION|Joy reward.condition: A positive outcome reinforces the preceding action; dopamine release occurs.

EMOTION|Learned fear.name: Learned fear
EMOTION|Learned fear.definition: A fear response that has been generalized to a broad context. Phobia.
EMOTION|Learned fear.condition: A fear response that has been generalised to a broad context; phobia.

EMOTION|Mood cycle.name: Mood cycle
EMOTION|Mood cycle.definition: A persistent emotional background that colors all experiences. Positive mood = optimistic bias.
EMOTION|Mood cycle.condition: A persistent emotional background that colours all experiences; positive mood = optimistic bias.

EMOTION|Moral emotions.name: Moral emotions
EMOTION|Moral emotions.definition: Emotions that enforce social norms. They regulate behavior within a group.
EMOTION|Moral emotions.condition: Emotions that enforce social norms; they regulate behaviour within a group.

EMOTION|Neural melody.name: Neural melody
EMOTION|Neural melody.definition: Emotions have a neural melody. A specific frequency and rhythm of brain activity.
EMOTION|Neural melody.condition: Emotions have a neural melody; a specific frequency and rhythm of brain activity.

EMOTION|Pride.name: Pride
EMOTION|Pride.definition: Positive valence directed at the self for an accomplishment. Promotes future effort.
EMOTION|Pride.condition: Positive valence directed at the self for an accomplishment; promotes future effort.

EMOTION|Primordial appraisal.name: Primordial appraisal
EMOTION|Primordial appraisal.definition: The first, non-conscious evaluation of a stimulus. Emotion precedes cognition.
EMOTION|Primordial appraisal.condition: The first, non‑conscious evaluation of a stimulus; emotion precedes cognition.

EMOTION|Sad withdraw.name: Sad withdraw
EMOTION|Sad withdraw.definition: Withdraw from activity. Conserve energy. Reflect on the loss.

EMOTION|Sad withdrawal.name: Sad withdrawal
EMOTION|Sad withdrawal.condition: Withdraw from activity; conserve energy; reflect on the loss.

EMOTION|Shame.name: Shame
EMOTION|Shame.definition: Negative valence directed at the self for a social failure. Promotes withdrawal.
EMOTION|Shame.condition: Negative valence directed at the self for a social failure; promotes withdrawal.

EMOTION|Social contagion.name: Social contagion
EMOTION|Social contagion.definition: Emotions spread through a group like a virus. A wave of panic or joy.
EMOTION|Social contagion.condition: Emotions spread through a group like a virus; a wave of panic or joy.

EMOTION|Surprise update.name: Surprise update
EMOTION|Surprise update.definition: A violation of expectation. Pause and attend to the anomaly.
EMOTION|Surprise update.condition: A violation of expectation; pause and attend to the anomaly.

EMOTION|The affective engine.name: The affective engine
EMOTION|The affective engine.definition: The engine that drives all behavior. Approach/avoid is the fundamental binary.
EMOTION|The affective engine.condition: The engine that drives all behaviour; approach/avoid is the fundamental binary.

EMOTION|The affective niche.name: The affective niche
EMOTION|The affective niche.definition: Organisms construct their environment to maintain a preferred emotional state.
EMOTION|The affective niche.condition: Organisms construct their environment to maintain a preferred emotional state.

EMOTION|The emotional universe.name: The emotional universe
EMOTION|The emotional universe.definition: The universe is not neutral; it is valenced. Everything has a felt tone.
EMOTION|The emotional universe.condition: The universe is not neutral; it is valenced; everything has a felt tone.

EMOTION|The somatic compass.name: The somatic compass
EMOTION|The somatic compass.definition: The body is a compass. It points toward what is good and away from what is bad.
EMOTION|The somatic compass.condition: The body is a compass; it points toward what is good and away from what is bad.

EMOTION|Valence judge.name: Valence judge
EMOTION|Valence judge.definition: Automatically assign a positive or negative value to a stimulus. Approach (+) or avoid (-).
EMOTION|Valence judge.condition: Automatically assign a positive/negative value to a stimulus; positive → approach, negative → avoid.

EXCHANGE|Arbitrage.name: Arbitrage

EXCHANGE|Arbitrage.condition: Buying low in one market and selling high in another.

EXCHANGE|Auction.name: Auction
EXCHANGE|Auction.condition: Exchange through competitive bidding; highest bidder wins.

EXCHANGE|Barter.name: Barter
EXCHANGE|Barter.definition: Direct exchange of one resource for another. No medium.
EXCHANGE|Barter.condition: Direct exchange of one resource for another; no money involved; double coincidence of wants.

EXCHANGE|Bidding war.name: Bidding war
EXCHANGE|Bidding war.definition: A competitive exchange where desire drives prices up.
EXCHANGE|Bidding war.condition: A competitive exchange where desire drives prices up.

EXCHANGE|Buy.name: Buy
EXCHANGE|Buy.definition: Acquiring a resource by giving currency. The "purchase."
EXCHANGE|Buy.condition: Acquiring a resource by giving currency; a purchase.

EXCHANGE|Charity.name: Charity
EXCHANGE|Charity.definition: Giving to those in need, without expectation of return.
EXCHANGE|Charity.condition: Giving to those in need, without expectation of return.

EXCHANGE|Contract.name: Contract
EXCHANGE|Contract.definition: A formalized agreement that ensures exchange, backed by enforcement.
EXCHANGE|Contract.condition: A formalised agreement that ensures exchange, backed by enforcement.

EXCHANGE|Credit system.definition: A system where value is exchanged now against future repayment, with interest.
EXCHANGE|Credit system.condition: A system where value is exchanged now against future repayment, with interest.

EXCHANGE|Currency net.name: Currency net
EXCHANGE|Currency net.definition: The use of a standardized medium of exchange, backed by social trust.

EXCHANGE|Currency network.name: Currency network
EXCHANGE|Currency network.definition: The use of a standardized medium of exchange.
EXCHANGE|Currency network.condition: The use of a standardized medium of exchange, backed by social trust.

EXCHANGE|Debt incur.name: Debt incur
EXCHANGE|Debt incur.definition: Receiving now with a promise to give later. The "I'll pay you back."
EXCHANGE|Debt incur.condition: Receiving now with a promise to give later; "I'll pay you back."

EXCHANGE|Debt repay.condition: Fulfilling an obligation; "I pay you back."

EXCHANGE|Exchange rate.name: Exchange rate
EXCHANGE|Exchange rate.definition: The ratio at which one currency can be exchanged for another.
EXCHANGE|Exchange rate.condition: The ratio at which one currency can be exchanged for another.

EXCHANGE|Gift.name: Gift
EXCHANGE|Gift.definition: Giving without expectation of immediate return. The "present."
EXCHANGE|Gift.condition: Giving without expectation of immediate return; the "present."

EXCHANGE|Gift economy.name: Gift economy
EXCHANGE|Gift economy.definition: A system of exchange based on gifts, where status is gained by giving.
EXCHANGE|Gift economy.condition: A system of exchange based on gifts; status is gained by giving.

EXCHANGE|Insurance.name: Insurance
EXCHANGE|Insurance.definition: Exchanging a small, certain payment now for protection against a large, uncertain loss later.
EXCHANGE|Insurance.condition: Exchanging a small, certain payment now for protection against a large, uncertain loss later.

EXCHANGE|Liquidity.name: Liquidity
EXCHANGE|Liquidity.definition: The ease with which a resource can be exchanged for currency.
EXCHANGE|Liquidity.condition: The ease with which a resource can be exchanged for currency.

EXCHANGE|Market economy.name: Market economy
EXCHANGE|Market economy.definition: A system of exchange based on prices, supply, and demand.
EXCHANGE|Market economy.condition: A system of exchange based on prices, supply, and demand.

EXCHANGE|Marketplace.name: Marketplace
EXCHANGE|Marketplace.definition: A structured venue for exchange. The "agora."
EXCHANGE|Marketplace.condition: A structured venue for exchange; the "agora."

EXCHANGE|Mutual aid.name: Mutual aid
EXCHANGE|Mutual aid.definition: Exchange based on mutual support. The "I help you, you help me."
EXCHANGE|Mutual aid.condition: Exchange based on mutual support; "I help you, you help me."

EXCHANGE|Mutual credit.condition: A system where community members extend credit to each other, settled periodically.

EXCHANGE|Negotiate.name: Negotiate

EXCHANGE|Negotiation frame.condition: The structured process of reaching a deal through offer and counteroffer.

EXCHANGE|Sell.name: Sell
EXCHANGE|Sell.definition: Giving a resource in exchange for currency. The "sale."
EXCHANGE|Sell.condition: Giving a resource in exchange for currency; a sale.

EXCHANGE|Social capital.name: Social capital

EXCHANGE|Social capital.condition: The value embedded in social relationships, which facilitates exchange.

EXCHANGE|The circulation.name: The circulation

EXCHANGE|The circulation.condition: The continuous circulation of resources through a society.

EXCHANGE|The debtor.name: The debtor

EXCHANGE|The debtor.condition: The archetype of the one who owes; the burden and hope of repayment.

EXCHANGE|The economic network.name: The economic network
EXCHANGE|The economic network.definition: The complete network of exchanges that constitutes an economy.
EXCHANGE|The economic network.condition: The complete network of exchanges that constitutes an economy.
