HABIT|Emotional habit.condition: An emotional state triggers a habitual coping mechanism.

HABIT|Environment cue.name: Environment cue
HABIT|Environment cue.definition: The environment itself becomes a trigger for habitual action.
HABIT|Environment cue.condition: The environment itself becomes a trigger for habitual action.

HABIT|Habit hierarchy.name: Habit hierarchy
HABIT|Habit hierarchy.definition: Multiple habits compete for control. Higher-order habits override lower-order ones.
HABIT|Habit hierarchy.condition: Multiple habits compete for control; higher‑order habits override lower‑order ones.

HABIT|Habit stack.name: Habit stack
HABIT|Habit stack.definition: Chaining multiple habits together. One habit triggers the next.
HABIT|Habit stack.condition: Chaining multiple habits together; one habit triggers the next.

HABIT|Inertia cont.name: Inertia cont
HABIT|Inertia cont.definition: The tendency to continue an action simply because it has been started.

HABIT|Kehring.name: Kehring
HABIT|Kehring.definition: A sequence of habits where the reward of one becomes the cue for the next.
HABIT|Kehring.condition: A sequence of habits where the reward of one becomes the cue for the next.

HABIT|Loop.name: Loop
HABIT|Loop.definition: The fundamental habit unit. A stimulus triggers an action that yields a reward.
HABIT|Loop.condition: A stimulus triggers an action that yields a reward; the fundamental habit unit.

HABIT|Novelty override.name: Novelty override
HABIT|Novelty override.definition: A new, stronger reward disrupts an established habit.
HABIT|Novelty override.condition: A new, stronger reward disrupts an established habit.

HABIT|Pattern lock.name: Pattern lock
HABIT|Pattern lock.definition: An agent becomes predictable because of its fixed behavioral patterns.
HABIT|Pattern lock.condition: An agent becomes predictable because of its fixed behavioural patterns.

HABIT|Procedural mem.name: Procedural mem
HABIT|Procedural mem.definition: The body remembers how to perform an action without conscious effort.

HABIT|Procedural memory.name: Procedural memory
HABIT|Procedural memory.definition: The body remembers how to perform an action without conscious effort.
HABIT|Procedural memory.condition: The body remembers how to perform an action without conscious effort.

HABIT|Recovery loop.name: Recovery loop
HABIT|Recovery loop.definition: The process of re-establishing a habit after it has been disrupted.
HABIT|Recovery loop.condition: The process of re‑establishing a habit after it has been disrupted.

HABIT|Reinforce.name: Reinforce
HABIT|Reinforce.definition: The strengthening of a habit through repeated reward.
HABIT|Reinforce.condition: The strengthening of a habit through repeated reward; probability of action increases.

HABIT|Replace.name: Replace
HABIT|Replace.definition: Substituting a new behavior for an old one in response to the same cue.
HABIT|Replace.condition: Substituting a new behaviour for an old one in response to the same cue.

HABIT|Sabotage loop.name: Sabotage loop
HABIT|Sabotage loop.definition: A self-perpetuating loop of procrastination or addiction.
HABIT|Sabotage loop.condition: A self‑perpetuating loop of procrastination or addiction.

HABIT|Social habit.name: Social habit
HABIT|Social habit.definition: A habit that is reinforced by group norms and expectations.
HABIT|Social habit.condition: A habit that is reinforced by group norms and expectations.

HABIT|Stimulus gen.name: Stimulus gen
HABIT|Stimulus gen.definition: A stimulus similar to the original cue triggers the same habit.

HABIT|Stimulus generalisation.name: Stimulus generalisation
HABIT|Stimulus generalisation.definition: A stimulus similar to the original cue triggers the same habit.
HABIT|Stimulus generalisation.condition: A stimulus similar to the original cue triggers the same habit.

HABIT|The adaptive habit.name: The adaptive habit
HABIT|The adaptive habit.definition: A habit that is flexible and adapts to changing conditions.
HABIT|The adaptive habit.condition: A habit that is flexible and adapts to changing conditions.

HABIT|The addictive loop.name: The addictive loop
HABIT|The addictive loop.definition: A habit that is self-reinforcing to the point of pathological repetition.
HABIT|The addictive loop.condition: A habit that is self‑reinforcing to the point of pathological repetition.

HABIT|The architect of habit.name: The architect of habit
HABIT|The architect of habit.definition: Character is the architect of habit. You build your character through the habits you choose to cultivate.
HABIT|The architect of habit.condition: Character is the architect of habit; you build your character through the habits you choose to cultivate.

HABIT|The automatic pilot.name: The automatic pilot
HABIT|The automatic pilot.definition: The state of acting entirely on autopilot. No conscious thought.
HABIT|The automatic pilot.condition: The state of acting entirely on autopilot; no conscious thought.

HABIT|The groove.name: The groove
HABIT|The groove.definition: A habit so smooth and efficient that it feels like a groove. The "in the zone" of habit.
HABIT|The groove.condition: A habit so smooth and efficient that it feels like a groove; "in the zone."

HABIT|The groove carver.name: The groove carver
HABIT|The groove carver.definition: The conscious cultivation of a habit. The carving of the groove.
HABIT|The groove carver.condition: The conscious cultivation of a habit; the carving of the groove.

HABIT|The habit weave.name: The habit weave
HABIT|The habit weave.definition: The complete, interconnected web of habits that constitutes a life.
HABIT|The habit weave.condition: The complete, interconnected web of habits that constitutes a life.

HABIT|The habitual universe.name: The habitual universe
HABIT|The habitual universe.definition: The universe is a play of recurring patterns. Habit is the fundamental structure of behavior.
HABIT|The habitual universe.condition: The universe is a play of recurring patterns; habit is the fundamental structure of behaviour.

HABIT|The inertial self.name: The inertial self
HABIT|The inertial self.definition: The self is the sum of its habits. You are what you repeatedly do.
HABIT|The inertial self.condition: The self is the sum of its habits; you are what you repeatedly do.

HABIT|The meta habit.name: The meta habit
HABIT|The meta habit.definition: The habit of reflecting on one's own habits. The capacity for self-change.

HABIT|The ritual.name: The ritual
HABIT|The ritual.definition: A highly structured, repeated pattern of behavior that carries symbolic weight.
HABIT|The ritual.condition: A highly structured, repeated pattern of behaviour that carries symbolic weight.

HABIT|The self correcting.name: The self correcting
HABIT|The self correcting.definition: A habit that includes a feedback loop and the capacity for correction.

HABIT|The unconscious actor.name: The unconscious actor
HABIT|The unconscious actor.definition: The agent who acts without conscious awareness. The automaton.
HABIT|The unconscious actor.condition: The agent who acts without conscious awareness; the automaton.

HABIT|Thought habit.name: Thought habit
HABIT|Thought habit.definition: A habitual pattern of thinking. A cognitive loop.
HABIT|Thought habit.condition: A habitual pattern of thinking; a cognitive loop.

HABIT|Trigger net.name: Trigger net
HABIT|Trigger net.definition: A network of triggers that all activate the same habit.
HABIT|Trigger net.condition: A network of triggers that all activate the same habit.

HEAT|Bimetallic strip.name: Bimetallic strip
HEAT|Bimetallic strip.definition: two materials curl at different rates
HEAT|Bimetallic strip.condition: Different expansion coefficients cause the strip to curl when heated; curvature is a measure of temperature.

HEAT|Boil.name: Boil
HEAT|Boil.condition: At boiling point, liquid becomes gas throughout the volume; vapour pressure equals external pressure.

HEAT|Condense.name: Condense
HEAT|Condense.condition: At the condensation point, gas becomes liquid; latent heat is released.

HEAT|Conduction.name: Conduction
HEAT|Conduction.definition: heat crosses to an adjacent cold thing
HEAT|Conduction.condition: Heat flows from hot to cold across a material; rate = k·A·ΔT/d.

HEAT|Convection.name: Convection
HEAT|Convection.condition: Hot fluid rises (lower density), cold fluid sinks; circulation loop forms.

HEAT|Efficiency limit.name: Efficiency limit
HEAT|Efficiency limit.definition: the best any cycle can do
HEAT|Efficiency limit.condition: Carnot efficiency = 1 – T_c/T_h; no real engine exceeds this.

HEAT|Entropy field.name: Entropy field
HEAT|Entropy field.definition: disorder spreads and does not reverse
HEAT|Entropy field.condition: Entropy increases in any spontaneous heat transfer; can be measured as ∫δQ/T.

HEAT|Expand.name: Expand
HEAT|Expand.condition: Volume increases as temperature increases (for most materials); ΔV = α V₀ ΔT.

HEAT|Expansion joint.name: Expansion joint
HEAT|Expansion joint.definition: a part that lengthens when heated
HEAT|Expansion joint.condition: A joint allows segments to expand/contract without buckling; gap size changes with temperature.

HEAT|Freeze.name: Freeze
HEAT|Freeze.condition: At the freezing point, liquid becomes solid; latent heat is released without temperature change.

HEAT|Friction removal.name: Friction removal
HEAT|Friction removal.definition: freeze a surface, sliding gets easier
HEAT|Friction removal.condition: Freezing a surface (making it icy) reduces friction, making sliding easier.

HEAT|Heat engine.name: Heat engine
HEAT|Heat engine.condition: Gas expands (does work) at high temperature, contracts (requires work) at low temperature; net work output per cycle.

HEAT|Heat pipe.name: Heat pipe
HEAT|Heat pipe.condition: Heat evaporates fluid at one end; vapour travels to the other end, condenses, and returns via wick (capillary action).

HEAT|Ignite.name: Ignite
HEAT|Ignite.definition: past a point, the reaction feeds itself
HEAT|Ignite.condition: Temperature exceeds ignition point; self‑sustaining exothermic reaction begins.

HEAT|Latent store.name: Latent store
HEAT|Latent store.definition: store energy in a phase, release it later
HEAT|Latent store.condition: Energy is stored/retrieved during a phase change at constant temperature; e.g., ice packs, phase‑change thermal batteries.

HEAT|Melt.name: Melt
HEAT|Melt.condition: At the melting point, solid becomes liquid; latent heat is absorbed without temperature change.

HEAT|Opaque plume.name: Opaque plume
HEAT|Opaque plume.condition: Sublimation produces a dense, opaque vapour that hides what is behind it.

HEAT|Phase counter.name: Phase counter
HEAT|Phase counter.condition: The material cycles through four phase transitions in a repeatable sequence.

HEAT|Quench.name: Quench
HEAT|Quench.definition: cool fast enough to stop it
HEAT|Quench.condition: Cooling the material below ignition point stops the combustion reaction.

HEAT|Refrigerator.name: Refrigerator
HEAT|Refrigerator.condition: Reverse heat engine: work input moves heat from cold to hot reservoir; uses latent heat for cooling.

HEAT|Rising current.name: Rising current
HEAT|Rising current.definition: an upward flow that carries things
HEAT|Rising current.condition: A plume of warm air rises, carrying particles/heat with it; can be detected and used.

HEAT|Steam pressure.name: Steam pressure
HEAT|Steam pressure.condition: Water boils in a sealed container; pressure builds as vapour occupies the volume.

HEAT|Sublimate.name: Sublimate
HEAT|Sublimate.condition: Solid becomes gas directly without passing through liquid; occurs below triple point.

HEAT|Thermal shock.name: Thermal shock
HEAT|Thermal shock.condition: Very rapid heating/cooling causes differential expansion, leading to cracks in brittle materials.

HUMAN|Abstract.name: Abstract
HUMAN|Abstract.definition: map the relational skeleton, not the surface
HUMAN|Abstract.condition: The relational structure (not surface features) is mapped from source to target and applied successfully.

HUMAN|Abut.name: Abut
HUMAN|Abut.definition: two meet and both persist; the boundary is still readable
HUMAN|Abut.condition: Two objects are in contact but both persist; their boundary is still detectable.

HUMAN|Adapt.name: Adapt
HUMAN|Adapt.definition: track errors, ignore the regular ones
HUMAN|Adapt.condition: Large prediction errors are tracked; small, regular errors are ignored (habituated).

HUMAN|Amalgamate.name: Amalgamate
HUMAN|Amalgamate.condition: Two objects come into contact and become a single object; their boundaries merge.

HUMAN|Anchor.name: Anchor
HUMAN|Anchor.definition: fix a base so the centre of mass stays over it
HUMAN|Anchor.condition: COM is within the base's support area; structure is stable.

HUMAN|Associate.name: Associate
HUMAN|Associate.definition: link events because one precedes the other
HUMAN|Associate.condition: Event A consistently precedes event B; intervening on A changes B.

HUMAN|Avoid.name: Avoid
HUMAN|Avoid.condition: Agent predicts a collision if it continues on current path; it changes path to avoid the predicted collision point.

HUMAN|Ballistics.name: Ballistics
HUMAN|Ballistics.condition: Given initial conditions, the trajectory is computed; impact point is predicted.

HUMAN|Bind.name: Bind
HUMAN|Bind.condition: Features are grouped by Gestalt rules (proximity, similarity, common fate); they move as a single bounded unit.

HUMAN|Calibrate.name: Calibrate
HUMAN|Calibrate.definition: place on a scale, adjust to the middle
HUMAN|Calibrate.condition: Measurements are placed on a scale; values are adjusted to centre on a target or norm.

HUMAN|Camouflage.name: Camouflage
HUMAN|Camouflage.condition: Object's colour matches the background; segmenter cannot distinguish object from surround.

HUMAN|Cascade.name: Cascade
HUMAN|Cascade.definition: trigger a chain of a few linked events
HUMAN|Cascade.condition: A small trigger initiates a chain of a few (≤4) linked events, each causing the next.

HUMAN|Chunk.name: Chunk
HUMAN|Chunk.definition: a repeating sequence becomes one unit
HUMAN|Chunk.condition: A repeated subsequence is perceived as a single unit; transitional probabilities within chunk are higher than across boundaries.

HUMAN|Collide.name: Collide
HUMAN|Collide.definition: a struck thing moves; an unstruck one does not
HUMAN|Collide.condition: Two objects overlap in space; after overlap, their velocities change (one struck moves, the other stays or changes).

HUMAN|Compensate.name: Compensate
HUMAN|Compensate.condition: Agent applies a counter‑force to exactly cancel a disturbing force, maintaining stillness.

HUMAN|Conflate.name: Conflate
HUMAN|Conflate.definition: admit two things under one heading that should have been two
HUMAN|Conflate.condition: Agent files two distinct items under the same heading, causing confusion; the filter was set incorrectly.

HUMAN|Confound.name: Confound
HUMAN|Confound.definition: introduce a spurious cause to mislead
HUMAN|Confound.condition: Agent introduces a spurious cause to make it difficult to distinguish the real cause from the false one.

HUMAN|Construct.name: Construct
HUMAN|Construct.definition: an object appears where there was none
HUMAN|Construct.condition: A new object appears on the board where none was before; it is composed of previously absent parts.

HUMAN|Contain.name: Contain
HUMAN|Contain.definition: a thing is held inside a boundary
HUMAN|Contain.condition: The point (object) lies inside the boundary of the container; cannot escape without crossing boundary.

HUMAN|Curate.name: Curate
HUMAN|Curate.definition: admit what falls inside a moving threshold
HUMAN|Curate.condition: Items that fall within a moving, calibrated threshold are admitted; others are rejected.

HUMAN|Decompose.name: Decompose
HUMAN|Decompose.definition: break a goal into ordered parts
HUMAN|Decompose.condition: A goal is broken into ordered sub‑goals that, when executed in sequence, achieve the main goal.

HUMAN|Disambiguate.name: Disambiguate
HUMAN|Disambiguate.definition: separate correlation from cause by acting
HUMAN|Disambiguate.condition: Agent acts to separate correlation from causation; after intervention, only one causal link remains.

HUMAN|Disclose.name: Disclose
HUMAN|Disclose.condition: Agent performs an action that makes a previously hidden state observable to others.

HUMAN|Diverge.name: Diverge
HUMAN|Diverge.condition: While tracking several objects, one is flipped (mirrored) relative to the others.

HUMAN|Empathise.name: Empathise
HUMAN|Empathise.condition: Agent simulates the other's predicted goal and performs an action that helps achieve that goal.

HUMAN|Encapsulate.name: Encapsulate
HUMAN|Encapsulate.definition: group the inside, enforce the outside
HUMAN|Encapsulate.condition: The interior is grouped and protected; only specified interactions are allowed across the boundary.

HUMAN|Equilibrate.name: Equilibrate
HUMAN|Equilibrate.definition: find the force that reaches balance
HUMAN|Equilibrate.condition: System reaches a stable balance where net force is zero; after perturbation, it returns.

HUMAN|Erase.name: Erase
HUMAN|Erase.definition: an object is removed from the board
HUMAN|Erase.condition: An object disappears from the board after contact/consumption; it ceases to exist in the environment.

HUMAN|Extrapolate.name: Extrapolate
HUMAN|Extrapolate.definition: extend an arc past what is visible
HUMAN|Extrapolate.condition: The observed arc is extended past the visible region to predict where it will go.

HUMAN|Fall.name: Fall
HUMAN|Fall.condition: No support points underneath; vertical acceleration is positive (downward) and velocity increases downward.

HUMAN|Filter.name: Filter
HUMAN|Filter.condition: Some objects/particles cross the boundary while others are blocked, based on a property (e.g., size).

HUMAN|Hypothesise.name: Hypothesise
HUMAN|Hypothesise.condition: Agent generates multiple explanatory models and selects the best one based on analogies to known structures.

HUMAN|Imitate.name: Imitate
HUMAN|Imitate.definition: predict a consequence, then perform it
HUMAN|Imitate.condition: Agent predicts the sensory consequence of the observed action, then performs a matching action that produces the same consequence.

HUMAN|Improvise.name: Improvise
HUMAN|Improvise.condition: In a novel situation, the agent stops searching and adopts a good‑enough solution, adapting on the fly.

HUMAN|Infer intent.name: Infer intent
HUMAN|Infer intent.definition: read the designer's purpose from the layout
HUMAN|Infer intent.condition: Agent sees a designed layout and infers the purpose/goal of the designer from the relational structure.

HUMAN|Intervene.name: Intervene
HUMAN|Intervene.definition: act on a thing to test what it does
HUMAN|Intervene.condition: Agent acts on an object and observes that the object changes in a way consistent with a causal link.

HUMAN|Invert.name: Invert
HUMAN|Invert.condition: Handedness (e.g., left‑handed vs right‑handed) is reversed after reflection.

HUMAN|Layer.name: Layer
HUMAN|Layer.definition: one sits over the other; what is underneath persists, is partly readable, and changes what the top does
HUMAN|Layer.condition: One object sits over another; the bottom is partly readable and influences the top's behaviour (e.g., colour blending).

HUMAN|Measure.name: Measure
HUMAN|Measure.definition: assign a magnitude to a spatial feature
HUMAN|Measure.condition: A number is assigned to a spatial property (length, area, angle) using a standard unit.

HUMAN|Merge.name: Merge
HUMAN|Merge.definition: two meet and the seam is gone; neither is recoverable
HUMAN|Merge.condition: Two objects combine and their boundary disappears; neither can be recovered.

HUMAN|Misdirect.name: Misdirect
HUMAN|Misdirect.definition: attend to a decoy, act on the target
HUMAN|Misdirect.condition: Agent uses a false premise and directs its gaze to make the target attend to a decoy while acting elsewhere.

HUMAN|Navigate.name: Navigate
HUMAN|Navigate.definition: use edges and angles to find a route
HUMAN|Navigate.condition: The agent follows a path that respects edges and angles; route avoids obstacles.

HUMAN|Optimise.name: Optimise
HUMAN|Optimise.condition: Agent balances actions with known high rewards and actions that gather information about unknown rewards.

HUMAN|Orbit.name: Orbit
HUMAN|Orbit.definition: move around a pivot while facing it
HUMAN|Orbit.condition: Object moves around a pivot while continuously facing it (tangential velocity; radial acceleration).

HUMAN|Pass through.name: Pass through
HUMAN|Pass through.condition: Object crosses from one side of an opening to the other without interruption; path is continuous.

HUMAN|Phantom.name: Phantom
HUMAN|Phantom.definition: an object your model holds and the world does not
HUMAN|Phantom.condition: The agent's model holds an object that is not present in the world; agent acts as if it is there.

HUMAN|Predict.name: Predict
HUMAN|Predict.definition: infer the next state from the last
HUMAN|Predict.condition: The most likely next state is inferred from statistical regularities; prediction error is small.

HUMAN|Proprioceive.name: Proprioceive
HUMAN|Proprioceive.definition: model a body you cannot see
HUMAN|Proprioceive.condition: Agent can model the position of its own body parts even when they are not visible, using internal simulation.

HUMAN|Recolour.name: Recolour
HUMAN|Recolour.condition: Color changes but object identity (ID) remains the same.

HUMAN|Recurse.name: Recurse
HUMAN|Recurse.definition: apply the same solution inside itself
HUMAN|Recurse.condition: The solution to a problem involves applying the same procedure to its sub‑parts.

HUMAN|Reflect.name: Reflect
HUMAN|Reflect.definition: an object flips to its mirror
HUMAN|Reflect.condition: Applying a mirror transform yields an enantiomer; handedness flips.

HUMAN|Reify.name: Reify
HUMAN|Reify.definition: treat a rule as a thing you can act on
HUMAN|Reify.condition: The agent treats an abstract rule as a concrete object that can be manipulated (e.g., a law can be changed).

HUMAN|Resonate.name: Resonate
HUMAN|Resonate.definition: oscillate in time with something else
HUMAN|Resonate.condition: Two oscillators have the same frequency and constant phase difference; energy transfer amplifies response.

HUMAN|Rotate.name: Rotate
HUMAN|Rotate.definition: an object turns about a centre
HUMAN|Rotate.condition: Object turns about its centre; all parts maintain relative positions; rotation angle changes continuously.

HUMAN|Sacrifice.name: Sacrifice
HUMAN|Sacrifice.definition: give something up to see the structure
HUMAN|Sacrifice.condition: Agent gives up a resource or action to gain structural information about the problem.

HUMAN|Schematise.name: Schematise
HUMAN|Schematise.definition: treat a cluster as one thing
HUMAN|Schematise.condition: A set of features or events is grouped into a single mental unit or schema.

HUMAN|Separate.name: Separate
HUMAN|Separate.definition: one object becomes the several it was made of
HUMAN|Separate.condition: A single object splits into its constituent parts; cohesion between parts is broken.

HUMAN|Stack.name: Stack
HUMAN|Stack.condition: Objects are arranged vertically; each object's bottom face contacts the top face of the one below; COM is over the contact area.

HUMAN|Track.name: Track
HUMAN|Track.definition: hold several moving things at once
HUMAN|Track.condition: For ≤4 objects, each is tracked individually; trajectories are maintained.

HUMAN|Trajectory.name: Trajectory
HUMAN|Trajectory.definition: track the paths of a few moving things
HUMAN|Trajectory.condition: For a small number of moving objects (≤4), their paths are tracked exactly; for more, approximate with bounds.

HUMAN|Transfigure.name: Transfigure
HUMAN|Transfigure.condition: An object changes its category but leaves a detectable signature of the change.

HUMAN|Translate.name: Translate
HUMAN|Translate.definition: a whole object moves along a path
HUMAN|Translate.condition: All parts move together with same velocity; path is continuous (no teleportation).

HUMAN|Uncamouflage.name: Uncamouflage
HUMAN|Uncamouflage.condition: Object's colour becomes distinct from background; segmenter can separate it.

HUMAN|Wayfind.name: Wayfind
HUMAN|Wayfind.condition: Agent integrates motion between landmarks and resets its position estimate when a landmark is recognised.

INFORMATION|Array.name: Array
INFORMATION|Array.condition: Elements are stored contiguously; access by index is O(1).

INFORMATION|Attention.name: Attention
INFORMATION|Attention.definition: weight what matters in a sequence
INFORMATION|Attention.condition: A mechanism that weights parts of the input sequence differently; focuses on the most relevant parts.

INFORMATION|Binary search.name: Binary search
INFORMATION|Binary search.condition: Search space is halved each step; complexity O(log n).

INFORMATION|Breadth and depth first.name: Breadth and depth first
INFORMATION|Breadth and depth first.definition: two ways to walk a graph
INFORMATION|Breadth and depth first.condition: BFS explores all neighbours first; DFS explores one branch fully before backtracking.

INFORMATION|Byte.name: Byte
INFORMATION|Byte.condition: A group of 8 bits forms a byte; can represent 256 distinct values.

INFORMATION|Checksum.name: Checksum
INFORMATION|Checksum.definition: a small digest that detects change
INFORMATION|Checksum.condition: A hash of the data is recomputed and compared to a stored checksum; a mismatch indicates change.

INFORMATION|Complexity class.name: Complexity class
INFORMATION|Complexity class.condition: Runtime grows as a specific function of input size (e.g., O(n²), O(log n)).

INFORMATION|Decision tree.name: Decision tree
INFORMATION|Decision tree.condition: A tree splits data based on features; each leaf assigns a class; prediction is a series of decisions.

INFORMATION|Encoding.name: Encoding
INFORMATION|Encoding.condition: A transformation reversible with the key; without the key, it is hard to decode.

INFORMATION|Evolved solution.name: Evolved solution
INFORMATION|Evolved solution.condition: A population of candidate solutions evolves over generations; fitness improves.

INFORMATION|Graph.name: Graph
INFORMATION|Graph.condition: Nodes connected by arbitrary edges; may contain cycles.

INFORMATION|Greedy.name: Greedy
INFORMATION|Greedy.condition: At each step, choose the locally optimal option; may or may not yield global optimum.

INFORMATION|Heuristic.name: Heuristic
INFORMATION|Heuristic.definition: a rule that is usually good enough
INFORMATION|Heuristic.condition: A rule that works well most of the time, but is not guaranteed optimal; adaptable.

INFORMATION|Interface.name: Interface
INFORMATION|Interface.condition: A clearly defined set of inputs/outputs; both sides adhere to the contract.

INFORMATION|Irreducibility.name: Irreducibility
INFORMATION|Irreducibility.definition: some things must be run to be known
INFORMATION|Irreducibility.condition: Some processes cannot be sped up; you must run the simulation to know the outcome.

INFORMATION|Layered network.name: Layered network
INFORMATION|Layered network.condition: A multi‑layer graph; weights are adjusted to minimise output error.

INFORMATION|Linked list.name: Linked list
INFORMATION|Linked list.condition: Each node contains data and a pointer to the next node; traversal follows pointers.

INFORMATION|Map.name: Map
INFORMATION|Map.condition: Keys are hashed to indices; values are stored in an array at that index.

INFORMATION|Memoisation.name: Memoisation
INFORMATION|Memoisation.definition: never solve the same subproblem twice
INFORMATION|Memoisation.condition: Results of expensive function calls are stored; reused when the same arguments appear again.

INFORMATION|Metadata.name: Metadata
INFORMATION|Metadata.condition: Information that describes the data (e.g., author, creation date, schema).

INFORMATION|Ontology.name: Ontology
INFORMATION|Ontology.condition: A formal representation of knowledge as a graph of concepts with defined relations.

INFORMATION|Protocol.name: Protocol
INFORMATION|Protocol.condition: A set of rules governing exchange; both parties follow state transitions.

INFORMATION|Prove without revealing.name: Prove without revealing
INFORMATION|Prove without revealing.definition: show you know it without saying it
INFORMATION|Prove without revealing.condition: Zero‑knowledge proof: you convince someone you know a secret without revealing it.

INFORMATION|Queue.name: Queue
INFORMATION|Queue.condition: First‑in, first‑out; element removed is the one that has been waiting longest.

INFORMATION|Recursion.name: Recursion
INFORMATION|Recursion.condition: A function calls itself; uses a stack to track calls; terminates at base case.

INFORMATION|Reward learning.name: Reward learning
INFORMATION|Reward learning.condition: Agent learns a policy that maximises cumulative reward (e.g., Q‑learning).

INFORMATION|Shortest description.name: Shortest description
INFORMATION|Shortest description.definition: the least you could say and still specify it
INFORMATION|Shortest description.condition: The shortest program that outputs the object; Kolmogorov complexity.

INFORMATION|Shortest path.name: Shortest path
INFORMATION|Shortest path.condition: The path with the minimum total cost (e.g., Dijkstra) is found.

INFORMATION|Sorting.name: Sorting
INFORMATION|Sorting.condition: The output list is non‑decreasing according to the comparator.

INFORMATION|Stack.name: Stack
INFORMATION|Stack.condition: Last‑in, first‑out; element removed is the most recently added.

INFORMATION|Symbol system.name: Symbol system
INFORMATION|Symbol system.condition: A set of symbols with combinatorial rules that generate structured, meaningful expressions.

INFORMATION|Tree.name: Tree
INFORMATION|Tree.condition: A node has zero or more children; each child has one parent; no cycles.

KINETIC|Brachiate.name: Brachiate

KINETIC|Brachiate.condition: Hand‑to‑hand swinging under branches; pendular energy exchange; grasp and release.

KINETIC|Burrow.name: Burrow

KINETIC|Burrow.condition: Moves through a solid (soil/sand) by displacing it and creating a tunnel behind.

KINETIC|Chaos step.name: Chaos step
KINETIC|Chaos step.condition: Alternates unpredictably between fleeing, tumbling, and dashing to break opponent tracking.

KINETIC|Corkscrew.name: Corkscrew
KINETIC|Corkscrew.definition: rotate about the forward axis while airborne
KINETIC|Corkscrew.condition: Rotates about its forward axis while airborne; combines tumbling with forward flight.

KINETIC|Crawl.name: Crawl
KINETIC|Crawl.definition: many low contact points; slow, stable, low
KINETIC|Crawl.condition: Multiple low‑lying contacts (e.g., 4 limbs); low COM; slow speed; high stability.

KINETIC|Dash.name: Dash
KINETIC|Dash.definition: brief extreme acceleration; crosses a gap at once
KINETIC|Dash.condition: Brief, extreme acceleration; covers a gap in a short time; then recovers.

KINETIC|Drift.name: Drift
KINETIC|Drift.condition: Moves sideways while facing forward; powered by gravity or current; minimal input.

KINETIC|Energy recovery.name: Energy recovery
KINETIC|Energy recovery.definition: capture energy on landing, spend it on the next push
KINETIC|Energy recovery.condition: Captures elastic energy on landing and releases it on the next take‑off (like a spring).

KINETIC|Evade.name: Evade
KINETIC|Evade.definition: break another's lock by combining all three
KINETIC|Evade.condition: Combines dashes, chaotic changes, and mimicry to break the opponent's prediction lock.

KINETIC|Flee.name: Flee
KINETIC|Flee.definition: fast with erratic changes to break another's prediction
KINETIC|Flee.condition: Fast running with erratic, unpredictable changes in direction to break prediction.

KINETIC|Fly.name: Fly
KINETIC|Fly.condition: In air; lift > weight; thrust > drag; requires continuous energy expenditure.

KINETIC|Glide.name: Glide
KINETIC|Glide.definition: descend shallowly; trade height for distance
KINETIC|Glide.condition: Forward momentum provides lift; descends slowly; no active propulsion.

KINETIC|Hop.name: Hop
KINETIC|Hop.definition: one ballistic leap on elastic recoil
KINETIC|Hop.condition: Vertical take‑off; spring‑like limb stores and releases energy; ballistic arc; gravity returns.

KINETIC|Hover.name: Hover
KINETIC|Hover.definition: thrust exactly cancels gravity; no horizontal motion
KINETIC|Hover.condition: Thrust exactly balances weight; vertical velocity ≈ 0; no horizontal motion.

KINETIC|Mimic gait.name: Mimic gait
KINETIC|Mimic gait.condition: Copies the exact movement pattern of another, matching joint angles and timing.

KINETIC|Omnidirectional.name: Omnidirectional
KINETIC|Omnidirectional.definition: equal speed in every direction; no turn radius
KINETIC|Omnidirectional.condition: Can move with equal speed in any direction without turning; no turn radius.

KINETIC|Optimal locomotion.condition: Chooses the cheapest gait for the current terrain (e.g., walk on flat, swim in water).

KINETIC|Pendular swing.name: Pendular swing
KINETIC|Pendular swing.definition: time swings to the natural frequency; amplify cheaply
KINETIC|Pendular swing.condition: Swings at the resonant frequency of the arm/body; amplifies motion with minimal energy.

KINETIC|Planing.name: Planing
KINETIC|Planing.definition: forward momentum generating lift in a liquid
KINETIC|Planing.condition: Forward momentum generates dynamic lift in water; skims just below the surface.

KINETIC|Pogo.name: Pogo
KINETIC|Pogo.condition: Repeated rhythmic bouncing using spring‑like legs; minimal ground contact time per hop.

KINETIC|Pursuit.name: Pursuit

KINETIC|Pursuit.condition: Moves to intercept a moving target's future position, not its current position (lead the target).

KINETIC|Roll.name: Roll

KINETIC|Roll.condition: Body rotates about a moving axis; continuous contact with ground; angular momentum conserved.

KINETIC|Run.name: Run
KINETIC|Run.definition: an airborne phase; faster, costlier, ballistic
KINETIC|Run.condition: Both feet lose contact simultaneously (airborne phase); speed > walking threshold; ballistic.

KINETIC|Scale.name: Scale
KINETIC|Scale.definition: ascend a vertical surface on alternating holds
KINETIC|Scale.condition: Ascends a vertical surface; uses alternating hand/foot holds; traction prevents slipping.

KINETIC|Scurry.condition: Fast, multi‑legged crawling; many contact points ensure high stability at speed.

KINETIC|Skim.name: Skim
KINETIC|Skim.definition: just above a liquid, on a cushion of compressed air
KINETIC|Skim.condition: Just above a liquid surface; compressed air or hydrodynamic lift prevents immersion.

KINETIC|Slide.name: Slide
KINETIC|Slide.condition: Moves without active propulsion; friction is negligible; momentum carries it.

KINETIC|Slipstream.name: Slipstream
KINETIC|Slipstream.definition: move behind another and use its wake
KINETIC|Slipstream.condition: Moves directly behind another object, using its wake to reduce drag and conserve energy.

KINETIC|Slither.name: Slither
KINETIC|Slither.condition: Side‑to‑side body waves; pushes against surface friction; no limbs.

KINETIC|Soar.name: Soar
KINETIC|Soar.condition: Gains altitude without flapping by riding thermal updrafts; energy expenditure near zero.

KINETIC|Stalk.name: Stalk

KINETIC|Stalk.condition: Very slow walk; body colour/texture matches background; minimises detection.

KINETIC|Swim.name: Swim
KINETIC|Swim.condition: In water; buoyancy offsets gravity; propulsion via limb/body undulations.

KINETIC|Terrain skate.condition: Uses downward slopes to maintain speed without active propulsion; friction is minimal.

KINETIC|Tread.definition: hold a vertical position in a liquid
KINETIC|Tread.condition: Maintains a fixed vertical position in water; limb movements counter gravity/buoyancy.

KINETIC|Tumble.name: Tumble

KINETIC|Wade.condition: Feet on ground; body partially submerged; moves by walking against water resistance.

KINETIC|Wall jump.condition: Pushes off a vertical wall to gain both height and lateral speed; rebound.

LARGE-SCALE|Attraction.name: Attraction
LARGE-SCALE|Attraction.condition: F = G m₁m₂/r²; force is attractive and obeys inverse‑square law.

LARGE-SCALE|Bound system.name: Bound system
LARGE-SCALE|Bound system.condition: A group of bodies held together by mutual gravity; total energy is negative.

LARGE-SCALE|Boundary encoding.name: Boundary encoding
LARGE-SCALE|Boundary encoding.definition: the contents describable from the edge
LARGE-SCALE|Boundary encoding.condition: The entropy of a black hole is proportional to its horizon area (Bekenstein–Hawking).

LARGE-SCALE|Collapsed mass.name: Collapsed mass
LARGE-SCALE|Collapsed mass.condition: The object's radius is less than its Schwarzschild radius; r_s = 2GM/c².

LARGE-SCALE|Degenerate mass.name: Degenerate mass
LARGE-SCALE|Degenerate mass.condition: Gravity compresses matter to the point where degeneracy pressure (Pauli exclusion) balances it (white dwarfs, neutron stars).

LARGE-SCALE|Differential clocks.name: Differential clocks
LARGE-SCALE|Differential clocks.definition: time runs differently in different places
LARGE-SCALE|Differential clocks.condition: Clocks at different gravitational potentials run at different rates (gravitational time dilation).

LARGE-SCALE|Dragged region.name: Dragged region
LARGE-SCALE|Dragged region.condition: The region outside the event horizon where spacetime is dragged; particles cannot remain stationary.

LARGE-SCALE|Dragging.name: Dragging
LARGE-SCALE|Dragging.definition: a turning mass drags its surroundings
LARGE-SCALE|Dragging.condition: A rotating massive body drags spacetime around it (Lense‑Thirring effect).

LARGE-SCALE|Escape threshold.name: Escape threshold
LARGE-SCALE|Escape threshold.condition: Escape velocity = √(2GM/R); if v_escape ≥ c, nothing escapes (black hole).

LARGE-SCALE|Expansion.name: Expansion
LARGE-SCALE|Expansion.condition: Distances between far‑away objects increase over time; v = H₀·d.

LARGE-SCALE|Infall disc.name: Infall disc
LARGE-SCALE|Infall disc.definition: a spiral of things falling in
LARGE-SCALE|Infall disc.condition: Matter spirals into the collapsed mass; forms a disc; heats up and emits radiation.

LARGE-SCALE|Missing mass.name: Missing mass
LARGE-SCALE|Missing mass.condition: The gravitational attraction exceeds that expected from visible matter; indicates dark matter.

LARGE-SCALE|Orbit.name: Orbit
LARGE-SCALE|Orbit.condition: Object moves around a pivot while continuously facing it (tangential velocity; radial acceleration).

LARGE-SCALE|Path bending.name: Path bending
LARGE-SCALE|Path bending.condition: Light paths are bent by mass (gravitational lensing); deflection angle ∝ M.

LARGE-SCALE|Rapid early expansion.name: Rapid early expansion
LARGE-SCALE|Rapid early expansion.definition: a brief period of very fast growth
LARGE-SCALE|Rapid early expansion.condition: In the very early universe, expansion was exponential (inflation); scale factor grew extremely fast.

LARGE-SCALE|Remnant radiation.name: Remnant radiation
LARGE-SCALE|Remnant radiation.condition: A leftover signal from the early universe; cosmic microwave background radiation with T ≈ 2.7 K.

LARGE-SCALE|Ripples.name: Ripples
LARGE-SCALE|Ripples.condition: Accelerating masses produce ripples in spacetime; detected as strain (LIGO).

LARGE-SCALE|Signal delay.name: Signal delay
LARGE-SCALE|Signal delay.condition: Signal (light/gravity) takes finite time to travel; delay = distance / c.

LARGE-SCALE|Slow evaporation.name: Slow evaporation
LARGE-SCALE|Slow evaporation.condition: Black holes emit radiation (Hawking) and slowly lose mass; rate ∝ 1/M².

LARGE-SCALE|Tidal stretching.name: Tidal stretching
LARGE-SCALE|Tidal stretching.condition: The difference in gravitational pull across the object stretches it; near a black hole.
