LINEAGE|The heritage self.condition: The self defined by its lineage; "I am of the line."

LINEAGE|The heritage witness.name: The heritage witness
LINEAGE|The heritage witness.definition: The one who witnesses and preserves the heritage. The "keeper of the line."
LINEAGE|The heritage witness.condition: The one who witnesses and preserves the heritage; the "keeper of the line."

LINEAGE|The legacy drive.name: The legacy drive
LINEAGE|The legacy drive.definition: The drive to leave a legacy. The "desire for immortality through the line."
LINEAGE|The legacy drive.condition: The drive to leave a legacy; the "desire for immortality through the line."

LINEAGE|The lineage universe.name: The lineage universe
LINEAGE|The lineage universe.definition: The universe is a vast web of lineages. All things descend from something.
LINEAGE|The lineage universe.condition: The universe is a vast web of lineages; all things descend from something.

LINEAGE|The root foundation.name: The root foundation
LINEAGE|The root foundation.definition: The foundational root of a lineage. The "source of all descent."
LINEAGE|The root foundation.condition: The foundational root of a lineage; the "source of all descent."

LINEAGE|The seed carrier.name: The seed carrier
LINEAGE|The seed carrier.definition: The one who carries the seed of the future. The "guardian of the lineage."
LINEAGE|The seed carrier.condition: The one who carries the seed of the future; the "guardian of the lineage."

LINEAGE|The seed self.name: The seed self
LINEAGE|The seed self.definition: The self as a seed. The "potential becoming."
LINEAGE|The seed self.condition: The self as a seed; the "potential becoming."

LINEAGE|The world tree.name: The world tree
LINEAGE|The world tree.definition: The universe as a single, vast, interconnected tree of lineage.
LINEAGE|The world tree.condition: The universe as a single, vast, interconnected tree of lineage.

LINEAGE|Trace.name: Trace
LINEAGE|Trace.definition: The act of tracing a lineage. The "genealogical search."
LINEAGE|Trace.condition: The act of tracing a lineage; the "genealogical search."

LINGUISTIC|Ambiguity.name: Ambiguity
LINGUISTIC|Ambiguity.definition: A sentence with more than one possible meaning. "I saw the man with the telescope."
LINGUISTIC|Ambiguity.condition: A sentence with more than one possible meaning (e.g., "I saw the man with the telescope").

LINGUISTIC|Conceptual metaphor.name: Conceptual metaphor
LINGUISTIC|Conceptual metaphor.definition: A systematic mapping between two domains that structures thought. Time is money. Argument is war.
LINGUISTIC|Conceptual metaphor.condition: A systematic mapping between two domains that structures thought (e.g., time is money, argument is war).

LINGUISTIC|Discourse.name: Discourse
LINGUISTIC|Discourse.definition: A connected series of utterances. A conversation, a speech, a text.
LINGUISTIC|Discourse.condition: A connected series of utterances; a conversation, a speech, a text.

LINGUISTIC|Discourse grammar.name: Discourse grammar
LINGUISTIC|Discourse grammar.definition: The rules governing how sentences connect to form coherent texts. Cohesion and coherence.
LINGUISTIC|Discourse grammar.condition: The rules governing how sentences connect to form coherent texts; cohesion and coherence.

LINGUISTIC|Discourse participation.name: Discourse participation
LINGUISTIC|Discourse participation.definition: The structure of conversation. Taking turns, responding, repairing misunderstandings.
LINGUISTIC|Discourse participation.condition: The structure of conversation; taking turns, responding, repairing misunderstandings.

LINGUISTIC|Framing.name: Framing
LINGUISTIC|Framing.definition: The context shapes the interpretation. The same event, framed differently, has different meaning.
LINGUISTIC|Framing.condition: The context shapes the interpretation; the same event, framed differently, has different meaning.

LINGUISTIC|Grammar.name: Grammar
LINGUISTIC|Grammar.definition: The complete system of structural rules that governs a language. The "code" of the language.
LINGUISTIC|Grammar.condition: The complete system of structural rules that governs a language; the "code" of the language.

LINGUISTIC|Homonymy.name: Homonymy
LINGUISTIC|Homonymy.definition: A word with multiple unrelated meanings. "Bat" (animal, sports equipment).
LINGUISTIC|Homonymy.condition: A word with multiple unrelated meanings (e.g., "bat" – animal, sports equipment).

LINGUISTIC|Interpretation.name: Interpretation
LINGUISTIC|Interpretation.definition: The process of deriving meaning from a text. The reader actively constructs meaning.
LINGUISTIC|Interpretation.condition: The process of deriving meaning from a text; the reader actively constructs meaning.

LINGUISTIC|Linguistic relativity.name: Linguistic relativity
LINGUISTIC|Linguistic relativity.definition: Language shapes thought. The structure of your language influences how you perceive reality.
LINGUISTIC|Linguistic relativity.condition: Language shapes thought; the structure of your language influences how you perceive reality.

LINGUISTIC|Metaphor grounding.name: Metaphor grounding
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor grounding.definition: Metaphors are grounded in embodied experience. Up = good; down = bad.
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor grounding.condition: Metaphors are grounded in embodied experience; up = good, down = bad.

LINGUISTIC|Metaphor network.name: Metaphor network
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor network.definition: All thought is metaphor. We understand the new in terms of the old.
LINGUISTIC|Metaphor network.condition: All thought is metaphor; we understand the new in terms of the old.

LINGUISTIC|Narrative arc.name: Narrative arc
LINGUISTIC|Narrative arc.definition: The emotional trajectory of a story. Exposition → Rising Action → Climax → Falling Action → Resolution.
LINGUISTIC|Narrative arc.condition: The emotional trajectory of a story; exposition → rising action → climax → falling action → resolution.

LINGUISTIC|Poetic function.name: Poetic function
LINGUISTIC|Poetic function.definition: Language is used for its own sake. Poetry, wordplay, rhythm, and beauty.
LINGUISTIC|Poetic function.condition: Language is used for its own sake; poetry, wordplay, rhythm, and beauty.

LINGUISTIC|Polysemy.name: Polysemy
LINGUISTIC|Polysemy.definition: A word with multiple related meanings. "Bank" (river bank, financial bank).
LINGUISTIC|Polysemy.condition: A word with multiple related meanings (e.g., "bank" – river bank, financial bank).

LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic contract.name: Pragmatic contract
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic contract.definition: Communication is governed by implicit social contracts. The cooperative principle (Grice).
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic contract.condition: Communication is governed by implicit social contracts; the cooperative principle (Grice).

LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic frame.name: Pragmatic frame
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic frame.definition: The inferred intention behind an utterance. What the speaker *actually* means.
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic frame.condition: The inferred intention behind an utterance; what the speaker actually means.

LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic inference.name: Pragmatic inference
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic inference.definition: The listener infers meaning beyond the literal. "Can you pass the salt?" is a request, not a question.
LINGUISTIC|Pragmatic inference.condition: The listener infers meaning beyond the literal (e.g., "Can you pass the salt?" is a request).

LINGUISTIC|Reference.name: Reference
LINGUISTIC|Reference.definition: The relationship between a symbol and the object/event it points to. The act of naming.
LINGUISTIC|Reference.condition: The relationship between a symbol and the object/event it points to; the act of naming.

LINGUISTIC|Register.name: Register
LINGUISTIC|Register.definition: A variety of language used in a specific context (formal, informal, technical, poetic).
LINGUISTIC|Register.condition: A variety of language used in a specific context (formal, informal, technical, poetic).

LINGUISTIC|Semantic field.name: Semantic field
LINGUISTIC|Semantic field.definition: A set of related meanings. The domain of "family" words (mother, father, sibling).
LINGUISTIC|Semantic field.condition: A set of related meanings; the domain of "family" words (mother, father, sibling).

LINGUISTIC|Sentence.name: Sentence
LINGUISTIC|Sentence.definition: A structured sequence of words that expresses a complete thought. The unit of propositional meaning.
LINGUISTIC|Sentence.condition: A structured sequence of words that expresses a complete thought; has a propositional meaning.

LINGUISTIC|Speech act.name: Speech act
LINGUISTIC|Speech act.definition: An utterance that performs an action. "I promise," "I apologize," "I baptize."
LINGUISTIC|Speech act.condition: An utterance that performs an action (e.g., "I promise," "I apologize," "I baptize").

LINGUISTIC|Story.name: Story
LINGUISTIC|Story.definition: A structured narrative. A sequence of events connected by causality and meaning.
LINGUISTIC|Story.condition: A structured narrative; a sequence of events connected by causality and meaning, with a beginning, middle, end.

LINGUISTIC|Symbol.name: Symbol
LINGUISTIC|Symbol.definition: An arbitrary sign that carries shared meaning within a community. A flag, a word, a gesture.
LINGUISTIC|Symbol.condition: An arbitrary sign carries shared meaning within a community; a flag, a word, a gesture.

LINGUISTIC|Textual world.name: Textual world
LINGUISTIC|Textual world.definition: A text creates a world in the reader's mind. The reader builds the world from the text.
LINGUISTIC|Textual world.condition: A text creates a world in the reader's mind; the reader builds the world from the text.

LINGUISTIC|The interpretive community.name: The interpretive community
LINGUISTIC|The interpretive community.definition: Meaning is not private; it is negotiated within a community of interpreters.
LINGUISTIC|The interpretive community.condition: Meaning is not private; it is negotiated within a community of interpreters.

LINGUISTIC|The linguistic universe.name: The linguistic universe
LINGUISTIC|The linguistic universe.definition: The universe is not just a collection of objects; it is a *text* that can be read, interpreted, and narrated.
LINGUISTIC|The linguistic universe.condition: The universe is not just a collection of objects; it is a text that can be read, interpreted, and narrated.

LINGUISTIC|The narrative mind.name: The narrative mind
LINGUISTIC|The narrative mind.definition: The self is a narrative construct. We tell ourselves stories about who we are.
LINGUISTIC|The narrative mind.condition: The self is a narrative construct; we tell ourselves stories about who we are.

LINGUISTIC|The semantic web.name: The semantic web
LINGUISTIC|The semantic web.definition: The complete network of all meanings, linked by associations, categories, and metaphors.
LINGUISTIC|The semantic web.condition: The complete network of all meanings, linked by associations, categories, and metaphors.

LINGUISTIC|The significant order.name: The significant order
LINGUISTIC|The significant order.definition: Meaning arises from differences within a system. A sign has meaning because of what it is not.
LINGUISTIC|The significant order.condition: Meaning arises from differences within a system; a sign has meaning because of what it is not.

LINGUISTIC|The storyteller.name: The storyteller
LINGUISTIC|The storyteller.definition: The agent who weaves events into a meaningful narrative. The author of the self.
LINGUISTIC|The storyteller.condition: The agent who weaves events into a meaningful narrative; the author of the self.

LINGUISTIC|Utterance.name: Utterance
LINGUISTIC|Utterance.definition: A sentence spoken in a specific context with a specific intention. The unit of communicative action.
LINGUISTIC|Utterance.condition: A sentence spoken in a specific context with a specific intention; the unit of communicative action.

LINGUISTIC|Word.name: Word
LINGUISTIC|Word.definition: A unit of meaning. A symbol that points to a concept. The building block of language.
LINGUISTIC|Word.condition: A unit of meaning exists; a symbol (sound/mark) points to a concept; identifiable by the community.

LIVING|Adaptation.name: Adaptation
LIVING|Adaptation.definition: a population comes to fit its surroundings
LIVING|Adaptation.condition: Population's traits shift to better fit the environment; fitness increases.

LIVING|Carrying capacity.name: Carrying capacity
LIVING|Carrying capacity.condition: Population growth levels off as resources become limiting; reaches K.

LIVING|Cellular automaton.name: Cellular automaton
LIVING|Cellular automaton.condition: Local rules (division, differentiation) produce a global, repeating spatial pattern (like a lattice).

LIVING|Chemical light.name: Chemical light
LIVING|Chemical light.condition: Chemical energy is converted to light without heat; enzyme catalyses the reaction.

LIVING|Contractile tissue.name: Contractile tissue
LIVING|Contractile tissue.condition: Cells specialised to shorten; use ATP; produce force.

LIVING|Copying.name: Copying
LIVING|Copying.condition: A DNA molecule is copied exactly, producing an identical sequence.

LIVING|Decomposer.name: Decomposer
LIVING|Decomposer.condition: Breaks down organic matter anaerobically; releases nutrients; reproduces by spores.

LIVING|Differentiation.name: Differentiation
LIVING|Differentiation.definition: a general cell becomes a specific one
LIVING|Differentiation.condition: A general cell becomes a specific cell type (e.g., neuron, muscle) through gene activation.

LIVING|Divergence.name: Divergence
LIVING|Divergence.condition: Isolated populations diverge genetically; they no longer interbreed.

LIVING|Division.name: Division
LIVING|Division.condition: One cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.

LIVING|Ecosystem.name: Ecosystem
LIVING|Ecosystem.condition: A self‑sustaining community with energy capture, consumption, decomposition, and nutrient cycling.

LIVING|Editing.name: Editing
LIVING|Editing.definition: change a sequence at a chosen place
LIVING|Editing.condition: A specific sequence is cut and modified; resulting sequence is altered at the targeted site.

LIVING|Energy capture.name: Energy capture
LIVING|Energy capture.condition: Light energy is converted to chemical energy (ATP, glucose); O₂ is released.

LIVING|Environmental expression.name: Environmental expression
LIVING|Environmental expression.condition: The same genotype produces different phenotypes depending on environmental conditions (e.g., temperature‑dependent sex).

LIVING|Fermentation.name: Fermentation
LIVING|Fermentation.condition: Glucose is broken down anaerobically; produces ATP and organic by‑products.

LIVING|Gene transfer.name: Gene transfer
LIVING|Gene transfer.condition: Genetic material is transferred horizontally between organisms via a vector.

LIVING|Grafting.name: Grafting
LIVING|Grafting.definition: move a part into another whole
LIVING|Grafting.condition: Tissue from one organism is transplanted to another and integrates functionally.

LIVING|Immune memory.name: Immune memory
LIVING|Immune memory.condition: On second exposure to the same pathogen, response is faster and stronger.

LIVING|Interface.name: Interface
LIVING|Interface.condition: A neural signal is converted to an electrical signal that a computer can process.

LIVING|Mutual benefit.name: Mutual benefit
LIVING|Mutual benefit.condition: Both species gain from the interaction (e.g., pollination).

LIVING|Neutral association.name: Neutral association
LIVING|Neutral association.definition: one gains, the other is unaffected
LIVING|Neutral association.condition: One species is unaffected by the interaction with the other.

LIVING|Osmosis.name: Osmosis
LIVING|Osmosis.condition: Water moves across a semi‑permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration.

LIVING|Parasitism.name: Parasitism
LIVING|Parasitism.condition: One species (parasite) benefits at the expense of the host; host is harmed.

LIVING|Predator.name: Predator
LIVING|Predator.condition: Consumes other organisms; has high metabolism; moves to find prey.

LIVING|Prey.name: Prey
LIVING|Prey.condition: Is consumed; has senses to detect predators; can flee or hide.

LIVING|Producer.name: Producer
LIVING|Producer.definition: makes its own energy, stays put
LIVING|Producer.condition: Makes its own energy from light; stays in one place; has support structures.

LIVING|Recombination.name: Recombination
LIVING|Recombination.condition: Offspring receives genetic material from two parents; recombination occurs.

LIVING|Respiration.name: Respiration
LIVING|Respiration.condition: Glucose is oxidised with oxygen to produce ATP, CO₂, and water.

LIVING|Selection over generations.name: Selection over generations
LIVING|Selection over generations.condition: Some variants reproduce more than others; trait frequencies change over generations.

LIVING|Signalling tissue.name: Signalling tissue
LIVING|Signalling tissue.condition: Cells specialised to transmit electrical signals (action potentials) and communicate chemically.

LIVING|Structural tissue.name: Structural tissue
LIVING|Structural tissue.condition: Cells produce a matrix that provides mechanical support and resistance to compression/tension.

LIVING|Transport fluid.name: Transport fluid
LIVING|Transport fluid.condition: Fluid (blood) carries oxygen and nutrients; driven by metabolic energy.

LOGISTICAL|Agile supply.name: Agile supply
LOGISTICAL|Agile supply.definition: A supply chain that can rapidly reconfigure in response to changing demand.
LOGISTICAL|Agile supply.condition: A supply chain that can rapidly reconfigure in response to changing demand.

LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck analysis.name: Bottleneck analysis
LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck analysis.definition: Find the exact point of constriction. Increase capacity there to increase total flow.
LOGISTICAL|Bottleneck analysis.condition: The exact point of constriction is identified; increasing capacity there increases total flow.

LOGISTICAL|Bulk transport.name: Bulk transport
LOGISTICAL|Bulk transport.definition: Move many resources at once. Reduces cost per unit but increases latency.
LOGISTICAL|Bulk transport.condition: Many resources are moved together; reduces cost per unit but increases latency.

LOGISTICAL|Capacity.name: Capacity
LOGISTICAL|Capacity.definition: The maximum flow that an edge can carry. Exceed it; congestion occurs.
LOGISTICAL|Capacity.condition: Current flow ≤ maximum capacity; if exceeded, congestion occurs.

LOGISTICAL|Choke point.name: Choke point
LOGISTICAL|Choke point.definition: A single edge that limits the flow of the entire network. The weakest link.
LOGISTICAL|Choke point.condition: A single edge limits the flow of the entire network; the weakest link.

LOGISTICAL|Conveyor belt.name: Conveyor belt
LOGISTICAL|Conveyor belt.definition: A continuous, automated mover. Resources flow at a fixed rate.
LOGISTICAL|Conveyor belt.condition: A continuous, automated mover; resources flow at a fixed rate.

LOGISTICAL|Cyclic routing.name: Cyclic routing
LOGISTICAL|Cyclic routing.definition: Resources flow in a loop. Return of empty containers, recycling, reverse logistics.
LOGISTICAL|Cyclic routing.condition: Resources flow in a loop; return of empty containers, recycling, reverse logistics.

LOGISTICAL|Dispatching.name: Dispatching
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching.definition: Decide which resource goes to which process, and when. Centralized control.
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching.condition: A centralised decision on which resource goes to which process and when.

LOGISTICAL|Dispatching AI.name: Dispatching AI
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching AI.definition: A central intelligence that manages the entire flow, learning and adapting over time.
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching AI.condition: A central intelligence manages the entire flow, learning and adapting over time.

LOGISTICAL|Dispatching system.name: Dispatching system
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching system.definition: A central AI that allocates resources to tasks in real-time, using predictive models.
LOGISTICAL|Dispatching system.condition: A central AI allocates resources to tasks in real‑time, using predictive models.

LOGISTICAL|Expedite.name: Expedite
LOGISTICAL|Expedite.definition: Accelerate a specific resource through the network, bypassing queues.
LOGISTICAL|Expedite.condition: A specific resource is accelerated through the network, bypassing queues.

LOGISTICAL|FIFO.name: FIFO
LOGISTICAL|FIFO.definition: First-In, First-Out. The default queuing discipline.
LOGISTICAL|FIFO.condition: The item that arrived first is served first; order is preserved.

LOGISTICAL|Inventory optimisation.name: Inventory optimisation
LOGISTICAL|Inventory optimisation.condition: The economic order quantity (EOQ) model; balance ordering and holding costs.

LOGISTICAL|Inventory optimization.name: Inventory optimization
LOGISTICAL|Inventory optimization.definition: The economic order quantity (EOQ) model. Balance ordering and holding costs.

LOGISTICAL|Just in case.name: Just in case
LOGISTICAL|Just in case.definition: The opposite of Just-In-Time. Keep large buffers to absorb uncertainty.

LOGISTICAL|Just in time.name: Just in time
LOGISTICAL|Just in time.definition: Resources arrive exactly when needed. No inventory. High risk, high efficiency.

LOGISTICAL|Lead time.name: Lead time
LOGISTICAL|Lead time.definition: The time between initiating a process and its completion. Latency in the supply chain.
LOGISTICAL|Lead time.condition: The time between initiating a process and its completion; latency in the supply chain.

LOGISTICAL|Lean logistics.name: Lean logistics
LOGISTICAL|Lean logistics.definition: Eliminate all forms of waste (motion, waiting, overproduction, defects). Continuous improvement.
LOGISTICAL|Lean logistics.condition: Eliminate all forms of waste (motion, waiting, overproduction, defects); continuous improvement.

LOGISTICAL|Logistical harmony.name: Logistical harmony
LOGISTICAL|Logistical harmony.definition: A perfectly synchronized system. No waiting, no congestion, no waste. Pure flow.
LOGISTICAL|Logistical harmony.condition: A perfectly synchronised system; no waiting, no congestion, no waste.

LOGISTICAL|Lot sizing.name: Lot sizing
LOGISTICAL|Lot sizing.definition: Determine the optimal batch size to minimize total cost (ordering + holding).
LOGISTICAL|Lot sizing.condition: The optimal batch size minimises total cost (ordering + holding) – economic order quantity.

LOGISTICAL|Max flow.name: Max flow
LOGISTICAL|Max flow.definition: Maximize the flow from source to sink given edge capacities. Ford-Fulkerson.
LOGISTICAL|Max flow.condition: The flow from source to sink is maximised subject to capacity constraints (Ford‑Fulkerson).

LOGISTICAL|Min cut.name: Min cut
LOGISTICAL|Min cut.definition: The smallest set of edges that disconnects source from sink. The *exact* bottleneck.
LOGISTICAL|Min cut.condition: The smallest set of edges that disconnects source from sink; capacity of cut = max flow.

LOGISTICAL|Network design.name: Network design
LOGISTICAL|Network design.definition: Design a network to meet demand at minimum cost. Facility location problem.
LOGISTICAL|Network design.condition: Design a network to meet demand at minimum cost; facility location problem.

LOGISTICAL|Priority q.name: Priority q
LOGISTICAL|Priority q.definition: Higher-priority resources are served before lower-priority ones, regardless of arrival time.

LOGISTICAL|Priority queue.name: Priority queue
LOGISTICAL|Priority queue.condition: Items with higher priority are served before lower‑priority items, regardless of arrival time.

LOGISTICAL|Queue formation.name: Queue formation
LOGISTICAL|Queue formation.definition: Resources arrive faster than they are served; a queue builds.
LOGISTICAL|Queue formation.condition: Arrival rate > service rate; queue length increases over time.

LOGISTICAL|Queueing network.name: Queueing network
LOGISTICAL|Queueing network.definition: Multiple queues connected in series or parallel. The Jackson network.
LOGISTICAL|Queueing network.condition: Multiple queues connected in series or parallel; a Jackson network.

LOGISTICAL|Route.name: Route
LOGISTICAL|Route.definition: Find a path from source to destination. Connectivity is the first requirement.
LOGISTICAL|Route.condition: There exists a continuous path from source to sink; all edges are traversable.

LOGISTICAL|Routing protocol.name: Routing protocol
LOGISTICAL|Routing protocol.definition: A dynamic system that finds paths in real-time, adapting to congestion.
LOGISTICAL|Routing protocol.condition: A dynamic system that finds paths in real‑time, adapting to congestion and failures.

LOGISTICAL|Schedule task.name: Schedule task
LOGISTICAL|Schedule task.definition: Assign a resource to a task at a specific time. Timing is everything.
LOGISTICAL|Schedule task.condition: A task is assigned to a resource at a specific time; timing is fixed.

LOGISTICAL|Shortest path.name: Shortest path
LOGISTICAL|Shortest path.definition: Find the path with the minimum total cost (distance, time, or effort). Dijkstra's algorithm.
LOGISTICAL|Shortest path.condition: The path with the minimum total cost (distance, time, or effort) is found (e.g., Dijkstra).

LOGISTICAL|Supply chain map.name: Supply chain map
LOGISTICAL|Supply chain map.definition: The complete, end-to-end visualization of a resource's journey.
LOGISTICAL|Supply chain map.condition: The complete, end‑to‑end visualisation of a resource's journey.

LOGISTICAL|Supply chain resilience.name: Supply chain resilience
LOGISTICAL|Supply chain resilience.definition: A supply chain that can absorb shocks. Alternative routes, buffer stocks, flexible suppliers.
LOGISTICAL|Supply chain resilience.condition: A supply chain that can absorb shocks; has alternative routes, buffer stocks, flexible suppliers.

LOGISTICAL|The capacity equation.name: The capacity equation
LOGISTICAL|The capacity equation.definition: Throughput = (Inventory) / (Time in System). Little's Law. The fundamental equation of logistics.
LOGISTICAL|The capacity equation.condition: Throughput = Inventory / Time in System (Little's Law).

LOGISTICAL|The optimal network.name: The optimal network
LOGISTICAL|The optimal network.definition: The network that balances cost, speed, and reliability. A multi-objective optimization.
LOGISTICAL|The optimal network.condition: The network balances cost, speed, and reliability; a multi‑objective optimisation.

LOGISTICAL|The supply web.name: The supply web
LOGISTICAL|The supply web.definition: The entire, interconnected, self-regulating system of resource extraction, production, distribution, consumption, and disposal.
LOGISTICAL|The supply web.condition: The entire, interconnected, self‑regulating system of resource extraction, production, distribution, consumption, and disposal.

LOGISTICAL|Traffic congestion.name: Traffic congestion
LOGISTICAL|Traffic congestion.definition: Traffic jam. Resources accumulate, slowing everything down.
LOGISTICAL|Traffic congestion.condition: Flow exceeds capacity; speed drops; resources accumulate.

LOGISTICAL|Trans shipment.name: Trans shipment
LOGISTICAL|Trans shipment.definition: A resource passes through an intermediate node without being processed. A relay.

LOGISTICAL|Warehouse.name: Warehouse
LOGISTICAL|Warehouse.definition: A place to store inventory. Efficient retrieval is crucial.
LOGISTICAL|Warehouse.condition: A place to store inventory; efficient retrieval is optimised.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurd situation.name: Absurd situation
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurd situation.definition: A situation that defies logic and expectations. The "absurdist theater."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurd situation.condition: A situation that defies logic and expectations; the "absurdist theater."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurdist rebellion.name: Absurdist rebellion
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurdist rebellion.definition: The refusal to impose meaning on a meaningless universe. The "rebellion of the absurd."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Absurdist rebellion.condition: The refusal to impose meaning on a meaningless universe; the "rebellion of the absurd."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Belly laugh.name: Belly laugh
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Belly laugh.definition: A deep, full, unreserved laugh. The "release of tension."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Belly laugh.condition: A deep, full, unreserved laugh; the "release of tension."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Callback.name: Callback
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Callback.definition: Referencing an earlier joke. The "remember when?" moment that rewards attention.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Callback.condition: Referencing an earlier joke; the "remember when?" moment that rewards attention.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Caricature.name: Caricature
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Caricature.definition: Exaggerating the features of a target to ridicule them.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Caricature.condition: Exaggerating the features of a target to ridicule them.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic ritual.name: Comic ritual
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic ritual.definition: A shared, structured comedic experience. The "comedy night."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic ritual.condition: A shared, structured comedic experience; the "comedy night."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic timing.name: Comic timing
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic timing.definition: The precise timing that makes a joke land. The "pause" and the "delivery."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Comic timing.condition: The precise timing that makes a joke land; the "pause" and the "delivery."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Cosmic joke.name: Cosmic joke
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Cosmic joke.definition: The recognition that the universe itself is a joke. The punchline is that there is no punchline.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Cosmic joke.condition: The recognition that the universe itself is a joke; the punchline is that there is no punchline.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Deadpan.name: Deadpan
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Deadpan.definition: Delivering humor with a completely serious expression. The "straight face."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Deadpan.condition: Delivering humour with a completely serious expression; the "straight face."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Double take.name: Double take
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Double take.definition: The moment of recognizing an incongruity. The "wait, what?" moment.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Double take.condition: The moment of recognising an incongruity; the "wait, what?" moment.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Gallows humor.name: Gallows humor
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Gallows humor.definition: Humor in the face of death, tragedy, or extreme stress. The "dark laughter."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Gallows humor.condition: Humor in the face of death, tragedy, or extreme stress; the "dark laughter."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic detachment.name: Ironic detachment
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic detachment.definition: Maintaining a state of ironic detachment. The "I am amused by this, not invested."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic detachment.condition: Maintaining a state of ironic detachment; "I am amused by this, not invested."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic gap.name: Ironic gap
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic gap.definition: The gap between what is said and what is meant, or what is seen and what is true.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Ironic gap.condition: The gap between what is said and what is meant, or what is seen and what is true.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Joke architecture.name: Joke architecture
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Joke architecture.definition: The formal structure of a joke: setup, escalation, punchline, release.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Joke architecture.condition: The formal structure of a joke: setup, escalation, punchline, release.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter as meaning.name: Laughter as meaning
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter as meaning.definition: The recognition that laughter itself is the meaning. The "joyful absurdity."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter as meaning.condition: The recognition that laughter itself is the meaning; the "joyful absurdity."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter cascade.name: Laughter cascade
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter cascade.definition: The spread of laughter through a group. The "contagious giggle."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Laughter cascade.condition: The spread of laughter through a group; the "contagious giggle."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Parody.name: Parody
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Parody.definition: Mimicking a style or work to ridicule it. The "imitation that exposes."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Parody.condition: Mimicking a style or work to ridicule it; the "imitation that exposes."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Pratfall.name: Pratfall
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Pratfall.definition: A physical, exaggerated fall or mishap. The "slapstick."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Pratfall.condition: A physical, exaggerated fall or mishap; the "slapstick."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Quip.name: Quip
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Quip.definition: A quick, sharp, humorous response. The "bon mot."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Quip.condition: A quick, sharp, humorous response; the "bon mot."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Relieving laugh.name: Relieving laugh
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Relieving laugh.definition: Laughter as a release of built-up tension. The "comic relief."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Relieving laugh.condition: Laughter as a release of built‑up tension; the "comic relief."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical critique.name: Satirical critique
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical critique.definition: Using humor to expose the flaws of a system, person, or idea.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical critique.condition: Using humor to expose the flaws of a system, person, or idea.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical mirror.name: Satirical mirror
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical mirror.definition: Satire as a mirror that reflects the truth back to us.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Satirical mirror.condition: Satire as a mirror that reflects the truth back to us.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Setup punch.name: Setup punch
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Setup punch.definition: The classic structure of a joke: building an expectation, then subverting it.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Setup punch.condition: The classic structure of a joke: building an expectation, then subverting it.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Surreal humor.name: Surreal humor
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Surreal humor.definition: Humor derived from surreal, dream-like imagery. The "I have no idea what is happening."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Surreal humor.condition: Humor derived from surreal, dream‑like imagery; "I have no idea what is happening."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd answer.name: The absurd answer
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd answer.definition: The answer to an unanswerable question is a joke. The "cosmic punchline."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd answer.condition: The answer to an unanswerable question is a joke; the "cosmic punchline."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd hero.name: The absurd hero
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd hero.definition: The hero who acts without seeking meaning. The "Sisyphus smiling."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The absurd hero.condition: The hero who acts without seeking meaning; the "Sisyphus smiling."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The comic vision.name: The comic vision
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The comic vision.definition: Seeing the world through the lens of humor. The "comic perspective."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The comic vision.condition: Seeing the world through the lens of humour; the "comic perspective."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The community of laugh.name: The community of laughter
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The community of laugh.definition: Laughter as a social bond. The shared joke creates community.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The community of laugh.condition: Laughter as a social bond; the shared joke creates community.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The cosmic comedian.name: The cosmic comedian
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The cosmic comedian.definition: The one who sees the universe as a joke and laughs. The "divine comedian."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The cosmic comedian.condition: The one who sees the universe as a joke and laughs; the "divine comedian."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The internal comedian.name: The internal comedian
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The internal comedian.definition: The inner voice that sees the absurdity of one's own life. The "self-deprecating humor."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The internal comedian.condition: The inner voice that sees the absurdity of one's own life; the "self‑deprecating humor."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The ironist.name: The ironist
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The ironist.definition: The self defined by ironic detachment. The "I take nothing seriously."
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The ironist.condition: The self defined by ironic detachment; "I take nothing seriously."

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester.name: The jester
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester.definition: The archetype of the jester. The one who tells the truth through jokes.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester.condition: The archetype of the jester; the one who tells the truth through jokes.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester universe.name: The jester universe
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester universe.definition: The universe as a cosmic joke. The punchline is that there is no final answer.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The jester universe.condition: The universe as a cosmic joke; the punchline is that there is no final answer.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The laughing soul.name: The laughing soul
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The laughing soul.definition: The soul that is free because it can laugh at itself.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The laughing soul.condition: The soul that is free because it can laugh at itself.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The release engine.name: The release engine
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The release engine.definition: Laughter as a healing mechanism. The release of tension and stress.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|The release engine.condition: Laughter as a healing mechanism; the release of tension and stress.

LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wordplay.name: Wordplay
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wordplay.definition: Humor based on the playful use of language. Puns, malapropisms, double entendres.
LUDIC / ABSURDIST|Wordplay.condition: Humor based on the playful use of language; puns, malapropisms, double entendres.

LUDOLOGICAL|Baiting.name: Baiting
LUDOLOGICAL|Baiting.definition: Deliberately perform a suboptimal action to lure the opponent into a trap.
LUDOLOGICAL|Baiting.condition: Deliberately perform a suboptimal action to lure the opponent into a trap.

LUDOLOGICAL|Balance.name: Balance
LUDOLOGICAL|Balance.definition: No strategy is dominant. All viable strategies have roughly equal winning potential.
LUDOLOGICAL|Balance.condition: No strategy is dominant; all viable strategies have roughly equal winning potential.

LUDOLOGICAL|Counterplay.name: Counterplay
LUDOLOGICAL|Counterplay.definition: A strategy that is specifically designed to defeat another strategy. Rock-paper-scissors.
LUDOLOGICAL|Counterplay.condition: A strategy that is specifically designed to defeat another strategy; rock‑paper‑scissors.

LUDOLOGICAL|Dominance.name: Dominance
LUDOLOGICAL|Dominance.definition: One action is always better than another, regardless of the state.
LUDOLOGICAL|Dominance.condition: One action is always better than another, regardless of the state.

LUDOLOGICAL|Draw.name: Draw
LUDOLOGICAL|Draw.definition: Neither player achieves the objective. The game terminates in a tie.
LUDOLOGICAL|Draw.condition: Neither player achieves the objective; the game terminates in a tie.

LUDOLOGICAL|Exploit.name: Exploit
LUDOLOGICAL|Exploit.definition: A sequence of actions that leverages a rule interaction not intended by the designer. A "cheat" within the rules.
LUDOLOGICAL|Exploit.condition: A sequence of actions that leverages a rule interaction not intended by the designer; a "cheat" within the rules.

LUDOLOGICAL|Fixed point.name: Fixed point
LUDOLOGICAL|Fixed point.definition: A game state that is stable under the rules. An equilibrium.
LUDOLOGICAL|Fixed point.condition: A game state that is stable under the rules; an equilibrium (e.g., stalemate).

LUDOLOGICAL|Game death.name: Game death
LUDOLOGICAL|Game death.definition: The game ends permanently. There is no restart. Finality.
LUDOLOGICAL|Game death.condition: The game ends permanently; there is no restart.

LUDOLOGICAL|Game tree.name: Game tree
LUDOLOGICAL|Game tree.definition: The complete graph of all possible game states and moves. Exponential complexity.
LUDOLOGICAL|Game tree.condition: The complete graph of all possible game states and moves; exponential complexity.

LUDOLOGICAL|House rule.name: House rule
LUDOLOGICAL|House rule.definition: A rule variation adopted by a specific group. A local mutation.
LUDOLOGICAL|House rule.condition: A rule variation adopted by a specific group; a local mutation of the ruleset.

LUDOLOGICAL|Lose.name: Lose
LUDOLOGICAL|Lose.definition: Fail to achieve the objective. The game terminates. A negative outcome.
LUDOLOGICAL|Lose.condition: The objective is not achieved; the game terminates with a negative outcome.

LUDOLOGICAL|Ludic fallacy.name: Ludic fallacy
LUDOLOGICAL|Ludic fallacy.definition: The error of assuming that the game's rules accurately model reality. The map is not the territory.
LUDOLOGICAL|Ludic fallacy.condition: The error of assuming that the game's rules accurately model reality; the map is not the territory.

LUDOLOGICAL|Ludology onomy.name: Ludology onomy
LUDOLOGICAL|Ludology onomy.definition: The study of games as systems. The rules create a state space; the state space generates meaning.
LUDOLOGICAL|Ludology onomy.condition: The study of games as systems; the rules create a state space; the state space generates meaning.

LUDOLOGICAL|Meta game theory.name: Meta game theory
LUDOLOGICAL|Meta game theory.definition: The evolution of strategies over time. The metagame is a dynamic, evolving system.

LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame theory.name: Metagame theory
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame theory.definition: The evolution of strategies over time.
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagame theory.condition: The evolution of strategies over time; the metagame is a dynamic, evolving system.

LUDOLOGICAL|Metagaming.name: Metagaming
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagaming.definition: Choosing a strategy based not on the game state, but on what *other players* are choosing. The game about the game.
LUDOLOGICAL|Metagaming.condition: Choosing a strategy based not on the game state, but on what other players are choosing; the game about the game.

LUDOLOGICAL|Nash equilibrium.name: Nash equilibrium
LUDOLOGICAL|Nash equilibrium.definition: A set of strategies where no player can improve by unilaterally changing.
LUDOLOGICAL|Nash equilibrium.condition: A set of strategies where no player can improve by unilaterally changing; a stable equilibrium.

LUDOLOGICAL|Nash lud.name: Nash lud
LUDOLOGICAL|Nash lud.definition: A set of strategies where no player can improve by unilaterally changing. A stable equilibrium.

LUDOLOGICAL|Nonzero sum.name: Nonzero sum
LUDOLOGICAL|Nonzero sum.definition: Both players can gain (or lose) simultaneously. Potential for cooperation.
LUDOLOGICAL|Nonzero sum.condition: Both players can gain (or lose) simultaneously; potential for cooperation.

LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal control.name: Optimal control
LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal control.definition: The optimal sequence of actions over time, given a cost function. Control theory.
LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal control.condition: The optimal sequence of actions over time, given a cost function; control theory.

LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal play.name: Optimal play
LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal play.definition: Choose the action that maximizes expected utility, assuming perfect play.
LUDOLOGICAL|Optimal play.condition: Choose the action that maximises expected utility, assuming perfect play.

LUDOLOGICAL|Paradox.name: Paradox
LUDOLOGICAL|Paradox.definition: A situation where the rules lead to a contradiction. "This statement is false."
LUDOLOGICAL|Paradox.condition: A situation where the rules lead to a contradiction (e.g., "This statement is false").

LUDOLOGICAL|Play.name: Play
LUDOLOGICAL|Play.definition: Engage in the game. Perform an action within the magic circle.
LUDOLOGICAL|Play.condition: Engage in the game; perform an action within the magic circle (rules apply).

LUDOLOGICAL|Player experience.name: Player experience
LUDOLOGICAL|Player experience.definition: The subjective experience of the player. The game is not the rules; it is the *feeling* of playing.
LUDOLOGICAL|Player experience.condition: The subjective experience of the player; the game is not the rules, it is the feeling of playing.

LUDOLOGICAL|Procedural rhetoric.name: Procedural rhetoric
LUDOLOGICAL|Procedural rhetoric.definition: Games make arguments through their rules. The mechanics *say* something.
LUDOLOGICAL|Procedural rhetoric.condition: Games make arguments through their rules; the mechanics say something.

LUDOLOGICAL|Real time.name: Real time
LUDOLOGICAL|Real time.definition: Players act simultaneously and continuously. No turn boundaries.
LUDOLOGICAL|Real time.condition: Players act simultaneously and continuously; no turn boundaries.

LUDOLOGICAL|Ruleset.name: Ruleset
LUDOLOGICAL|Ruleset.definition: The complete set of rules that define the game. The game's "constitution."
LUDOLOGICAL|Ruleset.condition: The complete set of rules that define the game; the game's constitution.

LUDOLOGICAL|Score keep.name: Score keep
LUDOLOGICAL|Score keep.definition: Track performance over time. An ongoing measure of success.

LUDOLOGICAL|Score keeping.name: Score keeping
LUDOLOGICAL|Score keeping.condition: Track performance over time; score changes according to actions.

LUDOLOGICAL|Second order.name: Second order
LUDOLOGICAL|Second order.definition: Thinking about thinking about the game. The metagame of the metagame.
LUDOLOGICAL|Second order.condition: Thinking about thinking about the game; the metagame of the metagame.

LUDOLOGICAL|Serious play.name: Serious play
LUDOLOGICAL|Serious play.definition: Play that has real-world consequences. Not "just a game."
LUDOLOGICAL|Serious play.condition: Play that has real‑world consequences; not "just a game."

LUDOLOGICAL|Snowball.name: Snowball
LUDOLOGICAL|Snowball.definition: An early advantage accumulates over time. The rich get richer.
LUDOLOGICAL|Snowball.condition: An early advantage accumulates over time; the rich get richer.

LUDOLOGICAL|Strategy.name: Strategy
LUDOLOGICAL|Strategy.definition: A complete plan of action across all possible states. A mapping from states to actions.
LUDOLOGICAL|Strategy.condition: A complete plan of action across all possible states; a mapping from states to actions.

LUDOLOGICAL|Tactics.name: Tactics
LUDOLOGICAL|Tactics.definition: A short-term, situation-specific action plan. Responds to the immediate state.
LUDOLOGICAL|Tactics.condition: A short‑term, situation‑specific action plan; responds to the immediate state.

LUDOLOGICAL|Telegraph.name: Telegraph
LUDOLOGICAL|Telegraph.definition: An action that signals your future action. A "tell" that can be exploited.
LUDOLOGICAL|Telegraph.condition: An action that signals your future action; a "tell" that can be exploited.

LUDOLOGICAL|The fun theorem.name: The fun theorem
LUDOLOGICAL|The fun theorem.definition: Fun emerges when challenge matches skill. Too easy = boredom; too hard = anxiety.
LUDOLOGICAL|The fun theorem.condition: Fun emerges when challenge matches skill; too easy = boredom; too hard = anxiety.

LUDOLOGICAL|The game itself.name: The game itself
LUDOLOGICAL|The game itself.definition: The complete, self-contained system of the game. It exists as an abstract entity, independent of any particular playthrough.
LUDOLOGICAL|The game itself.condition: The complete, self‑contained system of the game; exists as an abstract entity, independent of any particular playthrough.

LUDOLOGICAL|The magic circle.name: The magic circle
LUDOLOGICAL|The magic circle.definition: The boundary that separates the game from the real world. Inside, the rules are binding. Outside, they are irrelevant.
LUDOLOGICAL|The magic circle.condition: The boundary that separates the game from the real world; inside, the rules are binding; outside, irrelevant.

LUDOLOGICAL|Tier list.name: Tier list
LUDOLOGICAL|Tier list.definition: A ranking of strategies/characters/abilities based on competitive viability. Social consensus.
LUDOLOGICAL|Tier list.condition: A ranking of strategies/characters/abilities based on competitive viability; social consensus.

LUDOLOGICAL|Turn based.name: Turn based
LUDOLOGICAL|Turn based.definition: Players act sequentially. One action per turn.

LUDOLOGICAL|Voluntary play.name: Voluntary play
LUDOLOGICAL|Voluntary play.definition: Play is voluntary. You can leave the magic circle at any time. The game only exists because players consent.
LUDOLOGICAL|Voluntary play.condition: Play is voluntary; you can leave the magic circle at any time.

LUDOLOGICAL|Win.name: Win
LUDOLOGICAL|Win.definition: Achieve the objective. The game terminates. A positive outcome.
LUDOLOGICAL|Win.condition: The objective is achieved; the game terminates with a positive outcome.

LUDOLOGICAL|Zero sum.name: Zero sum
LUDOLOGICAL|Zero sum.definition: One player's gain is exactly another player's loss. Pure competition.
LUDOLOGICAL|Zero sum.condition: One player's gain is exactly another player's loss; sum of payoffs = 0.

MATERIAL|Anneal.name: Anneal
MATERIAL|Anneal.definition: Heat the material to soften it, then cool slowly. Removes internal stresses, resets fatigue damage, makes it more ductile.
MATERIAL|Anneal.condition: Heating and slow cooling removes internal stresses; material becomes more ductile; fatigue damage reset.

MATERIAL|Bauschinger effect.name: Bauschinger effect
MATERIAL|Bauschinger effect.definition: After plastic deformation in one direction, the yield strength in the opposite direction is reduced. Hysteresis in material memory.
MATERIAL|Bauschinger effect.condition: After plastic deformation in one direction, the yield strength in the opposite direction is reduced.

MATERIAL|Brittle failure.name: Brittle failure
MATERIAL|Brittle failure.definition: A material with low fracture toughness shatters instantly with no plastic deformation (glass, ceramic).
MATERIAL|Brittle failure.condition: Material shows little or no plastic deformation; sudden fracture; smooth fracture surface.

MATERIAL|Buckling.name: Buckling
MATERIAL|Buckling.definition: A long, thin column (pencil) under compression suddenly bows sideways. It fails not by crushing, but by geometric instability.
MATERIAL|Buckling.condition: A long, thin column under compression bows sideways at the critical load; Euler buckling formula.

MATERIAL|Composite.name: Composite
MATERIAL|Composite.definition: Combine two materials (e.g., fiberglass, reinforced concrete). The composite has the hardness of one and the toughness of the other. Resists cracks.
MATERIAL|Composite.condition: Combining brittle and ductile materials yields a composite with hardness from one and toughness from the other.

MATERIAL|Corrosion.name: Corrosion
MATERIAL|Corrosion.definition: Chemical attack (rust) eats away the surface. Combined with stress, it leads to stress-corrosion cracking—premature failure at low loads.
MATERIAL|Corrosion.condition: Chemical attack eats away the surface; combined with stress, leads to premature failure.

MATERIAL|Crack propagation.name: Crack propagation
MATERIAL|Crack propagation.definition: A microscopic flaw (crack) concentrates stress at its tip. The crack grows uncontrollably if the material is brittle.
MATERIAL|Crack propagation.condition: A microscopic flaw concentrates stress; crack grows if stress intensity exceeds critical value.

MATERIAL|Creep deformation.name: Creep deformation
MATERIAL|Creep deformation.definition: Under sustained load, the material slowly flows. Over many frames, a shelf warps or a rope stretches.
MATERIAL|Creep deformation.condition: Under constant stress, strain increases over time; strain rate is constant in steady state.

MATERIAL|Damage mechanics.name: Damage mechanics
MATERIAL|Damage mechanics.definition: A unified framework for predicting the life of a structure under real-world loads. Accumulated damage D = Σ(nᵢ / Nᵢ). When D = 1, failure occurs (Miner's rule).
MATERIAL|Damage mechanics.condition: Accumulated damage D = Σ(nᵢ/Nᵢ); failure occurs when D = 1 (Miner's rule).

MATERIAL|Decohesion.name: Decohesion
MATERIAL|Decohesion.definition: Molecules are pulled apart at the atomic level. The material separates along grain boundaries. The ultimate limit of all materials.
MATERIAL|Decohesion.condition: Molecules are pulled apart at the atomic level; material separates along grain boundaries.

MATERIAL|Ductile failure.name: Ductile failure
MATERIAL|Ductile failure.definition: A material stretches, necks, and then tears slowly (metal, chewing gum). Warning signs before break.
MATERIAL|Ductile failure.condition: Material stretches, necks, and tears slowly; rough fracture surface; warning signs appear.

MATERIAL|Fatigue cycle.name: Fatigue cycle
MATERIAL|Fatigue cycle.definition: Repeated stress below the yield point gradually weakens the material. After N cycles, it breaks without warning.
MATERIAL|Fatigue cycle.condition: Repeated stress below yield causes failure after N cycles; S‑N curve is characteristic.

MATERIAL|Fatigue limit.name: Fatigue limit
MATERIAL|Fatigue limit.definition: Below a certain stress amplitude, some materials (steel) have an *infinite* fatigue life. Above it, they will eventually break after a predictable number of cycles.
MATERIAL|Fatigue limit.condition: Below a certain stress amplitude, some materials (steel) have an infinite fatigue life (endurance limit).

MATERIAL|Fracture mechanics.name: Fracture mechanics
MATERIAL|Fracture mechanics.definition: The stress intensity factor (K) at a crack tip. If K exceeds Kᵢc (critical fracture toughness), the crack runs and the part fails. This gives exact failure thresholds.
MATERIAL|Fracture mechanics.condition: If stress intensity factor K exceeds K_IC, crack runs and fails.

MATERIAL|Granular structure.name: Granular structure
MATERIAL|Granular structure.definition: The internal grain structure of polycrystalline materials. Grain boundaries are strong (resist slip) but can also be sites of weakness (intergranular fracture).
MATERIAL|Granular structure.condition: Polycrystalline structure; grain boundaries are strong but also sites of weakness.

MATERIAL|Hardness test.name: Hardness test
MATERIAL|Hardness test.definition: A hard object (e.g., diamond) scores a softer material. Used to compare material toughness.
MATERIAL|Hardness test.condition: Hardness = Load / Indentation Area; harder materials show smaller indentation.

MATERIAL|Hooke's law.name: Hooke's law
MATERIAL|Hooke's law.definition: Stress is proportional to strain; predictable, reversible deformation.
MATERIAL|Hooke's law.condition: Stress is proportional to strain; F = k·x; within elastic limit, linear relationship holds.

MATERIAL|Hookes law.name: Hookes law
MATERIAL|Hookes law.definition: Stress is proportional to strain (F = kx). The spring constant (k) defines stiffness. Predictable, reversible deformation.

MATERIAL|Hydrogen embrittlement.name: Hydrogen embrittlement
MATERIAL|Hydrogen embrittlement.definition: Small hydrogen atoms diffuse into the metal lattice, making it extremely brittle. A strong metal suddenly turns to glass.
MATERIAL|Hydrogen embrittlement.condition: Hydrogen diffuses into the lattice; fracture toughness is significantly lowered; sudden brittle failure.

MATERIAL|Impact damage.name: Impact damage
MATERIAL|Impact damage.definition: A sudden hammer blow. If below yield, it dents (plastic). If above, it shatters (fracture). Energy is absorbed by deformation or crack creation.
MATERIAL|Impact damage.condition: A sudden hammer blow causes localised plastic deformation if below yield, or fracture if above.

MATERIAL|Load path.name: Load path
MATERIAL|Load path.definition: Forces travel through a structure like water through a pipe. If the path is interrupted, stress redistributes and may overload a weaker member.
MATERIAL|Load path.condition: Forces travel through a structure like water through a pipe; if path is interrupted, stress redistributes.

MATERIAL|Metallurgical memory.name: Metallurgical memory
MATERIAL|Metallurgical memory.definition: The material "remembers" its deformation history. The internal dislocation network is a physical record of stress events.
MATERIAL|Metallurgical memory.condition: The material "remembers" its deformation history; internal dislocations are a physical record.

MATERIAL|Neutron irradiation.name: Neutron irradiation
MATERIAL|Neutron irradiation.definition: Exposure to radiation embrittles materials. They become hard and brittle over time (nuclear reactor pressure vessels).
MATERIAL|Neutron irradiation.condition: Exposure to radiation embrittles materials; hardness increases, ductility decreases.

MATERIAL|Perfect elasticity.name: Perfect elasticity
MATERIAL|Perfect elasticity.definition: An ideal material that never yields, never fatigues, and always returns to its original shape. Unattainable in reality—but a useful theoretical maximum.
MATERIAL|Perfect elasticity.condition: Material always returns to original shape; no fatigue; ideal theoretical maximum.

MATERIAL|Perfect plasticity.name: Perfect plasticity
MATERIAL|Perfect plasticity.definition: A material that deforms without any resistance once yield is exceeded. It flows like honey.
MATERIAL|Perfect plasticity.condition: Once yield is exceeded, material deforms without any resistance; flows like honey.

MATERIAL|Quench.name: Quench
MATERIAL|Quench.definition: Heat then rapidly cool (water/oil). Hardens the material but makes it more brittle. Trade-off.
MATERIAL|Quench.condition: Heating then rapid cooling (water/oil) increases hardness but increases brittleness.

MATERIAL|Residual stress.name: Residual stress
MATERIAL|Residual stress.definition: Stress locked inside the material after uneven cooling or plastic deformation. It can suddenly release (a spring that "snaps").
MATERIAL|Residual stress.condition: Stress is locked inside the material; it can suddenly release (e.g., a spring that snaps).

MATERIAL|Rupture.name: Rupture
MATERIAL|Rupture.definition: Stress exceeds ultimate tensile strength. The material breaks completely. Separation into two pieces.
MATERIAL|Rupture.condition: Stress exceeds ultimate tensile strength; the material separates into two pieces.

MATERIAL|Shear failure.name: Shear failure
MATERIAL|Shear failure.definition: Forces slide one layer of material against another. Rivets snap, glue peels, beams twist.
MATERIAL|Shear failure.condition: Forces slide one layer against another; rivets snap, glue peels, beams twist.

MATERIAL|Stress concentration.name: Stress concentration
MATERIAL|Stress concentration.definition: A sharp corner, notch, or hole multiplies the local stress. A 1x force becomes a 10x force at a crack tip.
MATERIAL|Stress concentration.condition: A sharp corner, notch, or hole multiplies local stress by a factor (Kt > 1).

MATERIAL|Stress strain curve.name: Stress strain curve
MATERIAL|Stress strain curve.definition: The full lifecycle of a material under load: elastic region → yield point → plastic region → ultimate strength → fracture. A visual graph of the material's "personality."

MATERIAL|Thermal fatigue.name: Thermal fatigue
MATERIAL|Thermal fatigue.definition: Repeated heating and cooling cause differential expansion. Cracks form due to thermal cycling.
MATERIAL|Thermal fatigue.condition: Repeated heating and cooling cause differential expansion; cracks form due to thermal cycling.

MATERIAL|Viscelasticity.name: Viscelasticity
MATERIAL|Viscelasticity.definition: A material that behaves like both a spring (elastic) and a dashpot (viscous). Memory foam, rubber bands at high speed.

MATERIAL|Viscoelasticity.name: Viscoelasticity
MATERIAL|Viscoelasticity.definition: Behaves like both a spring and a dashpot (memory foam, rubber bands).
MATERIAL|Viscoelasticity.condition: Material behaves like a spring and a dashpot; strain depends on history; hysteresis in loading‑unloading.

MATERIAL|Weld zone.name: Weld zone
MATERIAL|Weld zone.definition: Two separate pieces joined by melting and mixing. The weld zone has different properties—often weaker and more brittle.
MATERIAL|Weld zone.condition: Two pieces joined by melting; the weld zone has different (often weaker) properties.

MATERIAL|Work harden.name: Work harden
MATERIAL|Work harden.definition: Repeated plastic deformation (hammering) increases hardness but decreases ductility. The material becomes stiffer until it cracks.
MATERIAL|Work harden.condition: Repeated plastic deformation (hammering) increases hardness but decreases ductility; material becomes stiffer until it cracks.

MATERIAL|Yield.name: Yield
MATERIAL|Yield.definition: Stress exceeds yield strength. The material bends permanently. It does not spring back. Shape changes forever.
MATERIAL|Yield.condition: Stress exceeds yield strength; after unloading, strain remains > 0 (permanent set).

MECHANICAL|Accumulator.name: Accumulator
MECHANICAL|Accumulator.definition: collect until a threshold, then release

MECHANICAL|Balance beam.name: Balance beam
MECHANICAL|Balance beam.definition: equalise turning force on both sides
MECHANICAL|Balance beam.condition: Torques on both sides are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction; beam remains horizontal.

MECHANICAL|Centre of mass.name: Centre of mass
MECHANICAL|Centre of mass.definition: the average position of the weight

MECHANICAL|Chain reaction.name: Chain reaction

OPTICAL|Aberration.name: Aberration
OPTICAL|Aberration.definition: Optical imperfection. Chromatic (color fringes), spherical (blurred edges), coma (comet-shaped blur). The "flaw" of all lenses.
OPTICAL|Aberration.condition: Optical imperfection; chromatic (color fringes), spherical (blurred edges), coma (comet‑shaped blur).

OPTICAL|Adaptive optics.name: Adaptive optics
OPTICAL|Adaptive optics.definition: A deformable mirror that corrects for atmospheric distortion in real-time. Sharpens blurry images.
OPTICAL|Adaptive optics.condition: A deformable mirror is adjusted in real time to correct atmospheric distortion; images are sharpened.

OPTICAL|Beam split.name: Beam split
OPTICAL|Beam split.definition: A half-silvered mirror. It splits one beam into two: one reflected, one transmitted.
OPTICAL|Beam split.condition: Half‑silvered mirror; beam is split into two: one reflected, one transmitted; intensities sum to incident.

OPTICAL|Entangled photons.name: Entangled photons
OPTICAL|Entangled photons.definition: Split a high-energy photon into two entangled, lower-energy photons. Perfectly correlated.
OPTICAL|Entangled photons.condition: A high‑energy photon is split into two entangled, lower‑energy photons; perfectly correlated.

OPTICAL|Fabry perot.name: Fabry perot
OPTICAL|Fabry perot.definition: Two parallel, partially reflecting mirrors. Creates sharp, periodic transmission peaks. An optical filter.

OPTICAL|Fiber optic.name: Fiber optic
OPTICAL|Fiber optic.definition: Light bounces inside a transparent core, trapped by total internal reflection. Guides light around corners.
OPTICAL|Fiber optic.condition: Light bounces inside a transparent core by total internal reflection; guided around corners.

OPTICAL|Filter.name: Filter
OPTICAL|Filter.definition: A material that absorbs some wavelengths and transmits others (e.g., a red filter only lets red through).
OPTICAL|Filter.condition: Some wavelengths are absorbed; only a specific band is transmitted (e.g., red filter).

OPTICAL|Grating.name: Grating
OPTICAL|Grating.definition: A periodic array of slits. Splits light into spectra with much higher resolution than a prism.
OPTICAL|Grating.condition: A periodic array of slits; splits light into spectra with much higher resolution than a prism.

OPTICAL|Hologram.name: Hologram
OPTICAL|Hologram.definition: Record the interference pattern of an object beam and a reference beam. Re-illuminate to reconstruct a 3D image.
OPTICAL|Hologram.condition: The interference pattern of object and reference beams is recorded; re‑illuminating reconstructs a 3D image.

OPTICAL|Interferometer.name: Interferometer
OPTICAL|Interferometer.definition: Split a beam, send it down two paths, recombine. The interference pattern reveals path-length differences with incredible precision.
OPTICAL|Interferometer.condition: Split beam, send down two paths, recombine; interference pattern reveals path differences with precision λ/2.

OPTICAL|Invisibility cloak.name: Invisibility cloak
OPTICAL|Invisibility cloak.definition: A metamaterial that guides light *around* an object, recombining it on the other side. The object is invisible.
OPTICAL|Invisibility cloak.condition: A metamaterial guides light around an object, recombining it on the other side; the object is invisible.

OPTICAL|Kaleidoscope.name: Kaleidoscope
OPTICAL|Kaleidoscope.definition: A tube of angled mirrors. Creates repeating, symmetrical patterns from simple inputs.
OPTICAL|Kaleidoscope.condition: A tube of angled mirrors creates repeating, symmetrical patterns from simple inputs.

OPTICAL|Lens.name: Lens
OPTICAL|Lens.definition: A curved transparent medium. Converging (convex) focuses light; diverging (concave) spreads it.
OPTICAL|Lens.condition: A curved transparent medium; parallel rays converge (convex) or diverge (concave) at the focal point.

OPTICAL|Microscope.name: Microscope
OPTICAL|Microscope.definition: Two convex lenses. Magnifies tiny objects. Brings the small large.
OPTICAL|Microscope.condition: Two convex lenses; total magnification = M_obj × M_eye; magnifies tiny objects.

OPTICAL|Mirage.name: Mirage
OPTICAL|Mirage.definition: Hot air near the ground has a different refractive index. Light bends, creating a false image of water/sky on the horizon.
OPTICAL|Mirage.condition: Hot air near the ground has a different refractive index; light bends, creating a false image.

OPTICAL|Mirror.name: Mirror
OPTICAL|Mirror.definition: A perfectly smooth surface. It redirects a light ray at an equal but opposite angle. The angle is reversible.
OPTICAL|Mirror.condition: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; surface is smooth (< λ/20 roughness).

OPTICAL|Nonlinear optics.name: Nonlinear optics
OPTICAL|Nonlinear optics.definition: Intense light changes the material's properties. Frequency doubles (infrared becomes green).
OPTICAL|Nonlinear optics.condition: At high intensity, the material's properties become nonlinear; frequency doubles (e.g., infrared → green).

OPTICAL|Optical coating.name: Optical coating
OPTICAL|Optical coating.definition: Thin film coatings. Destructive interference cancels reflection, making glass anti-reflective.
OPTICAL|Optical coating.condition: Thin film coating; destructive interference cancels reflection, making glass anti‑reflective.

OPTICAL|Optical computing.name: Optical computing
OPTICAL|Optical computing.definition: Compute by manipulating light beams instead of electrons. The Fourier transform happens at the speed of light.
OPTICAL|Optical computing.condition: Computation by manipulating light beams; the Fourier transform happens at the speed of light.

OPTICAL|Optical vortex.name: Optical vortex
OPTICAL|Optical vortex.definition: A beam of light with a helical wavefront. It carries orbital angular momentum. It looks like a "donut" and can trap particles (optical tweezers).
OPTICAL|Optical vortex.condition: A beam with a helical wavefront; looks like a "donut"; can trap particles (optical tweezers).

OPTICAL|Periscope.name: Periscope
OPTICAL|Periscope.definition: Two parallel mirrors at 45°. Allows you to see over/around obstacles without exposing yourself.
OPTICAL|Periscope.condition: Two parallel mirrors at 45° allow viewing over/around obstacles; line of sight is bent.

OPTICAL|Periscope array.name: Periscope array
OPTICAL|Periscope array.definition: A grid of periscopes. Allows you to see around multiple obstacles simultaneously. Perfect for maze navigation.
OPTICAL|Periscope array.condition: A grid of periscopes allows seeing around multiple obstacles simultaneously.

OPTICAL|Phase conjugation.name: Phase conjugation
OPTICAL|Phase conjugation.definition: A mirror that reflects light back along its exact incoming path, reversing both direction and phase. "Retroreflection."
OPTICAL|Phase conjugation.condition: A mirror that reflects light back along its exact incoming path, reversing both direction and phase.

OPTICAL|Photon bunching.name: Photon bunching
OPTICAL|Photon bunching.definition: Subatomic particles (photons) arrive in clusters or anti-clusters depending on their quantum statistics (Bose vs. Fermi).
OPTICAL|Photon bunching.condition: Photons arrive in clusters or anti‑clusters depending on quantum statistics (Bose vs. Fermi).

OPTICAL|Photonic crystal.name: Photonic crystal
OPTICAL|Photonic crystal.definition: A material with a periodic refractive index. It creates a "photonic bandgap"—light cannot propagate at certain wavelengths. The optical analog of a semiconductor.
OPTICAL|Photonic crystal.condition: A material with a periodic refractive index; creates a photonic bandgap—light cannot propagate at certain wavelengths.

OPTICAL|Pinhole.name: Pinhole
OPTICAL|Pinhole.definition: A tiny hole. Light diffracts. Inverts and projects an image of the outside world onto a surface (camera obscura).
OPTICAL|Pinhole.condition: Light diffracts through a tiny hole; an inverted image of the outside world is projected (camera obscura).

OPTICAL|Planck constant.name: Planck constant
OPTICAL|Planck constant.definition: E = hν; light comes in discrete packets.
OPTICAL|Planck constant.condition: The relationship E = hν holds; light comes in discrete packets (photons).

OPTICAL|Plank constant.name: Plank constant
OPTICAL|Plank constant.definition: E = hν. Light comes in discrete packets (photons). The granularity of optics.

OPTICAL|Polarimetry.name: Polarimetry
OPTICAL|Polarimetry.definition: Measure the polarization state of light. Detects stress, magnetic fields, and optical activity (chirality).
OPTICAL|Polarimetry.condition: Measures the polarization state; detects stress, magnetic fields, and chirality.

OPTICAL|Polarize.name: Polarize
OPTICAL|Polarize.definition: A material that only transmits light with a specific electric field orientation. Blocks glare.
OPTICAL|Polarize.condition: Only light with the electric field parallel to the axis is transmitted; intensity follows Malus' law (I = I₀ cos² θ).

OPTICAL|Prism.name: Prism
OPTICAL|Prism.definition: A triangular medium. Splits white light into a spectrum (ROYGBIV) because different colors refract at different angles.
OPTICAL|Prism.condition: White light is split into a spectrum; deviation angle depends on wavelength (n(λ) varies).

OPTICAL|Reflector telescope.name: Reflector telescope
OPTICAL|Reflector telescope.definition: Uses a curved mirror to collect and focus light, not a lens. No chromatic aberration.
OPTICAL|Reflector telescope.condition: Uses a curved mirror (not lens) to collect/focus light; no chromatic aberration.

OPTICAL|Shadow.name: Shadow

OPTICAL|Shadow.condition: Light rays are obstructed; an umbra (total shadow) and penumbra (partial shadow) are formed.

OPTICAL|Slow light.name: Slow light

OPTICAL|Spectrometer.name: Spectrometer
