PATHOLOGICAL|Transfiguration.condition: A radical transformation through suffering; the "rebirth."

PATHOLOGICAL|Transform pain.name: Transform pain
PATHOLOGICAL|Transform pain.definition: The transformation of suffering into something else. The alchemy of pain.
PATHOLOGICAL|Transform pain.condition: The transformation of suffering into something else; the alchemy of pain.

PATHOLOGICAL|Trauma integration.name: Trauma integration
PATHOLOGICAL|Trauma integration.definition: The long, difficult work of integrating a trauma. The healing of the fracture.
PATHOLOGICAL|Trauma integration.condition: The long, difficult work of integrating a trauma; the healing of the fracture.

PATHOLOGICAL|Traumatic fracture.name: Traumatic fracture
PATHOLOGICAL|Traumatic fracture.definition: A trauma that shatters the sense of self. The "ego fracture."
PATHOLOGICAL|Traumatic fracture.condition: A trauma that shatters the sense of self; the "ego fracture."

PATHOLOGICAL|Wound.name: Wound
PATHOLOGICAL|Wound.definition: The infliction of a wound. The moment of injury.
PATHOLOGICAL|Wound.condition: A wound is inflicted; tissue is breached; function is disrupted.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Affective tone.name: Affective tone
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Affective tone.definition: The specific emotional color of a situation—the atmosphere of fear, the lightness of joy.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Affective tone.condition: The specific emotional colour of a situation—the atmosphere of fear, the lightness of joy.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Atmosphere.name: Atmosphere
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Atmosphere.definition: The emotional coloring of the world. A room can feel "heavy," "light," or "tense."
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Atmosphere.condition: The emotional colouring of the world; a room can feel "heavy," "light," or "tense."

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body image.name: Body image
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body image.definition: The coherent, stable, pre-reflective sense of one's own body as a unified whole.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body image.condition: The coherent, stable, pre‑reflective sense of one's own body as a unified whole.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body subject.name: Body subject
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body subject.definition: The body as the point of view, not as an object. You *have* a body, but you *are* it.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Body subject.condition: The body as the point of view, not as an object; you have a body, but you are it.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Deja vu phen.name: Deja vu phen
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Deja vu phen.definition: The eerie feeling that the present moment has been experienced before. A glitch in the temporal horizon.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Déjà vu.name: Déjà vu
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Déjà vu.definition: The eerie feeling that the present moment has been experienced before.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Déjà vu.condition: The eerie feeling that the present moment has been experienced before; a glitch in the temporal horizon.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Empathic encounter.name: Empathic encounter
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Empathic encounter.definition: The experience of another person as a subject, not as an object.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Empathic encounter.condition: The experience of another person as a subject, not as an object; face‑to‑face encounter.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon awareness.name: Horizon awareness
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon awareness.definition: The marginal, unnoticed background that gives the focal object its sense.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Horizon awareness.condition: The marginal, unnoticed background that gives the focal object its sense; the fringe of awareness.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Inner time.name: Inner time
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Inner time.definition: The subjective, pre-reflective sense of time passing. Not clock-time, but lived-time.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Inner time.condition: The subjective, pre‑reflective sense of time passing; not clock‑time, but lived‑time.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentional act.name: Intentional act
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentional act.definition: Consciousness is always consciousness-of-something. You see *the tree*, not just a patch of brown and green.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Intentional act.condition: Consciousness is always consciousness‑of‑something; you see the tree, not just a patch of brown and green.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived meaning.name: Lived meaning
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived meaning.definition: A puzzle piece is not just a shape; it is a *fragment of a story* that invites completion.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived meaning.condition: A puzzle piece is not just a shape; it is a fragment of a story that invites completion.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived space.name: Lived space
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived space.definition: Space as experienced from the body. Not X/Y coordinates, but "near/far," "above/below," "reachable/unreachable."
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived space.condition: Space as experienced from the body; not X/Y coordinates, but "near/far," "above/below," "reachable/unreachable."

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived time.name: Lived time
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived time.definition: The flow of time as a continuous "specious present," holding the past and anticipating the future.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Lived time.condition: The flow of time as a continuous "specious present," holding the past and anticipating the future.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Meaning gestalt.name: Meaning gestalt
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Meaning gestalt.definition: A situation's meaning is a holistic Gestalt, not a collection of separate facts.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Meaning gestalt.condition: A situation's meaning is a holistic Gestalt, not a collection of separate facts.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Mirroring.name: Mirroring
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Mirroring.definition: The immediate recognition that the Other is like me: a subject with its own interiority.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Mirroring.condition: The immediate recognition that the Other is like me: a subject with its own interiority.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Pain.name: Pain
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Pain.definition: The raw, unpleasant, bodily-embedded feeling of damage or threat.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Pain.condition: The raw, unpleasant, bodily‑embedded feeling of damage or threat.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal reduction.name: Phenomenal reduction
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal reduction.definition: Systematically ignoring the objective, physical nature of an object to focus on its pure appearance (the epoché).
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal reduction.condition: Systematically ignoring the objective, physical nature of an object to focus on its pure appearance (the epoché).

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal transparency.name: Phenomenal transparency
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal transparency.definition: When we are engrossed in a task, the medium of perception disappears. You see through the window, not the glass.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Phenomenal transparency.condition: When engrossed in a task, the medium of perception disappears; you see through the window, not the glass.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence feel.name: Presence feel
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence feel.definition: The immediate, vivid, undeniable sense of "I am here, now, and this is happening."
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Presence feel.condition: The immediate, vivid, undeniable sense of "I am here, now, and this is happening."

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Quale net.name: Quale net
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Quale net.definition: The interwoven web of qualia. The smell of a particular flower and the memory of a summer day are fused.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Quale net.condition: The interwoven web of qualia; the smell of a flower and the memory of a summer day are fused.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Redness.name: Redness
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Redness.definition: The irreducible, subjective feel of the color red. You cannot describe it to a blind person.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|Redness.condition: The irreducible, subjective feel of the colour red; you cannot describe it to a blind person.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flesh of the world.name: The flesh of the world
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flesh of the world.definition: The world is experienced as a "flesh" that is continuous with our own bodily flesh. Touch is a two-way street.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flesh of the world.condition: The world is experienced as a "flesh" that is continuous with our own bodily flesh; touch is a two‑way street.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flow experience.name: The flow experience
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flow experience.definition: The state of being completely absorbed in an activity. The "I" disappears into the doing.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The flow experience.condition: The state of being completely absorbed in an activity; the "I" disappears into the doing.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gaze.name: The gaze
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gaze.definition: The feeling of being seen by another subject. The awareness that you are an object for another subject.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gaze.condition: The feeling of being seen by another subject; the awareness that you are an object for another subject.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gift of presence.name: The gift of presence
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gift of presence.definition: The miracle of being present in the moment. The sheer fact of being aware is the primary gift.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The gift of presence.condition: The miracle of being present in the moment; the sheer fact of being aware is the primary gift.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intentional arc.name: The intentional arc
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intentional arc.definition: The continuous, temporal directedness of consciousness. The conscious mind is always "at work" shaping the present.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intentional arc.condition: The continuous, temporal directedness of consciousness; the conscious mind is always "at work" shaping the present.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intersubjective.name: The intersubjective
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intersubjective.definition: The recognition that we share a common world, and that this shared world is the foundation of meaning.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The intersubjective.condition: The recognition that we share a common world, and that this shared world is the foundation of meaning.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lifeworld.name: The lifeworld
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lifeworld.definition: The everyday, pre-theoretical world of lived experience. The world as it is *before* physics, chemistry, and neuroscience.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lifeworld.condition: The everyday, pre‑theoretical world of lived experience; the world as it is before physics, chemistry, and neuroscience.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lived puzzle.name: The lived puzzle
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lived puzzle.definition: The puzzle is not a cold object; it is a *situation* that invites a lived response.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The lived puzzle.condition: The puzzle is not a cold object; it is a situation that invites a lived response.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The meaning given.name: The meaning given
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The meaning given.definition: The world is not passively perceived; it is actively *constituted* in consciousness.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The meaning given.condition: The world is not passively perceived; it is actively constituted in consciousness.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The mystery of qualia.name: The mystery of qualia
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The mystery of qualia.definition: The irreducible, unexplainable interiority of experience. I can describe redness, but I cannot convey it.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The mystery of qualia.condition: The irreducible, unexplainable interiority of experience; I can describe redness, but I cannot convey it.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other as witness.name: The other as witness
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other as witness.definition: The Other is a witness to my existence. Their presence validates (or threatens) my being.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other as witness.condition: The Other is a witness to my existence; their presence validates (or threatens) my being.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's gaze.name: The other's gaze
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's gaze.definition: The experience of being seen by another subject. This creates a sense of self-consciousness and possible shame.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's gaze.condition: The experience of being seen by another subject; this creates a sense of self‑consciousness and possible shame.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's innerity.name: The other's innerity
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's innerity.definition: The Other's consciousness is fundamentally inaccessible. I can never *feel* what you feel—I can only witness it.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's interiority.name: The other's interiority
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's interiority.definition: The Other's consciousness is fundamentally inaccessible.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The other's interiority.condition: The Other's consciousness is fundamentally inaccessible; I can never feel what you feel—I can only witness it.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal self.name: The phenomenal self
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal self.definition: The self as an ongoing, temporal, pre-reflective, and affective stream of experience.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal self.condition: The self as an ongoing, temporal, pre‑reflective, and affective stream of experience.

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal universe.name: The phenomenal universe
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal universe.definition: The entire universe is constituted by and for experience. There is no "view from nowhere."
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The phenomenal universe.condition: The entire universe is constituted by and for experience; there is no "view from nowhere."

PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The self as horizon.name: The self as horizon
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The self as horizon.definition: The self is not an object in the world; it is the *invisible horizon* from which the world appears.
PHENOMENOLOGICAL|The self as horizon.condition: The self is not an object in the world; it is the invisible horizon from which the world appears.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Anchoring.name: Anchoring
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Anchoring.definition: the first number disproportionately shapes the rest
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Anchoring.condition: The first number encountered disproportionately influences subsequent estimates.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Approach.name: Approach
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Approach.condition: Agent moves towards a positively valenced object; persists until contact.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Assign valence.name: Assign valence
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Assign valence.definition: attach good or bad to a thing
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Assign valence.condition: A stimulus is labelled as good (positive) or bad (negative); approach/avoid behaviour follows.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive fusion.name: Cognitive fusion
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive fusion.definition: the belief and the self are the same thing, so challenging it feels like an attack
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive fusion.condition: The belief is so identified with the self that challenging it feels like a personal attack.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive niche.name: Cognitive niche
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive niche.definition: build external structure so less has to be held internally
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Cognitive niche.condition: The agent builds external structures (notes, organisations) to reduce internal memory load.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Confirmation bias.name: Confirmation bias
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Confirmation bias.definition: seek and recall what agrees; overlook what does not
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Confirmation bias.condition: Agent preferentially seeks and recalls information that confirms the belief, ignoring disconfirming evidence.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Control depletion.name: Control depletion
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Control depletion.definition: effort spent on one thing reduces what is available for the next
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Control depletion.condition: After exerting effortful control, performance on a subsequent self‑control task is worse.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Counterthink.name: Counterthink
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Counterthink.condition: Agent actively inhibits a current belief and imagines an alternative: “what if this is wrong?”

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Dissonance.name: Dissonance
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Dissonance.definition: tension between what is believed and what was done
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Dissonance.condition: A belief and an action are inconsistent; the agent experiences discomfort and seeks to reduce it.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Empathy.name: Empathy
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Empathy.condition: Agent simulates the other's internal state and experiences a similar feeling.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Encode.name: Encode
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Encode.definition: store an association or an identity
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Encode.condition: A sensory experience is transformed into a memory trace; subsequent recall is possible.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Eureka.name: Eureka
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Eureka.definition: a sudden reconfiguration after a period of not working on it
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Eureka.condition: After a period of not working on the problem, a sudden reconfiguration yields a solution.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Flow.recipe: Att focused + Mot optimal + skill matched
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Flow.name: Flow
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Flow.definition: deep engagement, low self-consciousness, high performance
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Flow.condition: Deep engagement; challenge matches skill; low self‑consciousness; time distortion.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Framing.name: Framing
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Framing.definition: the same problem stated differently produces different choices
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Framing.condition: The same problem, stated differently (gain vs loss frame), produces different choices.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Global access.name: Global access
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Global access.definition: information becomes usable when it reaches everything at once
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Global access.condition: Information becomes globally available when it is in working memory and attention is broadcast.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Grit.name: Grit
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Grit.definition: continuing after failure toward a distant goal
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Grit.condition: Continues pursuing a distant goal despite failures; sustained effort over long periods.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit formation.name: Habit formation
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit formation.definition: consistent reward makes an action automatic
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Habit formation.condition: A consistent reward after an action makes that action more likely and more automatic.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Hypervigilance.name: Hypervigilance
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Hypervigilance.definition: over-focus on danger; peripheral awareness lost
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Hypervigilance.condition: Attention narrows onto a perceived threat; peripheral awareness is lost.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Insight.name: Insight
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Insight.definition: a solution arrives without a warmth gradient
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Insight.condition: A solution arrives suddenly without a gradual buildup of warmth (Metcalfe & Wiebe).

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Learned helplessness.recipe: Bel that action and outcome are uncoupled + Mot zero

ingredients.qual: that action and outcome are uncoupled

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Learned helplessness.name: Learned helplessness
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Learned helplessness.definition: unavoidable failure produces passive acceptance, even once escape is possible
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Learned helplessness.condition: After unavoidable failures, agent believes actions and outcomes are uncoupled; stops trying even when escape is possible.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Locus of control.name: Locus of control
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Locus of control.definition: whether outcomes depend on your actions or on something else
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Locus of control.condition: Agent believes outcomes are determined by its own actions (internal) or by external factors.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Loss aversion.name: Loss aversion
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Loss aversion.definition: losses weigh more than equivalent gains
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Loss aversion.condition: Losses are subjectively weighted more heavily than equivalent gains; agent avoids losses.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Metacognition.name: Metacognition
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Metacognition.definition: knowing what you know; calibrating confidence
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Metacognition.condition: Agent can assess its own knowledge and calibrate confidence; knows what it knows.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Narrative self.name: Narrative self
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Narrative self.definition: the account you keep of your own history
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Narrative self.condition: The self is a continuous, coherent story constructed from episodic memories.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Overload.name: Overload
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Overload.definition: too much at once; errors and latency both rise
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Overload.condition: Too much information arrives; working memory is saturated; errors and latency increase.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Pattern match.name: Pattern match
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Pattern match.condition: A current stimulus is compared to stored templates; the best match is recognised without analysis.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plan.name: Plan
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plan.definition: produce a sequence that would reach it
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plan.condition: A sequence of actions is generated that, if executed, will reach the goal.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plasticity.name: Plasticity
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plasticity.definition: repeated activity changes what is easy
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Plasticity.condition: Repeated activity changes neural connections, making the behaviour easier over time.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Priming.name: Priming
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Priming.definition: exposure shapes later responses without being noticed
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Priming.condition: Exposure to a stimulus (below awareness) facilitates a later response to a related stimulus.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Regulation.name: Regulation
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Regulation.definition: deliberately modulate a response; reappraise what a thing means
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Regulation.condition: Agent deliberately modulates an emotional response by reinterpreting the situation.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Retrieve.name: Retrieve
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Retrieve.definition: recall it; speed depends on recency and frequency
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Retrieve.condition: A cue triggers the recall of a stored association; speed depends on recency and frequency.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Rumination.name: Rumination
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Rumination.definition: repetitive passive focus that does not progress
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Rumination.condition: Agent repeatedly retrieves negative memories and focuses on them without making progress.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-determination.name: Self-determination
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-determination.definition: motivation arises from these three being satisfied

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-efficacy.name: Self-efficacy
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Self-efficacy.definition: belief you can do it, which changes how long you persist

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Shift attention.name: Shift attention
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Shift attention.definition: move the focus; details that were unread become read
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Shift attention.condition: Attention moves from one stimulus to a new one; details of the new stimulus become available.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Simulate.name: Simulate
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Simulate.condition: The agent runs an internal simulation of an action and its consequences without actually performing it.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Theory of mind.name: Theory of mind
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Theory of mind.definition: model another's beliefs explicitly, not by simulation
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Theory of mind.condition: Agent explicitly models another's beliefs, not just simulates; can reason about false beliefs.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Withdraw.name: Withdraw
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Withdraw.definition: move away — Human T3 Avoid is the spatial version
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Withdraw.condition: Agent moves away from a negatively valenced object; distance increases.

PSYCHOLOGICAL|Working memory.name: Working memory
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Working memory.definition: hold and manipulate about four things at once
PSYCHOLOGICAL|Working memory.condition: Can hold and manipulate about four chunks of information at a time; limited capacity.

QUANTUM|Amplitude search.name: Amplitude search
QUANTUM|Amplitude search.definition: find a target faster than checking each
QUANTUM|Amplitude search.condition: Amplitude amplification finds a target in O(√N) steps (Grover's algorithm).

QUANTUM|Collapse.name: Collapse
QUANTUM|Collapse.condition: After measurement, the state is found in exactly one basis state; probabilities match Born rule.

QUANTUM|Decoherence.name: Decoherence
QUANTUM|Decoherence.condition: The system becomes entangled with the environment; the system's quantum information is lost.

QUANTUM|Delayed erasure.name: Delayed erasure
QUANTUM|Delayed erasure.definition: undo a distinction after the fact
QUANTUM|Delayed erasure.condition: Whether an interference pattern appears depends on a choice made after the particle has passed the slits.

QUANTUM|Detect without touching.name: Detect without touching
QUANTUM|Detect without touching.definition: learn about a thing without disturbing it
QUANTUM|Detect without touching.condition: The presence of an object is inferred from the interference pattern without physically interacting with it.

QUANTUM|Entangled pair.name: Entangled pair
QUANTUM|Entangled pair.condition: Measurements on the two particles are correlated; Bell inequalities are violated.

QUANTUM|Error correction.name: Error correction
QUANTUM|Error correction.condition: Redundant encoding detects and corrects errors without measuring the logical state.

QUANTUM|Period extraction.name: Period extraction
QUANTUM|Period extraction.definition: find the repeat in a signal
QUANTUM|Period extraction.condition: Quantum Fourier transform extracts the period of a function (Shor's algorithm).

QUANTUM|Register.name: Register
QUANTUM|Register.condition: A register of n qubits can hold a superposition of 2ⁿ basis states.

QUANTUM|Reversible operation.name: Reversible operation
QUANTUM|Reversible operation.condition: The operation can be inverted; no information is lost; unitary evolution.

QUANTUM|Sequence of operations.name: Sequence of operations
QUANTUM|Sequence of operations.condition: Multiple reversible operations applied in sequence; entangling gates produce entanglement.

QUANTUM|Superposed candidates.name: Superposed candidates
QUANTUM|Superposed candidates.condition: The state is a linear combination of basis states; no one basis state is selected.

QUANTUM|Transfer and destroy.name: Transfer and destroy
QUANTUM|Transfer and destroy.definition: move a state; the original does not survive
QUANTUM|Transfer and destroy.condition: A state is transferred to another particle; the original state is destroyed (no cloning).

QUANTUM|Tunnel.name: Tunnel
QUANTUM|Tunnel.definition: pass a barrier that should have stopped you
QUANTUM|Tunnel.condition: Particle has E < V₀, yet appears on the other side of the barrier with probability > 0.

QUANTUM|Watched pot.name: Watched pot
QUANTUM|Watched pot.condition: Frequent measurements freeze the state evolution; transition probability is suppressed.

RAW DATA|Attractor.name: Attractor
RAW DATA|Attractor.condition: Trajectories in state space converge toward a low‑dimensional manifold.

RAW DATA|Autocorrelation.name: Autocorrelation
RAW DATA|Autocorrelation.definition: how much a thing predicts itself later
RAW DATA|Autocorrelation.condition: Correlation between a signal and a delayed version of itself; peaks indicate periodicity.

RAW DATA|Cavity.name: Cavity
RAW DATA|Cavity.definition: an enclosure with nothing in it; a hole

RAW DATA|Chaos.name: Chaos
RAW DATA|Chaos.definition: more variation than the current frame can hold
RAW DATA|Chaos.condition: More variation/entropy is arriving per frame than the system can absorb; exceeds processing capacity.

RAW DATA|Covariance.name: Covariance
RAW DATA|Covariance.condition: Cov = Σ (x‑x̄)(y‑ȳ) / n; non‑zero value indicates co‑variation.

RAW DATA|Curve.name: Curve
RAW DATA|Curve.definition: a run that changes direction; a line that is not straight

RAW DATA|Deform.name: Deform
RAW DATA|Deform.definition: the form changes and the thing survives as itself

RAW DATA|Density gradient.name: Density gradient
RAW DATA|Density gradient.condition: The rate of change of density/texture is computed; high gradient indicates boundaries.

RAW DATA|Disappear.name: Disappear
RAW DATA|Disappear.definition: present in one frame and absent in the next

RAW DATA|Enclosure.name: Enclosure
RAW DATA|Enclosure.definition: a boundary that closes, so what it holds has an inside

RAW DATA|Higher-order transition.name: Higher-order transition
RAW DATA|Higher-order transition.definition: what follows what, given two steps back

RAW DATA|Histogram.name: Histogram
RAW DATA|Histogram.condition: Count of each value is computed; frequencies sum to total.

RAW DATA|Indent.name: Indent
RAW DATA|Indent.definition: the boundary displaced inward without being broken

RAW DATA|Information density.name: Information density
RAW DATA|Information density.definition: how much a region actually says
RAW DATA|Information density.condition: Information density = Entropy / (1 – Redundancy); high when entropy is high and redundancy is low.

RAW DATA|Inside.name: Inside
RAW DATA|Inside.definition: within an enclosure and not on its edge

RAW DATA|Join.name: Join
RAW DATA|Join.definition: two regions become one where they meet

RAW DATA|Kernel.name: Kernel
RAW DATA|Kernel.definition: a filter that extracts a feature
RAW DATA|Kernel.condition: A local filter (kernel) extracts a specific feature (e.g., edge, blob) from the density gradient.

RAW DATA|Line.name: Line
RAW DATA|Line.definition: cells in a straight run; what a ray or an edge follows

RAW DATA|Manifold.name: Manifold
RAW DATA|Manifold.definition: a low-dimensional surface the data lies on

RAW DATA|Markov chain.name: Markov chain
RAW DATA|Markov chain.condition: The next state probability depends only on the current state; transition matrix is stationary.

RAW DATA|Object.name: Object
RAW DATA|Object.definition: cells held together as one thing, and tracked as that thing

RAW DATA|Outside.name: Outside
RAW DATA|Outside.definition: beyond the enclosure; the complement of inside

RAW DATA|Prediction residual.name: Prediction residual
RAW DATA|Prediction residual.definition: what the model failed to expect

RAW DATA|Principal axis.name: Principal axis
RAW DATA|Principal axis.condition: The eigenvector corresponding to the largest eigenvalue gives the direction of maximum variance.

RAW DATA|Region.name: Region
RAW DATA|Region.definition: every cell reachable from every other; what a boundary encloses

RAW DATA|Repetition.name: Repetition
RAW DATA|Repetition.definition: the same form recurring at a regular displacement

RAW DATA|Segment.name: Segment
RAW DATA|Segment.condition: Regions where autocorrelation exceeds a threshold are grouped into contiguous correlated regions.

RAW DATA|Split.name: Split
RAW DATA|Split.definition: one region becomes two where a boundary appears between them

RAW DATA|Texton.name: Texton
RAW DATA|Texton.condition: A micro‑pattern repeats across the image; it can be extracted by thresholding local textures.

RAW DATA|Texture.name: Texture
RAW DATA|Texture.condition: Local patterns (edges, spots, stripes) are detected by comparing adjacent pixel values.

RAW DATA|Threshold map.name: Threshold map
RAW DATA|Threshold map.condition: Regions where local variance exceeds a threshold are marked as high‑variation edges/boundaries.

RAW DATA|Tile.name: Tile

REBELLION|Preach heresy.condition: Articulating a belief that contradicts established doctrine.

REBELLION|The revolutionary self.condition: The self that is forged in the crucible of rebellion.

REBELLION|The transgressive act.definition: The boundary-breaking act that creates new meaning and possibility.
REBELLION|The transgressive act.condition: The boundary‑breaking act that creates new meaning and possibility.

REBELLION|Undermine.condition: Taking actions that weaken a system from within.

SOCIAL|Alliance.name: Alliance
SOCIAL|Alliance.definition: A formal or informal agreement to act cooperatively. A pact.
SOCIAL|Alliance.condition: A formal or informal agreement exists; agents act cooperatively toward shared ends.

SOCIAL|Bazaar.name: Bazaar
SOCIAL|Bazaar.definition: A decentralized social-economic system where reputation and trust enable exchange.
SOCIAL|Bazaar.condition: A decentralised social‑economic system where reputation and trust enable exchange.

SOCIAL|Betrayal.name: Betrayal
SOCIAL|Betrayal.definition: Acting against a cooperative agreement for personal gain.
SOCIAL|Betrayal.condition: An agent breaks a cooperative agreement for personal gain; trust is violated.

SOCIAL|Coalition.name: Coalition
SOCIAL|Coalition.definition: A temporary alliance of multiple individuals for a specific purpose.
SOCIAL|Coalition.condition: A temporary alliance of multiple individuals for a specific purpose.

SOCIAL|Cognitive niche.name: Cognitive niche
SOCIAL|Cognitive niche.definition: Culture creates external "crutches" that extend cognitive capacity.
SOCIAL|Cognitive niche.condition: Culture creates external "crutches" (writing, math, institutions) that extend cognitive capacity.

SOCIAL|Cognitive niche soc.name: Cognitive niche soc
SOCIAL|Cognitive niche soc.definition: Culture creates external "crutches" (writing, math, institutions) that extend cognitive capacity.

SOCIAL|Collective memory.name: Collective memory
SOCIAL|Collective memory.definition: A group remembers its past through shared narratives, archives, and rituals.
SOCIAL|Collective memory.condition: A group remembers its past through shared narratives, archives, and rituals.

SOCIAL|Communication.name: Communication
SOCIAL|Communication.definition: The transmission of information between agents. Language, gesture, symbol.
SOCIAL|Communication.condition: A signal is transmitted from one agent to another; the receiver's state changes in response.

SOCIAL|Competition.name: Competition
SOCIAL|Competition.definition: Two or more agents pursue conflicting goals. A zero-sum or negative-sum interaction.
SOCIAL|Competition.condition: Agents pursue conflicting goals; one agent's gain is the other's loss (zero‑sum or negative‑sum).

SOCIAL|Conformity.name: Conformity
SOCIAL|Conformity.definition: An individual adjusts their behavior to align with the group norm. Self-censorship.
SOCIAL|Conformity.condition: Individual changes their behaviour to align with the group norm; deviation from group is reduced.

SOCIAL|Cooperation.name: Cooperation
SOCIAL|Cooperation.definition: Two or more agents work together toward a common outcome. Mutual benefit.
SOCIAL|Cooperation.condition: Both agents work together; each gains a benefit that is greater than acting alone.

SOCIAL|Cultural transmission.name: Cultural transmission
SOCIAL|Cultural transmission.definition: Beliefs, norms, and practices are passed from one generation to the next. Social evolution.
SOCIAL|Cultural transmission.condition: Beliefs, norms, and practices are passed from one generation to the next via imitation and communication.

SOCIAL|Diffusion.name: Diffusion
SOCIAL|Diffusion.definition: A new idea spreads through the social network. S-curve adoption.
SOCIAL|Diffusion.condition: A new idea spreads through the social network; adoption follows an S‑curve.

SOCIAL|Dunbar number.name: Dunbar number
SOCIAL|Dunbar number.definition: The maximum number of stable relationships a human can maintain (~150). A network constraint.
SOCIAL|Dunbar number.condition: The maximum number of stable relationships is ~150; beyond this, group cohesion breaks down.

SOCIAL|Ecosystem soc.name: Ecosystem soc
SOCIAL|Ecosystem soc.definition: A social system with multiple interacting roles (producer, consumer, decomposer).

SOCIAL|Gossip.name: Gossip
SOCIAL|Gossip.definition: Information about an individual's reputation spreads through the network.
SOCIAL|Gossip.condition: Information about an individual's reputation spreads through the network; others' beliefs change.

SOCIAL|Imitation.name: Imitation
SOCIAL|Imitation.definition: Copy the actions of another agent. Learning through observation.
SOCIAL|Imitation.condition: The agent copies the action of another; the copied action matches the observed action in timing and form.

SOCIAL|Institution.name: Institution
SOCIAL|Institution.definition: A persistent structure of norms and roles that governs behavior. Government, law, marriage.
SOCIAL|Institution.condition: A persistent structure of norms and roles that governs behaviour; stable over time (government, law).

SOCIAL|Leadership.name: Leadership
SOCIAL|Leadership.definition: A designated agent that guides the group. Others follow.
SOCIAL|Leadership.condition: A designated agent guides the group; others follow the leader's actions or commands.

SOCIAL|Mob mentality.name: Mob mentality
SOCIAL|Mob mentality.definition: A loss of individual identity in a crowd. Behavior becomes impulsive and extreme.
SOCIAL|Mob mentality.condition: A loss of individual identity in a crowd; behaviour becomes impulsive and extreme.

SOCIAL|Norm enforcement.name: Norm enforcement
SOCIAL|Norm enforcement.definition: A norm is enforced by sanctions (punishment/reward).
SOCIAL|Norm enforcement.condition: A norm is enforced by sanctions; violators are punished, compliant are rewarded.

SOCIAL|Normling.name: Normling
SOCIAL|Normling.definition: A norm is enforced by sanctions (punishment for violation, reward for adherence).

SOCIAL|Persuasion.name: Persuasion
SOCIAL|Persuasion.definition: Change another agent's beliefs or intentions through communication.
SOCIAL|Persuasion.condition: The receiver's belief or intention changes after communication; trust mediates the effect.

SOCIAL|Polarization.name: Polarization
SOCIAL|Polarization.definition: Groups become more extreme in their positions due to internal conformity and external isolation.
SOCIAL|Polarization.condition: Groups become more extreme in their positions due to internal conformity and external isolation.

SOCIAL|Public goods.name: Public goods
SOCIAL|Public goods.definition: A resource that benefits all but requires collective contribution. The tragedy of the commons (Economic cross-synth).
SOCIAL|Public goods.condition: A resource that benefits all but requires collective contribution; risk of free‑riding (tragedy of the commons).

SOCIAL|Punishment.name: Punishment
SOCIAL|Punishment.definition: A costly action taken against a norm-violator. Enforces cooperation.
SOCIAL|Punishment.condition: A costly action is taken against a norm‑violator; enforces cooperation.

SOCIAL|Reputation cascade.name: Reputation cascade
SOCIAL|Reputation cascade.definition: A reputation spreads through the network like a cascade. Positive or negative.
SOCIAL|Reputation cascade.condition: A reputation spreads through the network like a cascade; positive or negative.

SOCIAL|Ritual.name: Ritual
SOCIAL|Ritual.definition: A repeated, structured social activity that reinforces group identity and norms.
SOCIAL|Ritual.condition: A repeated, structured social activity that reinforces group identity and norms.

SOCIAL|Scapegoating.name: Scapegoating
SOCIAL|Scapegoating.definition: Blame is redirected to a single individual. The group maintains cohesion by expelling the "other."
SOCIAL|Scapegoating.condition: Blame is redirected to a single individual; the group maintains cohesion by expelling the "other."

SOCIAL|Social attractor.name: Social attractor
SOCIAL|Social attractor.definition: A basin of attraction in the social space. Groups converge on dominant opinions.
SOCIAL|Social attractor.condition: A basin of attraction in the social space; groups converge on dominant opinions.

SOCIAL|Social capital.name: Social capital
SOCIAL|Social capital.definition: The value embedded in social relationships. It can be leveraged for cooperation.
SOCIAL|Social capital.condition: The value embedded in social relationships; it can be leveraged for cooperation.

SOCIAL|Social construction.name: Social construction
SOCIAL|Social construction.definition: A shared belief becomes "real" because the group acts as if it is real.
SOCIAL|Social construction.condition: A shared belief becomes "real" because the group acts as if it is real (e.g., money, borders).

SOCIAL|Social contruction.name: Social contruction
SOCIAL|Social contruction.definition: A shared belief becomes "real" because the group acts as if it is real. Money, borders, status.

SOCIAL|Social cycle.name: Social cycle
SOCIAL|Social cycle.definition: Culture changes over time, but with cycles. Generational oscillation.
SOCIAL|Social cycle.condition: Culture changes over time, but with cycles; generational oscillation.

SOCIAL|Social ecosystem.name: Social ecosystem
SOCIAL|Social ecosystem.definition: A social system with multiple interacting roles.
SOCIAL|Social ecosystem.condition: A social system with multiple interacting roles (producer, consumer, decomposer).

SOCIAL|Social graph.name: Social graph
SOCIAL|Social graph.definition: A map of who is connected to whom. The topology of the group.
SOCIAL|Social graph.condition: A map of who is connected to whom; edges represent interactions or relationships.

SOCIAL|Subculture.name: Subculture
SOCIAL|Subculture.definition: A group within a larger group with distinct norms and values.
SOCIAL|Subculture.condition: A group within a larger group with distinct norms and values; they identify as different.

SOCIAL|Swarm intelligence.name: Swarm intelligence
SOCIAL|Swarm intelligence.definition: Decentralized collective problem-solving. Ant colonies, flocks, crowds.
SOCIAL|Swarm intelligence.condition: Decentralised collective problem‑solving; simple local rules produce complex global behaviour (ants, flocks).

SOCIAL|Symbol.name: Symbol
SOCIAL|Symbol.definition: An arbitrary sign (word, flag, gesture) that carries shared meaning within a group.
SOCIAL|Symbol.condition: An arbitrary sign (word, flag, gesture) that carries shared meaning within a group.

SOCIAL|The hive.name: The hive
SOCIAL|The hive.definition: A group with such strong cohesion that it acts as a single super-organism. Individuality is suppressed.
SOCIAL|The hive.condition: A group with such strong cohesion that it acts as a single super‑organism; individuality is suppressed.

SOCIAL|Tribalism.name: Tribalism
SOCIAL|Tribalism.definition: In-group favoritism paired with out-group hostility. Us vs. Them.
SOCIAL|Tribalism.condition: In‑group favoritism paired with out‑group hostility; "us vs. them."

SOCIAL|Wisdom crowds.name: Wisdom crowds
SOCIAL|Wisdom crowds.definition: The aggregate judgment of many independent individuals is often more accurate than any single expert.

SOCIAL|Wisdom of crowds.name: Wisdom of crowds
SOCIAL|Wisdom of crowds.definition: Aggregate judgment of many independent individuals is more accurate.
SOCIAL|Wisdom of crowds.condition: The aggregate judgment of many independent individuals is often more accurate than any single expert.

SOMNIAL|Ascend.name: Ascend
SOMNIAL|Ascend.definition: The act of waking up. The return to the conscious world.
SOMNIAL|Ascend.condition: The crossing from sleep to wakefulness; EEG shifts from theta/delta to beta/alpha; full alertness returns.

SOMNIAL|Consolidation.name: Consolidation
SOMNIAL|Consolidation.definition: The process of memory consolidation during sleep. The "saving" of the day's experiences.
SOMNIAL|Consolidation.condition: The process of memory consolidation during sleep; the "saving" of the day's experiences.

SOMNIAL|Cycle.name: Cycle
SOMNIAL|Cycle.definition: The complete, recurring sequence of sleep stages across a night.
SOMNIAL|Cycle.condition: A complete cycle of the automaton's operation; the "full rotation."

SOMNIAL|Descend.name: Descend
SOMNIAL|Descend.definition: The act of falling asleep. The crossing of the threshold.
SOMNIAL|Descend.condition: The crossing from wakefulness to sleep; EEG shifts from beta/alpha to theta/delta; hypnagogic imagery may appear.

SOMNIAL|Dream incubation.name: Dream incubation
SOMNIAL|Dream incubation.definition: Planting a seed in the mind before sleep to influence the dream's content.
SOMNIAL|Dream incubation.condition: Planting a seed in the mind before sleep to influence the dream's content.

SOMNIAL|Dream laboratory.name: Dream laboratory
SOMNIAL|Dream laboratory.definition: Using lucid dreaming to solve creative problems or practice skills.
SOMNIAL|Dream laboratory.condition: Using lucid dreaming to solve creative problems or practice skills.

SOMNIAL|Dream narrate.name: Dream narrate
SOMNIAL|Dream narrate.definition: The creation of a dream narrative. The mind weaves a story from fragments.
SOMNIAL|Dream narrate.condition: The mind weaves a story from fragments during sleep; agent reports a dream after waking.

SOMNIAL|Hypnagogia state.name: Hypnagogia state
SOMNIAL|Hypnagogia state.definition: Entering the liminal state where logic loosens and imagery becomes fluid.
SOMNIAL|Hypnagogia state.condition: Entering the liminal state where logic loosens and imagery becomes fluid; hypnagogic hallucinations.

SOMNIAL|Hypnopompic.name: Hypnopompic
SOMNIAL|Hypnopompic.definition: The transitional state between sleep and waking. The fading dream residue.
SOMNIAL|Hypnopompic.condition: The transitional state between sleep and waking; the fading dream residue.

ZOOLOGICAL|The critical period.name: The critical period
ZOOLOGICAL|The critical period.definition: The narrow temporal window where specific environmental input must occur for normal development.
ZOOLOGICAL|The critical period.condition: The narrow temporal window where specific environmental input must occur for normal development.

ZOOLOGICAL|The ethological archive.name: The ethological archive
ZOOLOGICAL|The ethological archive.definition: Behaviors are encoded in the genes. The archive of survival across millennia.
ZOOLOGICAL|The ethological archive.condition: Behaviours are encoded in the genes; the archive of survival across millennia.

ZOOLOGICAL|The trophic web.name: The trophic web
ZOOLOGICAL|The trophic web.definition: The complete network of who eats whom in an ecosystem. The flow of matter and energy.
ZOOLOGICAL|The trophic web.condition: The complete network of who eats whom in an ecosystem; flow of matter and energy.

ZOOLOGICAL|The umwelt field.name: The umwelt field
ZOOLOGICAL|The umwelt field.definition: The entire set of meaningful stimuli for a given species. The world as *they* experience it.
ZOOLOGICAL|The umwelt field.condition: The entire set of meaningful stimuli for a given species; the world as they experience it.

ZOOLOGICAL|The wild self.name: The wild self
ZOOLOGICAL|The wild self.definition: The self as defined by ecological relationships, not by reflective thought.
ZOOLOGICAL|The wild self.condition: The self as defined by ecological relationships, not by reflective thought.

ZOOLOGICAL|Tool use.name: Tool use
ZOOLOGICAL|Tool use.definition: Using objects as tools to extract prey (sticks for termites, rocks for nuts).
ZOOLOGICAL|Tool use.condition: Using objects as tools to extract prey (sticks for termites, rocks for nuts).

ZOOLOGICAL|Trophic cascade.name: Trophic cascade
ZOOLOGICAL|Trophic cascade.definition: The removal/addition of a top predator causes effects that ripple down the entire food chain.
ZOOLOGICAL|Trophic cascade.condition: The removal/addition of a top predator causes effects that ripple down the entire food chain.

ZOOLOGICAL|UNGRATEFUL DEAD (Thanatosis).name: UNGRATEFUL DEAD (Thanatosis)
ZOOLOGICAL|UNGRATEFUL DEAD (Thanatosis).definition: Playing dead to stop the predatory response of a predator that only attacks moving prey.

ZOOLOGICAL|Venom delivery.name: Venom delivery
ZOOLOGICAL|Venom delivery.definition: The use of neurotoxins or hemotoxins to subdue prey or deter predators.
ZOOLOGICAL|Venom delivery.condition: The use of neurotoxins or hemotoxins to subdue prey or deter predators.

ZOOLOGICAL|Vigilance.name: Vigilance
ZOOLOGICAL|Vigilance.definition: The constant scanning for predators. In groups, vigilance drops (many eyes).
ZOOLOGICAL|Vigilance.condition: The constant scanning for predators; in groups, vigilance drops (many eyes).
